# ECalc Phase 2 (Agent Tool and Calculator Library) Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Give the AuraGo agent the native tool `ecalc` (`search`, `describe`, `calculate`, `open` with the values
pre-filled in the Virtual Desktop) and grow the ECalc catalog from 11 to 77 calculators in all ten calculator categories,
with the engine and UI extensions those calculators need.

**Architecture:** Unchanged from phase 1: a declarative YAML catalog embedded in `internal/ecalc`, validated at load time,
served localized by `GET /api/ecalc/catalog`, and evaluated by the same small expression language in Go and in a DOM-free
JavaScript mirror, both checked against shared vector files. Part A extends the engine (15 new dimensions, unit aliases,
radix units for the `integer` dimension, `floor`/`ceil`, the schema fields `units`/`ignore`/`finder`/`chart` and the
standard-value combiner). Part U extends the calculator page (narrowed unit dropdowns, dimmed unused fields, number
systems, the combiner block, the chart, the schematics split into one file per category, the launch hook). Part B adds the
read-only query API `internal/ecalc/query.go`, the native tool `ecalc` and the `open_app` pre-fill bridge of the desktop
core. Parts C1–C5 add the 65 calculators. Part Z merges the shared DOX entries, updates manual chapter 32 and runs the
integrated verification.

**Tech Stack:** Go 1.27 (`gopkg.in/yaml.v3`), vanilla JavaScript classic scripts in the AuraGo desktop, go-rod browser tests
(`AURAGO_RUN_BROWSER_SMOKE=1`), Node for the parity script `scripts/test-ecalc-core.mjs`.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-01-ecalc-design.md` (phase 2 = agent tool + calculator library). Phase 1:
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-01-ecalc-phase1-foundation.md`, landed on `main`.

### How this plan was made

Every part was implemented for real in its own scratch worktree at base `fa37bfdd4` (A, U and B in parallel, then C1–C5
on top of A + U), verified there, and its plan text was generated from the verified files: the code blocks are
byte-identical to those files, and the parts with edits to existing files replayed their edit blocks on the base commit
and reproduced the worktree. Afterwards all parts were applied together in an integration worktree, where the whole
plan was verified once more (results in Task Z3). The integration run found three problems that the separate drafts
could not see; all three are fixed in the parts below (a search test that pinned the size of the catalog, a chip overlap
in the `i2c_pullup` drawing at the real page scale, and a stray measuring test that must not be committed).

`main` has moved on since `fa37bfdd4`. Execute on a fresh branch from the current `main` (worktree under `.worktrees/`).
Other sessions commit to this repository concurrently: if a task's "Replace … with …" block no longer matches because a
foreign commit touched the same lines (likely only in the shared registries of Part B and the root-level DOX files), apply
the same change to the new text by hand and record it in the task's commit message.

### Controller notes (decisions taken while assembling; they take precedence over the contract in the appendix)

1. **Binary numbers are grouped by eight digits** (`0b1_00101100`), not by four as the contract first said: grouped by
   four, 2^53 − 1 is 68 characters and would not read back through the 64-character input cap. Part A implements it (its
   deviation 7), Part U's browser test expects it.
2. **Drawings are at most 32 grid units wide** (Part U measured it: at 33 the field chips no longer fit the default
   1100 px window and fall back to a list). All drawings of the content parts are within 32.
3. **Part A's tests are robust to content** (A2/A5): `TestPhaseOneCalculators` pins only the basics category and its 12
   ids, `TestLocalizedJSONLanguagesAndFallback` takes the item count from the catalog, and the new
   `TestCalculatorVectorFilesNameACalculator` fails for a vector file that names no calculator, so the "write the vectors
   first" step of every content task really goes red. The content parts were drafted before these fixes: their run
   commands below no longer carry the `-skip` for the two count tests (removed at assembly), while their deviation lists
   and verification tables still describe the drafting runs that needed it. With Part A as in this plan the whole package
   is green without `-skip` (Task Z3).
4. **The tool parameter for the values is `inputs`**, not `values` (Part B deviation 1: `values` is already the Sheets
   matrix of `ToolCall`). `menus-and-routing.js` needs no change: `ctx.launch` already reaches `ECalcApp.render` for a new
   window (Part B deviation 5).
5. **Aluminium constants** (C1 `wire_resistance`, C4 `cable_voltage_drop`): ρ20 = 0.028264 Ω·mm²/m and α = 0.00403 /K per
   IEC 60889 (hard-drawn aluminium wire), checked by the controller against the HD 532 S1 text of IEC 60889:1987 and
   GB/T 17048-2017. The drafts flagged other constants as uncertain (silver and gold resistivity, IPC-2221 and IPC-2141
   validity ranges, op-amp and LED rules of thumb, textbook chapter numbers); they are worded as such in the item docs and
   listed in each part's deviations. Review them before release.
6. **Scope decisions of this phase** (contract §3 and §7.1): the tool `ecalc` has no Config switch of its own (it only
   computes, like `text_diff`); `open` is gated like `retro_games` play (Virtual Desktop enabled, agent control allowed,
   `policy_denied` otherwise) and denied to A2A peers. The finders that read tables — the cable cross-section finder per
   VDE and the trace spacing by voltage — moved to phase 3 together with the tables.
7. **Known failures that are not this plan's:** `TestUpdateConfigFallbackOnlyTrustedTransactionBackups` (`internal/audit`,
   fails on this Windows box at the base commit too) and the two `./ui` tests that already fail at the base commit (see
   Task Z3). Do not "fix" them in this plan.

## Part A: Engine extensions (`internal/ecalc` and the JavaScript mirror)

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal of this part:** give the ECalc engine everything the phase 2 calculator library and the agent tool need, in Go and in the JavaScript mirror, kept identical by shared vectors: the `floor` and `ceil` functions; 15 new dimensions (capacitance, inductance, frequency, time, length, area, temperature, tempdiff, thermal_resistance, resistivity, tempco, ratio, angle, baudrate, integer) with unit aliases, offset and non-linear units (AWG, degC, degF, dBµV) and radix units; the integer range rule of the solver; the schema fields `units`, `ignore`, `finder: combine` and `chart`; and the standard-value combiner `Combine` with the calculator `eseries_combiner`.

**How this part was made and verified:** every code block below was generated from the files of a scratch worktree at base commit `fa37bfdd4` (phase 1 landed); no code was typed into the plan by hand. A mechanical replay of the plan's edits on a clean copy of the base commit (test edits, expected FAIL run, implementation edits, snapshot regeneration, full run, byte-for-byte comparison with the worktree file of that task) reproduced the worktree exactly: every expected-FAIL run failed, every PASS run passed and every regenerated snapshot was identical. Final state: `go test ./internal/ecalc -count=1` green (36 tests plus the 12 calculator subtests), `go vet` and `gofmt -l` clean, `npm run test:ecalc` **1156 cases ok** (777 before this part).

Contract deviations (CONTRACT section 1; where this list and the contract disagree, this list wins):

1. `formula` may be empty when a calculator has `finder: combine`: the combiner has a single variable and no rule, so a formula line would have nothing to name. Every other calculator still needs a formula. The catalog JSON then has `"formula": []`, and the page must not draw an empty formula card for such an item.
2. `Combine` details the contract leaves open: deviations that agree to 1e-9 percent count as equal when a group is ordered (so `0.27 + 0.2 = 0.47000000000000003` is not ranked behind the exact `0.36 + 0.11`; R1 then R2 ascending decide); a `limit` below 1 returns only the single entry; a `limit` above `ComboMaxLimit` (1000) counts as 1000, which bounds the cost of one call. The JavaScript `combine` returns `null` where Go returns an error (like `nearest`).
3. Formatting an `integer`-dimension value with no number system selected writes decimal digits (never rounded to the significant-digit setting) when the value is a whole number in range, and the ordinary number text otherwise. A radix unit returns `""` for a value it cannot show. The contract only says that radix formats ignore the significant digits.
4. `Load` of `units.yaml` is stricter than section 1: every spelling of a dimension (base symbol, dimension aliases, unit symbols, unit aliases) must be non-empty and unique within the dimension; an `integer` dimension has no prefixes and is not `positive`; a radix unit has radix 2, 8, 10 or 16 and no factor, `to`, `from` or aliases; a non-radix unit is not allowed in an integer dimension.
5. Catalog JSON fields the contract does not spell out: every explicit unit has `aliases` (array) and `radix` (number, 0 for a non-radix unit); every dimension has `integer` (boolean). They are always written.
6. `floor` and `ceil` become reserved names like every function: no variable, derived quantity or choice constant may be called that. None of the 12 current items is.
7. Contract section 1.2 is amended by the coordinator (found by Part U): binary output groups by eight digits (bytes) instead of four, e.g. `0b11111111` for 255 and `0b1_00000000` for 256. With groups of four, 2^53-1 would be 68 characters, over the 64 that `Parse` accepts, so the value would not read back from its own text; with groups of eight it is 61 characters (hex stays at groups of four, 19 characters). Input is unchanged: `_` and blanks between digits in any grouping, at most 64 characters. The `units_roundtrip` vectors pin that every largest-value text reads back.
8. The phase 1 dimensions `energy` and `charge` gain prefixes (found by content part C1; Task A2): `energy` is now `n µ m "" k M` (a capacitor energy of 1.25 µJ no longer reads 0.00125 mJ) and `charge` is `n µ m ""` (gate charges in nC). The other dimensions were checked against their typical values and need nothing: power `n µ m "" k M` (µW, mW, kW), time `p n µ m ""` (ps to s, plus min and h), current `p n µ m "" k`, voltage `n µ m "" k M`, capacitance `p n µ m ""`, inductance `n µ m ""`, frequency `"" k M G`, resistance `m "" k M G`, length `µ m "" k`.
9. The tests that counted the catalog no longer break when a content part adds a category file (found by content part C1; Task A5): `TestPhaseOneCalculators` pins the 12 basics ids in order by filtering on the category, `TestLocalizedJSONLanguagesAndFallback` takes the item count from the catalog (at least 12), and `TestSolvableSetsOfBasics` already looked its items up by id. Verified in a scratch copy of the worktree (never in `wa`) with a dummy `catalog/calculators/passive.yaml` and its vector file: after regenerating the snapshot everything is green, including these three tests and the Node test. `ui/desktop_ecalc_browser_test.go` (Part U's file) still expects 11 basics items.
10. New check `TestCalculatorVectorFilesNameACalculator` (and the same check in the Node script; found by content part C5; Task A5): every file in `testdata/vectors/calculators/` is called `<calc>.json` and names a calculator of the catalog. Before, `TestCalculatorVectors` only read the files of calculators that exist, so a vector file written before its YAML (or with a misspelled `calc`) was ignored and "vectors first, watch them fail" could not go red. Verified in the same scratch copy: a vector file without its calculator, a file whose `calc` names no calculator and a file whose name differs from its `calc` each fail the Go and the Node test.

GitNexus: the index predates `internal/ecalc` (phase 1 landed after the last `analyze`). Run from the main checkout, `node .gitnexus/run.cjs impact "<symbol>" --direction upstream --repo .` answered `Target '<symbol>' not found` with `risk: UNKNOWN` for `evalCall`, `isFunc`, `loadUnits`, `parseValue` and `valueError` (the other modified symbols are in the same package). UNKNOWN is not read as safe: a text search over the repository shows that every caller of the modified functions is inside `internal/ecalc` (`Eval` calls `evalCall`; `claim` in `(*loader).calculator` and `Deps` call `isFunc`; `Load` calls `loadUnits` and `(*loader).calculator`; `parseNormalized`, which `Parse` and `ParseList` call, calls `parseValue`; `Solve` and `listError` call `valueError`; `LocalizedJSON` calls `render`; `Format` has no caller outside tests yet). Outside the package only `internal/server/ecalc_handlers.go` (`Default`, `LocalizedJSON`) and two `ui` tests (`Default`, `LocalizedJSON`) use it, and they only see additional JSON fields. Risk: LOW (additive; no exported signature changes). Before every commit run the change check required by `CLAUDE.md` (`node .gitnexus/run.cjs detect-changes --scope all --repo .`) and expect only the files listed in the task.

### How to run Part A

All paths are relative to the worktree root; every Go command runs from there. Before the first Go command in a PowerShell session:

```powershell
$env:GOTMPDIR = 'C:\tmp\go-build-ecalc'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $env:GOTMPDIR | Out-Null
```

Every code block below is the exact text of an edit: "replace X with Y" means the lines of X occur exactly once in the file (at that point of the task, after the earlier edits of the same file) and are replaced line for line by Y. Edits of one file are listed top to bottom. The JavaScript files and `scripts/test-ecalc-core.mjs` have CRLF line endings in a Windows checkout (autocrlf; git stores LF): use an editor or edit tool that matches line by line, and do not mix line endings in one file. Use the micro sign U+00B5 and the Greek capital omega U+03A9 in YAML and JSON (never U+03BC or U+2126; the one Greek-mu vector below tests the folding on purpose). After each task `gofmt -l internal/ecalc` printed nothing, `go vet ./internal/ecalc` was clean and the package tests and the JavaScript parity test passed, so every task leaves the tree green.

Part A touches no file that is bundled into `ui/js/desktop/bundles/main.bundle.js` and runs no browser test, so no `npm run build:ui` is needed.

### What Parts U, B and C can rely on

Go (package `aurago/internal/ecalc`):

```go
func Combine(series string, target float64, limit int) ([]Combo, error)
type Combo struct { Kind string; R1, R2, Value, DevPct float64 } // JSON kind, r1, r2, value, dev_pct
const ComboSingle, ComboSeries, ComboParallel = "single", "series", "parallel"
const ComboMaxLimit = 1000
type Chart struct { X, Y string; To Expr; Samples int }          // Calculator.Chart (nil without a chart)
const ChartMinSamples, ChartMaxSamples, ChartDefaultSamples = 11, 401, 101
// new fields: Calculator.Finder string ("" or "combine"), Var.Units / Derived.Units []string,
// ChoiceOption.Ignore []string, Unit.Aliases []string, Unit.Radix int, Dim.Integer bool
```

JavaScript (`window.ECalcCore`):

- `eseries.combine(series, target, limit)` returns `[{kind, r1, r2, value, devPct}, ...]` (single first, then series, then parallel) or `null` for an unknown series or a target that is not finite and greater than zero. Cost in Node on this box: E24 about 4 ms, E96 about 30 ms, E192 about 110 to 200 ms (Go: 0.4, 3 and 6 ms), so compute it only while the combiner block is visible.
- `units.create(catalog.units)` handles the new dimensions without changes in the caller: `parse('25degC', 'temperature', '')`, `parse('0xFF', 'integer', 'hex')`, `format(255, 'integer', 'hex')` is `"0xFF"` (hex groups by four: `0xDEAD_BEEF`; binary groups by eight: `format(256, 'integer', 'bin')` is `"0b1_00000000"`; every text is at most 61 characters, so it reads back within the 64-character input limit),`format(0.002588186728012864, 'length', 'AWG')` is `"10 AWG"` and so on. `units.dim(id)` has `integer` (boolean); every unit of `units.dim(id).units` has `radix` and `aliases`; `units.options('integer')` is `['', 'dec', 'hex', 'bin', 'oct']` (ids). A radix unit's `format` returns `""` for a value it cannot show; `core.solve.exactText` falls back to the plain number text.
- `solve.solve` reports `range` for an integer variable that is not a whole number in 0 .. 2^53-1.
- `expr` knows `floor` and `ceil` (`ARITY`).

Catalog JSON (`GET /api/ecalc/catalog`): `units.dims[]` is `{id, symbol, aliases, prefixes, positive, integer, units}`, an explicit unit `{id, symbol, aliases, factor, to, from, radix}`; a var is `{..., unit, units, ...}` and a derived quantity `{..., unit, units}` with `units` an array (empty = every unit; `""` inside means the base symbol with automatic prefixes); a choice option is `{id, name, consts, ignore}`; an item has `finder` (`""` or `"combine"`) and `chart` (`null` or `{x, y, to, samples}`). Aliases are input spellings only: they are never dropdown entries.

New dimensions in `units.yaml`, after the eight of phase 1 and in this order (base symbol; prefixes; explicit units, aliases in brackets):

| id | symbol | prefixes | positive | explicit units |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| capacitance | F | p n µ m "" | yes | none |
| inductance | H | n µ m "" | yes | none |
| frequency | Hz | "" k M G | yes | none |
| time | s | p n µ m "" | yes | min, h |
| length | m | µ m "" k | yes | mil, in, ft, oz (copper weight, 35 µm), AWG |
| area | m² | "" | yes | mm2 (mm², [mm2]), mil2 (mil²), kcmil, AWG |
| temperature | K | "" | yes | degC (°C, [C, degC]), degF (°F, [F, degF]) |
| tempdiff | K | "" | no | degC (°C), degF (°F) |
| thermal_resistance | K/W | "" | yes | degCW (°C/W) |
| resistivity | Ω·m | n µ m "" | yes | ohmmm2m (Ω·mm²/m) |
| tempco | 1/K | "" | no | ppmK (ppm/K), pctK (%/K) |
| ratio | (empty) | "" | no | pct (%) |
| angle | rad | m "" | no | deg (°, [deg]) |
| baudrate | Bd | "" k M | yes | none |
| integer | (empty) | none | no | dec, hex, bin, oct (radix units) |

and the voltage dimension gains `dBuV` (symbol dBµV, alias dBuV). The phase 1 dimensions `energy` (n µ m "" k M) and `charge` (n µ m "") gained the n and µ prefixes. Notes for the content parts: a value in AWG is a diameter on `length` and a cross-section on `area` (ASTM B258: `0.000127 * 92^((36-n)/39)` m, AWG 0 = 8.251 mm, AWG 10 = 2.588 mm and 5.261 mm², AWG 36 = 0.127 mm); use `tempdiff` for a temperature rise and `temperature` for an absolute value (its default display unit is chosen with `unit: degC`); a `units` whitelist entry must be an explicit unit id or `""`.

Shared vector sections added to `core.json`: `units_roundtrip`, `solve_range`, `combine`, `combine_count`, `combine_error`, and more entries in `expr`, `parse`, `parse_error`, `deps`, `units_parse`, `units_parse_error` and `units_format`. A calculator vector file with `finder: combine` must carry `combos` (same shape as `combine`, checked against `Combine` in Go and against `ECalcCore.eseries.combine` in Node); no other calculator may have them.


### Task A1: `floor` and `ceil` in both evaluators

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/ecalc/testdata/vectors/core.json` (shared vectors)
- Modify: `internal/ecalc/expr.go`
- Modify: `ui/js/desktop/apps/ecalc/ecalc-expr.js`

GitNexus: modified are `funcArity` (the function whitelist, read by the parser, `isFunc` and `Deps`) and `evalCall` (caller: `Eval`). `isFunc` also makes `floor` and `ceil` reserved names in `claim` of `(*loader).calculator`; no catalog item uses either name (`grep -rn -E '\b(floor|ceil)\b' internal/ecalc/catalog` finds nothing). Index answer: UNKNOWN (see above); callers confirmed by text search, all inside the package.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

The vectors pin both rounding directions for positive and negative numbers and the .5 cases (`floor(-2.5)` is -3, `ceil(-2.5)` is -2), whole numbers, the infinities and NaN, a composite use (`floor(vin/vref*2^bits)` with a 10-bit converter at half the reference gives code 512), the parse tree, the arity errors and `Deps`. `ceil(-0.5)` is negative zero in both languages; a zero `want` accepts it.

// The dimensions of units.yaml in their order, with the base symbol, the prefixes, the positive flag and the ids of the
// explicit units. The unit dropdowns of the app follow this order, and the vectors rely on these definitions.
func TestUnitsCatalogDimensions(t *testing.T) {
	u := testUnits(t)
	want := []string{
		"voltage|V|n µ m '' k M|false|dBV dBu dBuV",
		"current|A|p n µ m '' k|false|",
		"resistance|Ω|m '' k M G|true|",
		"power|W|n µ m '' k M|false|dBm",
		"charge|C|n µ m ''|false|mAh Ah",
		"energy|J|n µ m '' k M|false|mWh Wh kWh",
		"number||(none)|true|",
		"gain|dB|(none)|false|",
		"capacitance|F|p n µ m ''|true|",
		"inductance|H|n µ m ''|true|",
		"frequency|Hz|'' k M G|true|",
		"time|s|p n µ m ''|true|min h",
		"length|m|µ m '' k|true|mil in ft oz AWG",
		"area|m²|''|true|mm2 mil2 kcmil AWG",
		"temperature|K|''|true|degC degF",
		"tempdiff|K|''|false|degC degF",
		"thermal_resistance|K/W|''|true|degCW",
		"resistivity|Ω·m|n µ m ''|true|ohmmm2m",
		"tempco|1/K|''|false|ppmK pctK",
		"ratio||''|false|pct",
		"angle|rad|m ''|false|deg",
		"baudrate|Bd|'' k M|true|",
	}
	var got []string
	for _, d := range u.Dims {
		prefixes := make([]string, len(d.Prefixes))
		for i, p := range d.Prefixes {
			prefixes[i] = p
			if p == "" {
				prefixes[i] = "''"
			}
		}
		if len(prefixes) == 0 {
			prefixes = []string{"(none)"}
		}
		ids := make([]string, len(d.Units))
		for i, un := range d.Units {
			ids[i] = un.ID
		}
		got = append(got, fmt.Sprintf("%s|%s|%s|%t|%s", d.ID, d.Symbol, strings.Join(prefixes, " "), d.Positive, strings.Join(ids, " ")))
	}
	if strings.Join(got, "\n") != strings.Join(want, "\n") {
		t.Errorf("dimensions of units.yaml\n got:\n%s\nwant:\n%s", strings.Join(got, "\n"), strings.Join(want, "\n"))
	}
}

// The units whose conversion is a formula or a published constant: AWG (ASTM B258; the published table is rounded to
// four digits, hence the loose tolerance on those rows), the degree in radians and the Fahrenheit degree of a
// temperature difference.
func TestUnitsReferenceConstants(t *testing.T) {
	u := testUnits(t)
	awgLen, awgArea := u.Dim("length").Unit("AWG"), u.Dim("area").Unit("AWG")
	for _, c := range []struct {
		name      string
		got, want float64
		tol       float64
	}{
		{"AWG 0 diameter, 8.251 mm", awgLen.ToBase(0), 8.251e-3, 5e-4},
		{"AWG 10 diameter, 2.588 mm", awgLen.ToBase(10), 2.588e-3, 5e-4},
		{"AWG 36 diameter, 0.127 mm", awgLen.ToBase(36), 0.127e-3, 1e-12},
		{"AWG 10 area, 5.261 mm2", awgArea.ToBase(10), 5.261e-6, 5e-4},
		{"AWG number of 0.127 mm", awgLen.FromBase(0.127e-3), 36, 1e-12},
		{"AWG number of 5.261154954510375 mm2", awgArea.FromBase(5.261154954510375e-6), 10, 1e-12},
		{"9 degF of temperature difference in K", u.Dim("tempdiff").Unit("degF").ToBase(9), 5, 1e-12},
		{"180 degrees in radians", u.Dim("angle").Unit("deg").ToBase(180), math.Pi, 1e-12},
	} {
		if !near(c.got, c.want, c.tol) {
			t.Errorf("%s = %v, want %v", c.name, c.got, c.want)
		}
	}
}

// The radix units belong to the integer dimension only: the catalog marks them (Radix) and the dimension (Integer),
// and the non-radix units of other dimensions carry neither.
func TestUnitsRadixMarkers(t *testing.T) {
	u := testUnits(t)
	for _, d := range u.Dims {
		for _, un := range d.Units {
			if (un.Radix != 0) != d.Integer {
				t.Errorf("dim %s unit %s: radix %d on a dimension with integer=%v", d.ID, un.ID, un.Radix, d.Integer)
			}
		}
	}
	want := map[string]int{"dec": 10, "hex": 16, "bin": 2, "oct": 8}
	for id, radix := range want {
		if un := u.Dim("integer").Unit(id); un == nil || un.Radix != radix {
			t.Errorf("integer unit %s = %+v, want radix %d", id, un, radix)
		}
	}
}

// TestSolveRangeVectors runs the solve_range section of core.json: a single input variable of a given dimension, no
// rules. The ECMAScript twin (scripts/test-ecalc-core.mjs) runs the same cases through its own solver.
func TestSolveRangeVectors(t *testing.T) {
	var f struct {
		Cases []struct {
			Dim  string `json:"dim"`
			V    any    `json:"v"`
			Want string `json:"want"`
		} `json:"solve_range"`
	}
	readJSON(t, "testdata/vectors/core.json", &f)
	if len(f.Cases) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("core.json lacks the solve_range section")
	}
	u := testUnits(t)
	for _, v := range f.Cases {
		if u.Dim(v.Dim) == nil {
			t.Fatalf("solve_range: unknown dimension %q", v.Dim)
		}
		c := &Calculator{Vars: []Var{{ID: "n", Dim: v.Dim, dim: u.Dim(v.Dim), Input: true}}}
		res := c.Solve(Inputs{Values: map[string]float64{"n": vecNum(t, v.V)}})
		if got := res.Errors["n"]; got != v.Want {
			t.Errorf("Solve(%s = %v) error = %q, want %q", v.Dim, v.V, got, v.Want)
		}
	}
}

// radixLetter is the letter of the optional prefix of a radix number: 0x, 0b and 0o (decimal has no prefix).
func radixLetter(radix int) byte {
	switch radix {
	case 16:
		return 'x'
	case 2:
		return 'b'
	case 8:
		return 'o'
	}
	return 0
}

// parseRadix reads a whole number in the base of un from text without blanks: an optional 0x, 0b or 0o prefix of that
// base (either case), then at least one digit of the base (hex digits in either case) with underscores allowed between
// digits. There is no sign and no SI prefix, and the value must not exceed maxSafeInt.
func parseRadix(un *Unit, s string) (float64, error) {
	bad := fmt.Errorf("cannot read %q as a %s number", s, un.ID)
	digits := s
	if l := radixLetter(un.Radix); l != 0 && len(digits) >= 2 && digits[0] == '0' && digits[1]|0x20 == l {
		digits = digits[2:]
	}
	if digits == "" || digits[0] == '_' || digits[len(digits)-1] == '_' {
		return 0, bad
	}
	var v uint64
	for i := 0; i < len(digits); i++ {
		c := digits[i]
		if c == '_' {
			continue
		}
		var digit int
		switch {
		case c >= '0' && c <= '9':
			digit = int(c - '0')
		case c >= 'a' && c <= 'f':
			digit = int(c-'a') + 10
		case c >= 'A' && c <= 'F':
			digit = int(c-'A') + 10
		default:
			return 0, bad
		}
		if digit >= un.Radix {
			return 0, bad
		}
		if v = v*uint64(un.Radix) + uint64(digit); v > maxSafeInt {
			return 0, fmt.Errorf("the value %q is out of range (at most %d)", s, uint64(maxSafeInt))
		}
	}
	return float64(v), nil
}

// groupDigits writes the ASCII text s in groups of n characters counted from the right, joined by underscores.
func groupDigits(s string, n int) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
		if i > 0 && (len(s)-i)%n == 0 {
			b.WriteByte('_')
		}
		b.WriteByte(s[i])
	}
	return b.String()
}

// formatRadix writes a whole number in 0 .. maxSafeInt in the given base: decimal as plain digits, hex as 0x and
// upper-case digits grouped by four (0xDEAD_BEEF), binary as 0b grouped by eight, that is by byte (0b1_00000000), octal
// as 0o. Anything else gives "". The largest value, 2^53-1, is 61 characters in binary, so every text this function
// writes is within the 64 characters that Parse accepts. The significant-digit setting does not apply.
func formatRadix(radix int, v float64) string {
	if v != math.Trunc(v) || v < 0 || v > maxSafeInt {
		return ""
	}
	n := uint64(v)
	switch radix {
	case 16:
		return "0x" + groupDigits(strings.ToUpper(strconv.FormatUint(n, 16)), 4)
	case 2:
		return "0b" + groupDigits(strconv.FormatUint(n, 2), 8)
	case 8:
		return "0o" + strconv.FormatUint(n, 8)
	}
	return strconv.FormatUint(n, 10)
}

    // 0o prefix, digits with underscores between them, no sign, at most 2^53 - 1.
    function parseRadix(unit, text) {
        let digits = text;
        const letter = RADIX_LETTER[unit.radix];
        if (letter && digits.length >= 2 && digits[0] === '0' && digits[1].toLowerCase() === letter) digits = digits.slice(2);
        if (!RADIX_DIGITS[unit.radix].test(digits)) throw fail('cannot read ' + JSON.stringify(text) + ' as a ' + unit.id + ' number');
        let value = 0;
        for (const char of digits) {
            if (char === '_') continue;
            value = value * unit.radix + parseInt(char, 16);
            if (value > MAX_SAFE) throw fail('the value ' + JSON.stringify(text) + ' is out of range (at most ' + MAX_SAFE + ')');
        }
        return value;
    }

    // Groups of `size` characters from the right, joined by underscores (1F_FFFF).
    function groupDigits(digits, size) {
        let out = '';
        for (let i = 0; i < digits.length; i += 1) {
            if (i > 0 && (digits.length - i) % size === 0) out += '_';
            out += digits[i];
        }
        return out;
    }

    // A whole number in 0 .. 2^53 - 1 written in the given base: decimal plain, hex 0xDEAD_BEEF (groups of four), binary
    // 0b1_00000000 (groups of eight, so 2^53 - 1 is 61 characters, within the 64 that parse() accepts), octal 0o377;
    // anything else gives ''. The significant-digit setting does not apply.
    function formatRadix(radix, value) {
        if (!Number.isInteger(value) || value < 0 || value > MAX_SAFE) return '';
        if (radix === 16) return '0x' + groupDigits(value.toString(16).toUpperCase(), 4);
        if (radix === 2) return '0b' + groupDigits(value.toString(2), 8);
        if (radix === 8) return '0o' + value.toString(8);
        return value.toString(10);
    }

// mutate applies old/new pairs to a fixture (each old text once) and fails the test when a pair does not apply.
func mutate(t *testing.T, base string, pairs ...string) string {
	t.Helper()
	for i := 0; i+1 < len(pairs); i += 2 {
		if !strings.Contains(base, pairs[i]) {
			t.Fatalf("fixture does not contain %q", pairs[i])
		}
		base = strings.Replace(base, pairs[i], pairs[i+1], 1)
	}
	return base
}

// choiceYAML is a choice q whose option o ignores the variables of ignoreO (a YAML flow list) and whose option p ignores
// none; both define the constant k. It ends with the dof line of baseCalc, so it replaces "  dof: 2".
func choiceYAML(ignoreO, rest string) string {
	return "  choices:\n    q: {name: " + flow16("Q") + ", default: o, options: {o: {name: " + flow16("O") + ", consts: {k: 1}" + ignoreO +
		"}, p: {name: " + flow16("P") + ", consts: {k: 2}}}}\n" + rest + "  dof: 2"
}

// combineCalc is the smallest standard-value combiner: one scalar resistance, dof 1, no rules, no formula.
var combineCalc = strings.ReplaceAll(`- id: t_combine
  kind: calculator
  category: basics
  name: NAME16
  doc: {en: "Doc.", de: "Doku."}
  tags: [test]
  source: "Textbook"
  vars:
    target: {dim: resistance, label: R, name: {en: "R", de: "R"}, default: "5k"}
  dof: 1
  finder: combine
`, "NAME16", flow16("T"))

// The schema extensions of phase 2: the display-unit whitelist of a variable or derived quantity (units), the variables
// an option does not use (ignore), the chart and the finder.
func TestLoadAcceptsDisplayUnitsIgnoreChartAndFinder(t *testing.T) {
	src := mutate(t, baseCalc,
		`default: "10 V"}`, `default: "10 V", unit: dBV, units: ["", dBV, dBu]}`,
		`expr: "a*c"}`, `expr: "a*c", unit: dBm, units: [dBm, ""]}`,
		"  dof: 2", choiceYAML(", ignore: [b]", `  chart: {x: a, y: c, to: "10", samples: 21}`+"\n"))
	cat, err := Load(fixtureFS(t, map[string]string{"t.yaml": src}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Load: %v", err)
	}
	c := cat.Calculator("t_div")
	if got := c.Var("a").Units; !reflect.DeepEqual(got, []string{"", "dBV", "dBu"}) {
		t.Errorf("var a units = %q", got)
	}
	if got := c.Derived[0].Units; !reflect.DeepEqual(got, []string{"dBm", ""}) {
		t.Errorf("derived p units = %q", got)
	}
	if o := c.Choices[0].Options; !reflect.DeepEqual(o[0].Ignore, []string{"b"}) || len(o[1].Ignore) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("ignore lists = %q / %q, want [b] and none", o[0].Ignore, o[1].Ignore)
	}
	if ch := c.Chart; ch == nil || ch.X != "a" || ch.Y != "c" || ch.To.Src != "10" || ch.Samples != 21 {
		t.Errorf("chart = %+v, want x a, y c, to 10, 21 samples", ch)
	}

	// The catalog JSON carries all of it; a missing list is [] and no chart is null (never a missing key).
	body, _, err := cat.LocalizedJSON("en")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var doc struct {
		Items []struct {
			Finder string `json:"finder"`
			Chart  *struct {
				X       string `json:"x"`
				Y       string `json:"y"`
				To      string `json:"to"`
				Samples int    `json:"samples"`
			} `json:"chart"`
			Vars    []struct{ Units []string } `json:"vars"`
			Derived []struct{ Units []string } `json:"derived"`
			Choices []struct {
				Options []struct{ Ignore []string } `json:"options"`
			} `json:"choices"`
		} `json:"items"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &doc); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	it := doc.Items[0]
	if it.Chart == nil || it.Chart.X != "a" || it.Chart.Y != "c" || it.Chart.To != "10" || it.Chart.Samples != 21 || it.Finder != "" {
		t.Errorf("item JSON chart/finder = %+v / %q", it.Chart, it.Finder)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(it.Vars[0].Units, []string{"", "dBV", "dBu"}) || it.Vars[1].Units == nil || len(it.Vars[1].Units) != 0 ||
		!reflect.DeepEqual(it.Derived[0].Units, []string{"dBm", ""}) {
		t.Errorf("JSON units = %q / %q / %q", it.Vars[0].Units, it.Vars[1].Units, it.Derived[0].Units)
	}
	if o := it.Choices[0].Options; !reflect.DeepEqual(o[0].Ignore, []string{"b"}) || o[1].Ignore == nil || len(o[1].Ignore) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("JSON ignore = %q / %q", o[0].Ignore, o[1].Ignore)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(string(body), `"chart":{"x":"a","y":"c","to":"10","samples":21}`) {
		t.Errorf("the chart is not written as {x, y, to, samples}: %s", body)
	}

	// Samples default to 101.
	dflt := mutate(t, src, `, samples: 21`, ``)
	if c := loadOne(t, dflt); c.Chart == nil || c.Chart.Samples != 101 {
		t.Errorf("default samples = %+v, want 101", c.Chart)
	}

	// The combiner finder: no formula, no rules.
	combiner, err := Load(fixtureFS(t, map[string]string{"t.yaml": combineCalc}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Load combiner: %v", err)
	}
	cc := combiner.Calculator("t_combine")
	if cc.Finder != "combine" || len(cc.Formula) != 0 || len(cc.Rules) != 0 || cc.Chart != nil {
		t.Errorf("combine calculator = finder %q formula %q rules %d chart %v", cc.Finder, cc.Formula, len(cc.Rules), cc.Chart)
	}
	cb, _, _ := combiner.LocalizedJSON("en")
	if !strings.Contains(string(cb), `"finder":"combine"`) || !strings.Contains(string(cb), `"chart":null`) || !strings.Contains(string(cb), `"formula":[]`) {
		t.Errorf("combine JSON lacks finder, chart null or an empty formula: %s", cb)
	}
}

func TestLoadRejectsBrokenDisplayUnitsIgnoreChartAndFinder(t *testing.T) {
	withChart := func(chart string) string {
		return mutate(t, baseCalc, "  dof: 2", "  chart: "+chart+"\n  dof: 2")
	}
	extraDerived := mutate(t, baseCalc, "    p: {dim: power,", "    q: {dim: resistance, label: Q, name: {en: \"Q\", de: \"Q\"}, expr: \"b*2\"}\n    p: {dim: power,")
	cases := []struct{ name, src, want string }{
		{"units entry that is no explicit unit", mutate(t, baseCalc, `default: "10 V"}`, `default: "10 V", units: [dBm]}`), `units entry "dBm" is not an explicit unit of voltage`},

// checkDisplayUnits validates the optional units whitelist of a variable or derived quantity: every entry is "" (the
// base symbol with automatic prefixes) or an explicit unit of the dimension, none twice, and the default display unit
// (when set) is one of them. An empty list offers every unit.
func checkDisplayUnits(fail func(string, ...any), what string, dim *Dim, units []string, unit string) {
	if len(units) == 0 {
		return
	}
	listed := map[string]bool{}
	for _, id := range units {
		switch {
		case listed[id]:
			fail("%s: units entry %q is listed twice", what, id)
		case id != "" && dim.Unit(id) == nil:
			fail("%s: units entry %q is not an explicit unit of %s", what, id, dim.ID)
		}
		listed[id] = true
	}
	if unit != "" && !listed[unit] {
		fail("%s: unit %q is not in its units list", what, unit)
	}
}

// buildChart validates the chart of a calculator: x is a scalar variable, y a rule target or derived quantity that uses
// x, to an expression over known names that does not use x, samples within the chart limits (0 = the default).
func buildChart(fail func(string, ...any), c *Calculator, rc *rawChart, known func(string, Expr)) *Chart {
	ch := &Chart{X: rc.X, Y: rc.Y, Samples: rc.Samples}
	if ch.Samples == 0 {
		ch.Samples = ChartDefaultSamples
	}
	if ch.Samples < ChartMinSamples || ch.Samples > ChartMaxSamples {
		fail("chart: samples must be between %d and %d, got %d", ChartMinSamples, ChartMaxSamples, ch.Samples)
	}
	x := c.Var(ch.X)
	switch {
	case x == nil:
		fail("chart: x %q is not a variable", ch.X)
	case x.List:
		fail("chart: x %q is a list variable", ch.X)
	}
	var alts []Expr
	for _, r := range c.Rules {
		if r.Target == ch.Y {
			alts = r.Alts
		}
	}
	for _, d := range c.Derived {
		if d.ID == ch.Y {
			alts = d.Alts
		}
	}
	usesX := false
	for _, alt := range alts {
		usesX = usesX || contains(alt.Deps, ch.X)
	}
	switch {
	case len(alts) == 0:
		fail("chart: y %q needs a rule or a derived expression", ch.Y)
	case x != nil && !usesX:
		fail("chart: y %q does not depend on x %q", ch.Y, ch.X)
	}
	to, err := newExpr(rc.To)
	if err != nil {
		fail("chart: to: %v", err)
		return ch
	}
	known("chart to", to)
	if contains(to.Deps, ch.X) {
		fail("chart: to %q must not depend on x %q", rc.To, ch.X)
	}
	ch.To = to
	return ch
}

Every case has a hand-written `ref`. The expected entries come from an independent reference: exact decimal candidates, its own enumeration and ordering code, deviations as plain doubles (Python), not from the Go or JavaScript code; several lines are also checkable by hand (`10k || 10k = 5k`, `820 + 180 = 1000`, `1k || 39k = 975`, `4.7k + 270 = 4970`).
- `TestCombineVectors`, `TestCombineInvariants` (for every series and five targets: the single entry is `Nearest`, the ranges and the R1/R2 order of the pairs, every value is a three-digit value of the series, the deviation formula, the group order, no pair twice, a larger limit only appends) and `BenchmarkCombine`.
- `calculators_test.go` reads `combos` from a calculator vector file: required when `finder` is `combine`, forbidden otherwise, each checked with the same function as `combine`. The Node script does the same through `core.eseries.combine`.
- `eseries_combiner.json`: sets, solve vectors for the single target (range, nonfinite and undetermined errors) and four `combos` (E12 5k, E24 5k, E96 5k, E12 4.7k).
- Basics tests: `TestPhaseOneCalculators` pins the 12 basics ids by category (the combiner is the 12th), `TestSolvableSetsOfBasics` lists the combiner's set, `TestESeriesCombinerItem` pins its shape, `TestLocalizedJSONLanguagesAndFallback` takes the item count from the catalog (deviation 9).
- `TestCalculatorVectorFilesNameACalculator` and the matching loop in the Node script (deviation 10).

// combineVector is a Combine case: the entries Combine(Series, Target, Limit) must return, in this order. The same
// shape is used by the combine section of core.json and by the combos of a calculator with finder: combine.
type combineVector struct {
	Series string  `json:"series"`
	Target float64 `json:"target"`
	Limit  int     `json:"limit"`
	Ref    string  `json:"ref"`
	Want   []Combo `json:"want"`
}

// checkCombine runs one combineVector: the same entries in the same order, r1, r2 and value at 1e-12 and the
// deviation at 1e-9 relative error.
func checkCombine(t *testing.T, v combineVector) {
	t.Helper()
	name := fmt.Sprintf("Combine(%s, %v, %d)", v.Series, v.Target, v.Limit)
	if v.Ref == "" {
		t.Errorf("%s: the vector has no ref", name)
	}
	got, err := Combine(v.Series, v.Target, v.Limit)
	if err != nil {
		t.Errorf("%s: %v", name, err)
		return
	}
	if len(got) != len(v.Want) {
		t.Errorf("%s returned %d entries, want %d: %+v", name, len(got), len(v.Want), got)
		return
	}
	for i, want := range v.Want {
		g := got[i]
		if g.Kind != want.Kind || !near(g.R1, want.R1, 1e-12) || !near(g.R2, want.R2, 1e-12) || !near(g.Value, want.Value, 1e-12) || !near(g.DevPct, want.DevPct, 1e-9) {
			t.Errorf("%s entry %d = %+v, want %+v", name, i, g, want)
		}
	}
}

func TestCombineVectors(t *testing.T) {
	var f struct {
		Combine []combineVector `json:"combine"`
		Count   []struct {
			Series string  `json:"series"`
			Target float64 `json:"target"`
			Limit  int     `json:"limit"`
			Want   int     `json:"want"`
		} `json:"combine_count"`
		Errors []struct {
			Series string `json:"series"`
			Target any    `json:"target"`
		} `json:"combine_error"`
	}
	readJSON(t, "testdata/vectors/core.json", &f)
	if len(f.Combine) < 6 || len(f.Count) == 0 || len(f.Errors) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("core.json has %d combine, %d combine_count and %d combine_error vectors, want at least 6, 1 and 1", len(f.Combine), len(f.Count), len(f.Errors))
	}
	for _, v := range f.Combine {
		checkCombine(t, v)
	}
	for _, v := range f.Count {
		if got, err := Combine(v.Series, v.Target, v.Limit); err != nil || len(got) != v.Want {
			t.Errorf("Combine(%s, %v, %d) returned %d entries (%v), want %d", v.Series, v.Target, v.Limit, len(got), err, v.Want)
		}
	}
	for _, v := range f.Errors {
		if got, err := Combine(v.Series, vecNum(t, v.Target), 5); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("Combine(%q, %v) = %+v, want an error", v.Series, v.Target, got)
		}
	}
}

// Properties that hold for every series and target, independent of the vectors: the single entry is the nearest value,
// series pairs have r1 >= r2 within [target/1000, target], parallel pairs r1 <= r2 within [target, 1000*target], every
// value is a three-digit value of the series, the entries of a group are ordered and no pair appears twice.
func TestCombineInvariants(t *testing.T) {
	for _, series := range ESeriesIDs {
		mantissas, _ := ESeriesValues(series)
		isStandard := func(r float64) bool {
			m := r / math.Pow10(int(math.Floor(math.Log10(r))))
			for _, x := range mantissas {
				if math.Abs(m-x) < 1e-9 {
					return true
				}
			}
			return false
		}
		for _, target := range []float64{1, 4.7, 5000, 123456, 0.0033} {
			got, err := Combine(series, target, 7)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("Combine(%s, %v): %v", series, target, err)
			}
			nearest, dev, _ := Nearest(series, target)
			if got[0] != (Combo{Kind: "single", R1: nearest, Value: nearest, DevPct: dev}) {
				t.Errorf("%s %v: first entry %+v, want the single nearest value %v", series, target, got[0], nearest)
			}
			seen := map[[3]float64]bool{}
			var lastKind string
			var lastDev, lastR1, lastR2 float64
			counts := map[string]int{}
			for _, c := range got[1:] {
				counts[c.Kind]++
				if !isStandard(c.R1) || roundSig(c.R1, 3) != c.R1 || !isStandard(c.R2) || roundSig(c.R2, 3) != c.R2 {
					t.Errorf("%s %v: %+v uses a value that is not a three-digit %s value", series, target, c, series)
				}
				key := [3]float64{c.R1, c.R2, float64(len(c.Kind))}
				if seen[key] {
					t.Errorf("%s %v: the pair %v, %v appears twice", series, target, c.R1, c.R2)
				}
				seen[key] = true
				switch c.Kind {
				case "series":
					if c.R1 < c.R2 || c.R1 > target || c.R2 < target/1000 || c.R1+c.R2 != c.Value {
						t.Errorf("%s %v: bad series entry %+v", series, target, c)
					}
				case "parallel":
					if c.R1 > c.R2 || c.R1 < target || c.R2 > 1000*target || c.R1*c.R2/(c.R1+c.R2) != c.Value {
						t.Errorf("%s %v: bad parallel entry %+v", series, target, c)
					}
				default:
					t.Errorf("%s %v: unexpected kind %q", series, target, c.Kind)
				}
				if !near(c.DevPct, (c.Value-target)/target*100, 1e-12) {
					t.Errorf("%s %v: %+v has the deviation %v", series, target, c, (c.Value-target)/target*100)
				}
				if c.Kind == lastKind {
					q, lastQ := math.Round(math.Abs(c.DevPct)*1e9), math.Round(math.Abs(lastDev)*1e9)
					if q < lastQ || (q == lastQ && (c.R1 < lastR1 || (c.R1 == lastR1 && c.R2 <= lastR2))) {
						t.Errorf("%s %v: %+v is out of order after |dev| %v r1 %v r2 %v", series, target, c, lastDev, lastR1, lastR2)
					}
				}
				lastKind, lastDev, lastR1, lastR2 = c.Kind, c.DevPct, c.R1, c.R2
			}
			if counts["series"] != 7 || counts["parallel"] != 7 {
				t.Errorf("%s %v: %d series and %d parallel entries, want 7 each", series, target, counts["series"], counts["parallel"])
			}
		}
	}
	// A larger limit only appends: the entries of a smaller limit are the first ones of each group.
	small, _ := Combine("E96", 5000, 5)
	big, _ := Combine("E96", 5000, 40)
	if len(small) != 11 || len(big) != 81 || !reflect.DeepEqual(small[:6], big[:6]) || !reflect.DeepEqual(small[6:], big[41:46]) {
		t.Errorf("limit 5 is not the head of limit 40: %d and %d entries", len(small), len(big))
	}
	// A limit below one leaves the single entry.
	if got, _ := Combine("E3", 100, 0); len(got) != 1 || got[0].Kind != "single" {
		t.Errorf("limit 0 gave %+v, want only the single entry", got)
	}
}

// BenchmarkCombine measures the finest series, the slowest case (about 170 000 pairs per group): go test -bench Combine.
func BenchmarkCombine(b *testing.B) {
	for _, series := range []string{"E24", "E96", "E192"} {
		b.Run(series, func(b *testing.B) {
			for i := 0; i < b.N; i++ {
				if _, err := Combine(series, 5000, 5); err != nil {
					b.Fatal(err)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestCalculatorVectorFilesNameACalculator makes the vector directory strict: every file in it is called <calc>.json and
// names a calculator of the catalog. TestCalculatorVectors only reads the files of calculators that exist, so without
// this check a vector file for a missing or misspelled calculator would be ignored and writing the vectors first could
// never go red. (The other direction, a calculator without a file, already fails TestCalculatorVectors.)
func TestCalculatorVectorFilesNameACalculator(t *testing.T) {
	cat, err := Default()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	files, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.FromSlash("testdata/vectors/calculators/*"))
	if err != nil || len(files) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("no calculator vector files found (%v)", err)
	}
	for _, file := range files {
		name := filepath.Base(file)
		if !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".json") {
			t.Errorf("%s: only <calc>.json files belong in testdata/vectors/calculators", name)
			continue
		}
		var v struct {
			Calc string `json:"calc"`
		}
		readJSON(t, "testdata/vectors/calculators/"+name, &v)
		switch {
		case v.Calc == "":
			t.Errorf("%s declares no calc", name)
		case name != v.Calc+".json":
			t.Errorf("%s declares calc %q, so the file must be called %s.json", name, v.Calc, v.Calc)
		case cat.Calculator(v.Calc) == nil:
			t.Errorf("%s names the calculator %q, which the catalog does not have", name, v.Calc)
		}
	}
}

// TestESeriesCombinerItem pins the shape of the standard-value combiner: one scalar resistance (the target, 5 kOhm),
// dof 1, the combine finder, no rules, no formula, no schematic and no chart; the page and the agent list the
// combinations of the selected E-series.
func TestESeriesCombinerItem(t *testing.T) {
	cat, err := Default()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	c := cat.Calculator("eseries_combiner")
	if c == nil {
		t.Fatal("the catalog has no eseries_combiner")
	}
	if c.Category != "basics" || c.Kind != "calculator" || c.Finder != "combine" || c.DOF != 1 || c.Schematic != "" || c.Chart != nil ||
		len(c.Rules) != 0 || len(c.Derived) != 0 || len(c.Formula) != 0 || len(c.Choices) != 0 || len(c.Vars) != 1 {
		t.Errorf("unexpected shape: %+v", c)
	}
	v := c.Vars[0]
	if v.ID != "target" || v.Dim != "resistance" || v.Label != "R" || v.List || !v.Input || v.ESeries || v.Default == nil || *v.Default != 5000 {
		t.Errorf("target var = %+v, want a scalar resistance input R with the default 5 kOhm", v)
	}
	if len(c.Name) != len(Locales) || c.Name["en"] != "Standard-value combiner" || c.Doc["en"] == "" || c.Doc["de"] == "" || len(c.Tags) < 5 {
		t.Errorf("name %v doc %v tags %v", c.Name, c.Doc, c.Tags)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(c.Source, "IEC 60063") {
		t.Errorf("source %q does not cite IEC 60063", c.Source)
	}
}

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

`Combine` enumerates the three-digit candidates `roundSig(mantissa x 10^k, 3)` of the ranges [target/1000, target] (series) and [target, 1000 target] (parallel) and keeps the best `limit` pairs per group with a bounded sorted list (the total order (rank, R1, R2) makes the result independent of the enumeration order; sorting all 170 000 pairs of E192 was an order of magnitude slower). The JavaScript `combine` is the same algorithm. `eseries_combiner` is a normal basics item: 16 names, English and German doc, tags, an honest source (IEC 60063 for the series, Horowitz and Hill ch. 1 for the series/parallel rules), one variable `target` (5 kΩ), `dof: 1`, `finder: combine`, no rules, no formula, no schematic.

```go

}

// Kinds of a Combo.
const (
	ComboSingle   = "single"
	ComboSeries   = "series"
	ComboParallel = "parallel"
)

// Combo is one way to reach a target resistance with standard values: the single nearest value (R2 is 0), two values in
// series (R1 >= R2, Value = R1 + R2) or two values in parallel (R1 <= R2, Value = R1*R2/(R1+R2)). DevPct is
// (Value - target) / target in percent.
type Combo struct {
	Kind   string  `json:"kind"`
	R1     float64 `json:"r1"`
	R2     float64 `json:"r2"`
	Value  float64 `json:"value"`
	DevPct float64 `json:"dev_pct"`
}

// comboCandidates lists the three-digit values mantissa x 10^k of the series that lie in [lo, hi], ascending. Each is
// roundSig(m*10^k, 3), the double nearest to the decimal (and the same number in JavaScript).
func comboCandidates(mantissas []float64, lo, hi float64) []float64 {
	var out []float64
	for k := int(math.Floor(log10(lo))) - 1; k <= int(math.Floor(log10(hi)))+1; k++ {
		scale := math.Pow10(k)
		for _, m := range mantissas {
			if c := roundSig(m*scale, 3); c >= lo && c <= hi && (len(out) == 0 || c > out[len(out)-1]) {
				out = append(out, c)
			}
		}
	}
	return out
}

// ComboMaxLimit caps the limit of Combine: the groups of a real target hold thousands of pairs and nobody reads more.
const ComboMaxLimit = 1000

// comboRank is the sort key of an entry's deviation: |DevPct| in units of 1e-9 percent, rounded, so that deviations
// that agree to that precision count as equal (floating-point noise cannot reorder exact hits).
func comboRank(c Combo) float64 { return math.Round(math.Abs(c.DevPct) * 1e9) }

// comboBefore orders the entries of one group: by rank, then by R1, then by R2.
func comboBefore(qa float64, a Combo, qb float64, b Combo) bool {
	switch {
	case qa != qb:
		return qa < qb
	case a.R1 != b.R1:
		return a.R1 < b.R1
	}
	return a.R2 < b.R2
}

// comboBest keeps the best limit entries of a stream of candidates, in order. Because the order is total (R1 and R2
// differ between candidates), the result does not depend on the order in which the candidates are offered.
type comboBest struct {
	limit int
	list  []Combo
	rank  []float64
}

func (b *comboBest) offer(c Combo) {
	q := comboRank(c)
	n := len(b.list)
	if n == b.limit && !comboBefore(q, c, b.rank[n-1], b.list[n-1]) {
		return
	}
	at := n
	for at > 0 && comboBefore(q, c, b.rank[at-1], b.list[at-1]) {
		at--
	}
	if n < b.limit {
		b.list, b.rank = append(b.list, Combo{}), append(b.rank, 0)
	}
	m := len(b.list)
	copy(b.list[at+1:m], b.list[at:m-1])
	copy(b.rank[at+1:m], b.rank[at:m-1])
	b.list[at], b.rank[at] = c, q
}

// Combine lists standard values of the series that reach target: first the single nearest value (see Nearest), then at
// most limit pairs in series (both values in [target/1000, target]) and at most limit pairs in parallel (both values in
// [target, 1000*target]). Each group is ordered by |DevPct| (deviations that agree to 1e-9 percent are equal), then R1,
// then R2, and a pair appears once. A limit below one leaves the single entry and a limit above ComboMaxLimit counts as
// ComboMaxLimit. The series must be known and target finite and greater than zero.
func Combine(series string, target float64, limit int) ([]Combo, error) {
	value, dev, err := Nearest(series, target)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	out := []Combo{{Kind: ComboSingle, R1: value, Value: value, DevPct: dev}}
	if limit < 1 {
		return out, nil
	}
	limit = min(limit, ComboMaxLimit)
	mantissas := eseriesTables[series]
	deviation := func(v float64) float64 { return (v - target) / target * 100 }

	inSeries := &comboBest{limit: limit}
	small := comboCandidates(mantissas, target/1000, target)
	for i, r1 := range small {
		for _, r2 := range small[:i+1] {
			v := r1 + r2
			inSeries.offer(Combo{Kind: ComboSeries, R1: r1, R2: r2, Value: v, DevPct: deviation(v)})
		}
	}
	inParallel := &comboBest{limit: limit}
	large := comboCandidates(mantissas, target, target*1000)
	for i, r1 := range large {
		for _, r2 := range large[i:] {
			v := r1 * r2 / (r1 + r2)
			inParallel.offer(Combo{Kind: ComboParallel, R1: r1, R2: r2, Value: v, DevPct: deviation(v)})
		}
	}
	return append(append(out, inSeries.list...), inParallel.list...), nil
}

```js
    // The three-digit values mantissa x 10^k of a series in [lo, hi], ascending; each is the double nearest to the
    // decimal (Number(x.toPrecision(3)), the roundSig of internal/ecalc/eseries.go).
    function comboCandidates(table, lo, hi) {
        const out = [];
        for (let k = Math.floor(Math.log10(lo)) - 1; k <= Math.floor(Math.log10(hi)) + 1; k += 1) {
            const scale = Math.pow(10, k);
            for (const mantissa of table) {
                const candidate = Number((mantissa * scale).toPrecision(3));
                if (candidate >= lo && candidate <= hi && (out.length === 0 || candidate > out[out.length - 1])) out.push(candidate);
            }
        }
        return out;
    }

    // Order of one group: the rank of the absolute deviation (in units of 1e-9 percent, rounded, so that deviations that
    // agree to that precision are equal and floating-point noise cannot reorder exact hits), then r1, then r2.
    // Math.round and Go's math.Round agree for the non-negative values here.
    const COMBO_MAX_LIMIT = 1000;
    const comboBefore = (qa, r1a, r2a, qb, b) => (qa !== qb ? qa < qb : r1a !== b.r1 ? r1a < b.r1 : r2a < b.r2);

    // Keeps the best `limit` entries of a stream of candidates, in order; an entry is only built when it makes the list.
    // The order is total (r1 and r2 differ between candidates), so the result does not depend on the order in which the
    // candidates are offered.
    function bestOf(kind, limit, target) {
        const list = [], ranks = [];
        let worst = Infinity; // the rank of the last entry once the list is full: anything worse is dropped at once
        return {
            list,
            offer(r1, r2, value) {
                const devPct = (value - target) / target * 100;
                const q = Math.round(Math.abs(devPct) * 1e9), n = list.length;
                if (q > worst || (n === limit && !comboBefore(q, r1, r2, ranks[n - 1], list[n - 1]))) return;
                let at = n;
                while (at > 0 && comboBefore(q, r1, r2, ranks[at - 1], list[at - 1])) at -= 1;
                list.splice(at, 0, { kind, r1, r2, value, devPct });
                ranks.splice(at, 0, q);
                if (list.length > limit) { list.pop(); ranks.pop(); }
                if (list.length === limit) worst = ranks[limit - 1];
            }
        };
    }

    // The standard-value combiner (Combine in internal/ecalc/eseries.go): the single nearest value first, then at most
    // `limit` pairs in series (r1 >= r2, both values in [target/1000, target]) and at most `limit` pairs in parallel
    // (r1 <= r2, both in [target, 1000 * target]), each group by |devPct|, then r1, then r2. A limit below one leaves the
    // single entry; a limit above 1000 counts as 1000. Entries are {kind: 'single' | 'series' | 'parallel', r1, r2,
    // value, devPct}; r2 is 0 for the single value. Returns null for an unknown series or a target that is not finite
    // and greater than zero.
    function combine(series, target, limit) {
        const single = nearest(series, target);
        if (!single) return null;
        const out = [{ kind: 'single', r1: single.value, r2: 0, value: single.value, devPct: single.dev }];
        if (!(limit >= 1)) return out;
        const cap = Math.min(Math.floor(limit), COMBO_MAX_LIMIT);
        const table = TABLES[series];
        const inSeries = bestOf('series', cap, target), inParallel = bestOf('parallel', cap, target);
        const small = comboCandidates(table, target / 1000, target);
        small.forEach((r1, i) => { for (let j = 0; j <= i; j += 1) inSeries.offer(r1, small[j], r1 + small[j]); });
        const large = comboCandidates(table, target, target * 1000);
        large.forEach((r1, i) => { for (let j = i; j < large.length; j += 1) inParallel.offer(r1, large[j], r1 * large[j] / (r1 + large[j])); });
        return out.concat(inSeries.list, inParallel.list);
    }

    core.eseries = { TABLES, SERIES, nearest, combine };
```

```markdown
- Dimensions of `units.yaml` (order significant, the unit dropdowns follow it): voltage, current, resistance, power, charge, energy, number, gain, then capacitance, inductance, frequency, time, length, area, temperature, tempdiff, thermal_resistance, resistivity, tempco, ratio, angle, baudrate and integer. Energy (n µ m "" k M) and charge (n µ m "") carry the n and µ prefixes, so capacitor energies read 1.25 µJ and gate charges 47 nC. Temperature has the offset units degC and degF (non-linear `to`/`from`); a temperature difference is the separate dimension `tempdiff`, whose units only scale. Length and area carry the AWG unit (ASTM B258: diameter 0.000127 m x 92^((36-n)/39), AWG 0 = 8.251 mm, AWG 10 = 2.588 mm and 5.261 mm2, AWG 36 = 0.127 mm; the area unit is the cross-section of that diameter) and `oz` is the copper weight (35 um).

Every spelling of a dimension (base symbol, dimension aliases, unit symbols, unit aliases) belongs to one thing only; `Load` rejects a clash and an empty alias.
- The integer dimension (`integer: true`) holds whole numbers from 0 to 2^53-1 (9007199254740991) and has radix units only (`radix: 2|8|10|16`: dec, hex, bin, oct; no factor, to, from, aliases, prefixes or positive flag). `Parse` with a radix unit reads an optional `0x`/`0b`/`0o` prefix of that base (either case; decimal has none), then digits of the base (hex either case) with `_` and blanks between digits (not at either end), no sign and no SI prefix; a value above 2^53-1 is a parse error. Without a unit an integer field reads an ordinary decimal number. `Format` ignores the significant-digit setting: dec plain digits, hex `0x` plus upper-case digits in groups of four from the right (`0xDEAD_BEEF`), bin `0b` in groups of eight, that is by byte (`0b11111111`, `0b1_00000000`), oct `0o`, no unit symbol; every text `Format` writes is at most 61 characters (the largest value in binary), so it is within the 64 characters `Parse` accepts and reads back to the same value (`units_roundtrip` vectors); a value that is not a whole number in range gives "" (no unit selected: decimal digits, or the ordinary number text when the value is no whole number). `Solve` reports `range` for an integer-dimension variable that is not a whole number in 0 .. 2^53-1.
- Schema fields of phase 2: a var or derived quantity may carry `units` (the display units its dropdown offers; "" is the base symbol with automatic prefixes, every other entry an explicit unit of the dimension, no entry twice, `unit` must be in the list; empty means all, JSON `"units": []`). A choice option may carry `ignore` (primary variable ids the option does not use; the page dims them, the solver is unchanged, JSON `"ignore": []`). A calculator may carry `finder: combine` (JSON `"finder": ""|"combine"`): exactly one scalar resistance variable and `dof: 1`, and `formula` may then be empty because the page shows the combinations instead. A calculator may carry `chart: {x, y, to, samples}` (JSON `null` or an object): x is a scalar variable, y a rule target or derived quantity with an alternative that uses x, `to` an expression over known names that does not use x, `samples` 11 to 401 (101 when unset); the chart plots y over x from 0 to `to`.
- `Combine(series, target, limit)` (JavaScript `ECalcCore.eseries.combine`, entries `{kind, r1, r2, value, devPct}`; JSON `dev_pct`): the single nearest standard value first (kind `single`, r2 0), then up to `limit` series pairs (r1 >= r2, value r1 + r2, both values in [target/1000, target]) and up to `limit` parallel pairs (r1 <= r2, value r1*r2/(r1+r2), both in [target, 1000*target]). Candidates are series mantissas x 10^k rounded to 3 significant digits. Each group is ordered by |deviation| (deviations that agree to 1e-9 percent are equal, so floating-point noise cannot reorder exact hits), then r1, then r2; a pair appears once. A limit below 1 leaves the single entry and a limit above `ComboMaxLimit` (1000) counts as 1000. The catalog item `eseries_combiner` (basics) uses it; its vector file carries `combos` that are checked against `Combine` and the JavaScript mirror, and only a `finder: combine` calculator has them.
- `LocalizedJSON` normalizes the language (unknown or empty means `en`) and caches by the normalized language, so the cache never exceeds the 16 locales; the body and ETag of `en`, `xx` and `""` are identical. Collections in the JSON are never `null`.
```

## Part U — UI extensions (tasks U1–U6)

Contract deviations:

1. **`desktop.ecalc_combos` carries the placeholder `{series}`** ("Combinations of {series} values", like `ecalc_eseries_nearest`): the combiner heading names the E series of the settings. `TestDesktopECalcLocaleKeysExistInAllLanguages` pins the placeholder in all 16 locales. Every other key is a plain string.
2. **What the `units` list of a variable means for the dropdown.** `""` admits the automatic prefix *and* the fixed prefixes of the base symbol (`prefix:m`, `prefix:k`, ...); every other entry must be an explicit unit of the dimension and admits just that unit. So `units: ["", "mil", "in"]` on a length shows Auto, the prefixes, mil and in but no AWG, and `units: ["dec", "hex", "bin", "oct"]` shows exactly the four number systems. A list that leaves a single choice shows it as static text. When neither the stored choice nor the catalog's `unit` is offered, the first offered choice applies.
3. **The schematics test is one check stricter than the contract**: besides reading all ten files and failing on a duplicate id, it fails when a schematic sits in the file of another category than its calculator (a content part cannot file a drawing under the wrong category). The category of the calculator comes from the catalog JSON (`category`).
4. **Symbol geometry.** `switch` is a two-terminal symbol (pins `a` (0, 0) and `b` (3, 0), drawn open). `pot` is four grid units wide: pins `a` (0, 0), `b` (4, 0) and the wiper `w` (2, -2) above the body (`flip` puts the wiper below); IEC draws the rectangle with a wiper arrow, ANSI the zigzag with the arrow. Content parts place them with `{"sym": "pot", "x": .., "y": .., "rot": ..}` and may not add symbols.
5. **Launch details beyond the contract.** A launch always starts from the defaults of the calculator (not from what the window stored), then applies the given choices and values; a text that does not read as a value of its variable is skipped (typing such a text does not store it either); a launch clears the search box; `ECalcApp.launch` returns `false` for an unknown window or a payload that is not an object and `true` otherwise (an unknown page id is accepted and ignored). A payload that arrives while the catalog is loading waits for it, also across a failed load that is retried.

Implementation notes (decisions the contract leaves open, not deviations):

- **File format of the category files.** The wrapper is exactly `window.ECalcSchematics = Object.assign(window.ECalcSchematics || {}, ` + the JSON object + `);`. `ecalc-schematics-basics.js` keeps the multi-line layout of phase 1 (first line ends with `{`, last line is `});`); the nine other files are one line, `{}`. The Go test accepts both because it decodes the text between the wrapper and `);`.
- **The `wheatstone` drawing is corrected in the same edit** (found by the geometry checker of the content parts): the top rail and the bottom rail each join the R1 / R2 branch in a T that had no junction dot (dots added at (16, 2) and (16, 10)), and the chip of V_D hung 0.1 grid units above the bottom rail. The bottom rail moves from y = 9 to y = 10 (`h` 11 → 12) so that the pocket below the meter between R2 and R4 is 4.3 units high and the V_D chip (anchor (20, 6.2), side `bottom`, about 2.8 units high at the default scale) sits beside the detector branch with at least 0.7 units to every wire; the width stays 32. Measured in the page, no chip of any of the seven drawings comes within 0.2 grid units of a wire (the chips of the other drawings sit directly beside their parts by design). The width limit for anchored chips at the default 1100 px window is **32** grid units (at 33 the chips no longer fit and are listed under the drawing), which is what `AGENTS.md` says.
- **No bundled core file changes.** `module-loader.js` is loaded by `desktop.html`, it is not part of `main.bundle.js`, so `npm run build:ui` leaves every bundle unchanged and `npm run build:ui -- --check` stays clean (it is still run in U1 and U6). Part B's changes to `menus-and-routing.js` (filling `ctx.launch`) are the ones that need a bundle rebuild.
- **Chart semantics.** y is evaluated by `ECalcCore.solve.solve` with every other quantity of the page (inputs and computed values alike) held at its current value and x overridden, so it is the curve "y over x, everything else fixed". The chart is hidden while an expression of y needs a quantity that has no finite value, or while `to` (evaluated with the page's values) is not finite and above zero. The x axis runs 0 .. `to`; the y axis always contains 0 and has five round ticks (steps 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4 or 5 times a power of ten); tick texts come from the units formatter with at most three significant digits and the unit selected for the field (a derived y uses its `unit`).
- **Combiner block.** It sits between the field stage / formula card and the E-series and derived blocks; the groups are Single value (first column `–`), In series (`R1 + R2`) and In parallel (`R1 ∥ R2`), at most five rows each, deviations coloured like the E-series rows. It needs `ECalcCore.eseries.combine(series, target, limit)` returning `{kind, r1, r2, value, devPct}` (contract §1.5) and shows nothing when that function is missing, the target is not above zero or the series is unknown. The target is the only scalar `resistance` variable of the calculator. Part A measured the search at about 30 ms in E96 and 110-200 ms in E192, so `paintCombos` waits 120 ms after the last change (`COMBO_PAUSE_MS`), does not search again while series and target stay the same (a change of the significant digits only redraws the texts) and `dispose` stops the pending timer. The combiner's `formula` is empty: a calculator with neither a formula nor a chart gets no formula card and a one-column main block.
- **Radix fields.** The UI part is the text keyboard (`inputmode="text"` instead of `decimal`) for fields of the `integer` dimension; formatting and parsing (`0xDEAD_BEEF`, `0b1_00101100`, no unit symbol) come from `ECalcCore.units` (Part A). The solver's range error for a value that is not an integer in [0, 2^53 - 1] reuses the text of `desktop.ecalc_error_range` ("This value must be greater than zero.").
- **Browser test fixtures.** Content that later parts write is stood in for by patches of the served catalog: a `units` list on V_out of the voltage divider, a `chart` on the divider (V_out over R_2, stands in for `rc_time_constant`), an `ignore` list on the "power" option of the decibel calculator (stands in for the cable calculator) and a calculator `fx_radix` with two `integer` fields in the category passive (stands in for `number_systems`). The combiner steps use the real `eseries_combiner`. Counts and the list of drawings come from the served catalog, so the test follows the content parts.

**Binary grouping (found while verifying U6, resolved in Part A).** Grouped by four, a binary value of 2^50 or more formats to more than 64 characters (68 for 2^53 - 1) and would not read back through the 64-character input cap. Part A therefore groups binary output by eight digits from the right (`0b1_00101100` for 300; 61 characters for 2^53 - 1); the browser test of U6 expects that form.

**Dependencies on the other parts (read before starting).**

- **Part A** is needed only by Task U6 (and by the manual verification of U4/U5): `ECalcCore.eseries.combine`, the radix units of the `integer` dimension with their JS formatting, the new dimensions and `dBuV`, and the real `eseries_combiner` item of the basics category (`internal/ecalc/**`, `ui/js/desktop/apps/ecalc/ecalc-{expr,units,eseries,solve}.js`, `testdata/catalog.en.json`). Tasks U1-U5 need nothing from A: their guard tests do not read the catalog beyond the schematics cross-check, and the phase 1 browser test (run once after U4 and once after U5) passes both on the base files and with A's final tree in place (there the basics list is twelve long and the old test counts eleven: raise its two counts, `got != 11 {` and `.length===11`, to 12 for that run).
- **Part B** is not needed. B fills `ctx.launch` in the desktop core and calls `window.ECalcApp.launch(windowId, payload)`; U5 provides exactly that hook and U6 calls it directly.
- Order: **U1 → U2 → U3 → U4 → U5 → U6**.

### Task U1: Split the schematics into ten category files; the `switch` and `pot` symbols

**Files:**
- Rename (and edit): `ui/js/desktop/apps/ecalc/ecalc-schematics.js` → `ui/js/desktop/apps/ecalc/ecalc-schematics-basics.js` (the seven phase 1 drawings, new wrapper; the `wheatstone` drawing is corrected, see below)
- Create: `ui/js/desktop/apps/ecalc/ecalc-schematics-{digital,filters,opamps,passive,power,rf,semiconductors,timers,wiring}.js` (nine one-line files, `{}`)
- Modify: `ui/js/desktop/apps/ecalc/ecalc-symbols.js`, `ui/js/desktop/core/module-loader.js`
- Modify: `ui/desktop_ecalc_schematics_test.go`, `ui/desktop_ecalc_test.go`

Each category file is exactly `window.ECalcSchematics = Object.assign(window.ECalcSchematics || {}, {JSON});` where `{JSON}` is the JSON object of the schematics of that category, so the ten files add up to the single object of phase 1. Wave-2 content parts replace the `{}` of their category file with their drawings and may use every symbol of the library (new: `switch`, `pot`).

The schematics test reads all ten files (basics first, then alphabetical, the order of the module loader), fails on a duplicate id and on a schematic that sits in the file of another category than its calculator, and a new test pins the split and the two new symbols with their pins. The count of scripts in the folder moves from 11 to 20 and the load order lists the ten files.

// ecalcCatalogItem is the part of the catalog JSON of the server route (contract section 7) the cross-check reads.
type ecalcCatalogItem struct {
	Kind      string `json:"kind"`
	ID        string `json:"id"`
	Category  string `json:"category"`
	Schematic string `json:"schematic"`
	Vars      []struct {
		ID string `json:"id"`
	} `json:"vars"`
}

// loadECalcSchematics reads the ten schematics files. Each is exactly
// `window.ECalcSchematics = Object.assign(window.ECalcSchematics || {}, {JSON});`; the schematics of all files are merged
// by id and a duplicate id fails. files maps every schematic id to the category of the file that holds it.
func loadECalcSchematics(t *testing.T) (specs map[string]ecalcSchematic, files map[string]string) {
	t.Helper()
	specs, files = map[string]ecalcSchematic{}, map[string]string{}
	for _, category := range ecalcSchematicCategories {
		path := ecalcSchematicsPath(category)
		text := strings.TrimSpace(readDesktopAssetText(t, path))
		if !strings.HasPrefix(text, ecalcSchematicsWrapper+"{") || !strings.HasSuffix(text, "});") {
			t.Fatalf("%s must be exactly `%s{JSON});`", path, ecalcSchematicsWrapper)
		}
		body := strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimPrefix(text, ecalcSchematicsWrapper), ");")
		decoder := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader([]byte(body)))
		decoder.DisallowUnknownFields()
		var own map[string]ecalcSchematic
		if err := decoder.Decode(&own); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s is not strict JSON of the schematic schema: %v", path, err)
		}
		for id, spec := range own {
			if first, dup := files[id]; dup {
				t.Errorf("schematic %q is defined in both ecalc-schematics-%s.js and ecalc-schematics-%s.js", id, first, category)
				continue
			}
			specs[id], files[id] = spec, category
		}
	}
	return specs, files
}

// The split is complete: exactly the ten category files exist (the old single file is gone), every one starts with the
// wrapper and ends with `});`, and the symbol library holds the two symbols that phase 2 adds, with the pin names the
// schematic authors rely on (switch: a, b; pot: a, b and the wiper w).
func TestECalcSchematicFilesAndNewSymbols(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	entries, err := fs.ReadDir(Content, ecalcDir)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read %s: %v", ecalcDir, err)
	}
	found := map[string]bool{}
	for _, entry := range entries {
		if strings.HasPrefix(entry.Name(), "ecalc-schematics") {
			found[entry.Name()] = true
		}
	}
	for _, category := range ecalcSchematicCategories {
		name := "ecalc-schematics-" + category + ".js"
		if !found[name] {
			t.Errorf("%s/%s is missing", ecalcDir, name)
		}
		delete(found, name)
		text := strings.TrimSpace(readDesktopAssetText(t, ecalcSchematicsPath(category)))
		if !strings.HasPrefix(text, ecalcSchematicsWrapper+"{") || !strings.HasSuffix(text, "});") || strings.Count(text, "window.ECalcSchematics") != 2 {
			t.Errorf("%s must be exactly `%s{JSON});`", name, ecalcSchematicsWrapper)
		}
	}
	for name := range found {
		t.Errorf("%s/%s is not one of the ten category files (the single ecalc-schematics.js is gone)", ecalcDir, name)
	}
	symbols := readDesktopAssetText(t, ecalcSymbolsPath)
	for _, marker := range []string{"        switch: {", "        pot: {", "pins: () => ({ a: [0, 0], b: [4, 0], w: [2, -2] }),"} {
		if !strings.Contains(symbols, marker) {
			t.Errorf("%s is missing %q", ecalcSymbolsPath, marker)
		}
	}
}

### Task U2: Strings for the new dimensions, the dimmed field, the combiner and the chart (16 languages)

**Files:**
- Modify: `ui/lang/desktop/{cs,da,de,el,en,es,fr,hi,it,ja,nl,no,pl,pt,sv,zh}.json` (23 keys each, 368 lines in all)
- Modify: `ui/desktop_ecalc_i18n_test.go`, `ui/desktop_ecalc_test.go`

The keys: `desktop.ecalc_dim_<id>` for the 15 new dimensions of contract §1.1 (`capacitance inductance frequency time length area temperature tempdiff thermal_resistance resistivity tempco ratio angle baudrate integer`; the unit dropdown looks them up dynamically as its label and title), `desktop.ecalc_unused_field` (the title of a dimmed field), `desktop.ecalc_combos` (heading, with `{series}`), `desktop.ecalc_combo_single`, `desktop.ecalc_combo_series`, `desktop.ecalc_combo_parallel` (the group rows), `desktop.ecalc_combo_value`, `desktop.ecalc_combo_deviation` (the column heads) and `desktop.ecalc_chart` (the chart heading and the start of its accessible name). The `integer` dimension is labelled "Number base" (the dropdown offers dec, hex, bin and oct), the `area` dimension "Area" (it holds cross-sections too).

Save this script next to it as `add-ecalc-keys.mjs`. It puts the new lines into the contiguous block of `"desktop.ecalc_*"` keys of every file at their sorted position and touches no other byte (running it twice is harmless):

```javascript
// Adds the phase 2 ECalc UI strings to the 16 desktop language files. Usage: node add-ecalc-keys.mjs <i18n-u.json> <repo root>
// The new lines go into the contiguous block of "desktop.ecalc_*" keys at their sorted position; every other byte of
// the files stays as it is. Running it twice is harmless (a key that already exists is replaced in place).
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';

const [dataFile, repo] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (!dataFile || !repo) throw new Error('usage: node add-ecalc-keys.mjs <i18n-u.json> <repo root>');
const data = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(dataFile, 'utf8'));
const LOCALES = ['cs', 'da', 'de', 'el', 'en', 'es', 'fr', 'hi', 'it', 'ja', 'nl', 'no', 'pl', 'pt', 'sv', 'zh'];
const prefix = '  "desktop.ecalc_';

for (const lang of LOCALES) {
    if (!data[lang]) throw new Error('no strings for ' + lang);
    const file = path.join(repo, 'ui', 'lang', 'desktop', lang + '.json');
    const text = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
    const lines = text.split('\n');
    const first = lines.findIndex(line => line.startsWith(prefix));
    let last = first;
    while (last + 1 < lines.length && lines[last + 1].startsWith(prefix)) last += 1;
    if (first < 0) throw new Error(file + ': no desktop.ecalc_ block');
    const entries = new Map();
    for (const line of lines.slice(first, last + 1)) {
        const key = /^ {2}"([^"]+)":/.exec(line)[1];
        entries.set(key, line.endsWith(',') ? line : line + ',');
    }
    for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(data[lang])) {
        entries.set('desktop.' + name, '  ' + JSON.stringify('desktop.' + name) + ': ' + JSON.stringify(value) + ',');
    }
    const block = [...entries.keys()].sort().map(key => entries.get(key));
    const next = lines.slice(0, first).concat(block, lines.slice(last + 1)).join('\n');
    JSON.parse(next);
    fs.writeFileSync(file, next);
    console.log(lang + ': ' + Object.keys(data[lang]).length + ' keys, block now ' + block.length + ' lines');
}
```

### Task U3: The chart builder `ecalc-chart.js`

**Files:**
- Create: `ui/js/desktop/apps/ecalc/ecalc-chart.js`
- Modify: `ui/js/desktop/core/module-loader.js`, `ui/desktop_ecalc_test.go`

`window.ECalcChart.svg(spec, sample)` is a DOM-free string builder like the schematic renderer: it samples `sample(x)` at `spec.samples` points (11-401, default 101) from 0 to `spec.xMax`, picks a y axis that contains 0 with five round ticks, draws grid, axes, the curve (gaps where `sample` is not finite) and, when `spec.point` is inside, a dot with two dashed guides, and writes the tick texts through `spec.fmtX` / `spec.fmtY` (the page passes the units formatter). It returns `''` when there is nothing to draw. Every stroke is `currentColor`; the colours of the curve and the dot come from the classes `ec-chart-*` of the stylesheet (U4). The accessible name is `spec.label`.
