```go
// The chart builder is a DOM-free string builder (it is run by the page, the markup uses currentColor and the ec-chart-*
// classes of the stylesheet), so it holds no document access and no colour of its own.
func TestECalcChartIsADomFreeStringBuilder(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	chart := ecalcScripts(t)["ecalc-chart.js"]
	for _, marker := range []string{"window.ECalcChart = { svg };", "function svg(spec, sample)", "function axis(lo, hi)", "const TICKS = 5,", `stroke="currentColor"`, `class="ec-chart-curve"`, `class="ec-chart-dot"`, `class="ec-chart-axis"`} {
		if !strings.Contains(chart, marker) {
			t.Errorf("ecalc-chart.js is missing %q", marker)
		}
	}
	body := regexp.MustCompile(`(?s)/\*.*?\*/`).ReplaceAllString(chart, "")
	for label, pattern := range map[string]string{
		"document access": `\bdocument\b`,
		"DOM write":       `\b(?:innerHTML|createElement|appendChild)\b`,
		"hex colour":      `#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\b`,
		"colour function": `\b(?:rgba?|hsla?)\(`,
	} {
		if regexp.MustCompile(pattern).MatchString(body) {
			t.Errorf("ecalc-chart.js must not contain a %s", label)
		}
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement the chart builder**

Create `ui/js/desktop/apps/ecalc/ecalc-chart.js` with exactly this content:

```javascript
/* ECalc chart: the line chart of a calculator that declares `chart` in the catalog (a curve of one quantity over another,
   for example the charge curve of an RC circuit). A DOM-free classic script that publishes window.ECalcChart and builds
   one inline SVG string, like the schematics do: every stroke is currentColor, the colours of the curve and the dot come
   from the classes ec-chart-* in css/desktop-app-ecalc.css (tokens only).

   ECalcChart.svg(spec, sample) -> SVG markup, or '' when there is nothing to draw (no finite sample, xMax not > 0).
     spec:   {xMax, samples, label, xLabel, yLabel, fmtX, fmtY, point}
             xMax      the curve runs from x = 0 to xMax (base units)
             samples   number of points, clamped to 11..401 (default 101)
             label     accessible name of the drawing
             xLabel, yLabel   axis titles; the text behind the first underscore is a subscript (V_C)
             fmtX, fmtY       tick text of a value (the page passes the units formatter, so ticks read "1.25 ms")
             point     {x, y} of the current operating point, drawn as a dot with guides, or null
     sample: x -> y (base units); a non-finite y leaves a gap in the curve.
   Both axes carry five ticks. The x axis is 0 .. xMax. The y axis always contains 0 and runs in steps of 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4 or 5
   times a power of ten, so the tick values are round numbers. */
(function () {
    'use strict';

    const W = 320, H = 200;
    const LEFT = 58, RIGHT = 12, TOP = 18, BOTTOM = 46;
    const TICKS = 5, MIN_SAMPLES = 11, MAX_SAMPLES = 401, DEFAULT_SAMPLES = 101;
    const escape = text => String(text).replace(/[&<>"']/g, char => ({ '&': '&amp;', '<': '&lt;', '>': '&gt;', '"': '&quot;', "'": '&#39;' }[char]));
    const num = x => String(Math.round(x * 100) / 100);
    const round12 = x => Number(x.toPrecision(12));

    // V_C -> V<tspan>C</tspan>: the text behind the first underscore is the subscript.
    function titleMarkup(text) {
        const label = String(text == null ? '' : text), at = label.indexOf('_');
        if (at <= 0) return escape(label);
        return escape(label.slice(0, at)) + '<tspan class="ec-chart-sub" dy="3">' + escape(label.slice(at + 1)) + '</tspan>';
    }

    // The y axis for data between lo and hi: {min, max, step} with max = min + 4 * step, 0 inside.
    function axis(lo, hi) {
        const low = Math.min(0, lo), high = Math.max(0, hi);
        if (!(high > low)) return { min: 0, max: TICKS - 1, step: 1 };
        const raw = (high - low) / (TICKS - 1);
        for (let scale = Math.pow(10, Math.floor(Math.log10(raw))); ; scale *= 10) {
            for (const factor of [1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 5]) {
                const step = factor * scale, min = round12(Math.floor(low / step + 1e-9) * step);
                if (min + step * (TICKS - 1) >= high - step * 1e-9) return { min, max: round12(min + step * (TICKS - 1)), step };
            }
        }
    }

    function svg(spec, sample) {
        const xMax = Number(spec && spec.xMax);
        if (!(xMax > 0) || !Number.isFinite(xMax) || typeof sample !== 'function') return '';
        const count = Math.max(MIN_SAMPLES, Math.min(MAX_SAMPLES, Math.round(Number(spec.samples) || DEFAULT_SAMPLES)));
        const points = [];
        let lo = Infinity, hi = -Infinity;
        for (let i = 0; i < count; i += 1) {
            const x = xMax * i / (count - 1);
            let y;
            try { y = sample(x); } catch (error) { y = NaN; }
            points.push([x, y]);
            if (Number.isFinite(y)) { lo = Math.min(lo, y); hi = Math.max(hi, y); }
        }
        if (!Number.isFinite(lo)) return '';
        const dot = spec.point && Number.isFinite(spec.point.x) && Number.isFinite(spec.point.y) && spec.point.x >= 0 && spec.point.x <= xMax ? spec.point : null;
        if (dot) { lo = Math.min(lo, dot.y); hi = Math.max(hi, dot.y); }
        const y = axis(lo, hi);
        const left = LEFT, right = W - RIGHT, top = TOP, bottom = H - BOTTOM;
        const px = x => left + x / xMax * (right - left);
        const py = value => bottom - (value - y.min) / (y.max - y.min) * (bottom - top);
        const fmtX = spec.fmtX || String, fmtY = spec.fmtY || String;

        let grid = '', labels = '';
        for (let i = 0; i < TICKS; i += 1) {
            const x = round12(xMax * i / (TICKS - 1)), value = round12(y.min + y.step * i);
            const gx = num(px(x)), gy = num(py(value));
            if (i > 0) grid += '<path class="ec-chart-grid" d="M' + gx + ' ' + top + 'V' + bottom + '"/>';
            if (i > 0) grid += '<path class="ec-chart-grid" d="M' + left + ' ' + gy + 'H' + right + '"/>';
            labels += '<text class="ec-chart-text" x="' + gx + '" y="' + (bottom + 13) + '" text-anchor="' + (i === TICKS - 1 ? 'end' : 'middle') + '" stroke="none" fill="currentColor">' + escape(fmtX(x)) + '</text>';
            labels += '<text class="ec-chart-text" x="' + (left - 6) + '" y="' + num(py(value) + 3.5) + '" text-anchor="end" stroke="none" fill="currentColor">' + escape(fmtY(value)) + '</text>';
        }
        labels += '<text class="ec-chart-text" x="' + num((left + right) / 2) + '" y="' + (H - 6) + '" text-anchor="middle" stroke="none" fill="currentColor">' + titleMarkup(spec.xLabel) + '</text>';
        labels += '<text class="ec-chart-text" x="' + left + '" y="' + (top - 7) + '" text-anchor="start" stroke="none" fill="currentColor">' + titleMarkup(spec.yLabel) + '</text>';

        let d = '', pen = false;
        for (const [x, value] of points) {
            if (!Number.isFinite(value)) { pen = false; continue; }
            d += (pen ? 'L' : 'M') + num(px(x)) + ' ' + num(py(value));
            pen = true;
        }
        let marker = '';
        if (dot) {
            const cx = num(px(dot.x)), cy = num(py(dot.y));
            marker = '<path class="ec-chart-guide" d="M' + cx + ' ' + bottom + 'V' + cy + 'H' + left + '"/><circle class="ec-chart-dot" cx="' + cx + '" cy="' + cy + '" r="4"/>';
        }
        return '<svg class="ec-chart-svg" viewBox="0 0 ' + W + ' ' + H + '" role="img" aria-label="' + escape(spec.label || '') + '" focusable="false" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round">'
            + grid
            + '<path class="ec-chart-axis" d="M' + left + ' ' + top + 'V' + bottom + 'H' + right + '"/>'
            + '<path class="ec-chart-curve" d="' + d + '"/>'
            + marker + labels + '</svg>';
    }

    window.ECalcChart = { svg };
})();
```

### Task U4: Calculator page — units list, unused fields, radix keyboard, combiner and chart blocks

**Files:**
- Modify: `ui/js/desktop/apps/ecalc/ecalc-calc-page.js`, `ui/css/desktop-app-ecalc.css`, `ui/desktop_ecalc_test.go`

All of it is driven by the catalog JSON (contract §1.4); nothing changes for a calculator that has none of the fields:

- `units` on a variable: `unitChoices(v, units)` narrows the dropdown (deviation 2); `unitFor(calc, store, units)` is the former inline `unitOf` (stored choice, else the catalog's `unit`, else the first offered choice).
- `ignore` on a choice option: `ignoredIds()` is the union over the selected options; such a field gets `data-unused="true"` and the title `desktop.ecalc_unused_field`, stays editable, keeps `data-state="input"` whatever the solver says about it (only a text that was typed and cannot be read still shows its error), and is left out of the copied results and of the E-series suggestions.
- Radix: `inputmode="text"` for `integer` fields.
- `finder: combine`: the combiner block (`paintCombos` / `drawCombos`, debounced, see the combiner note).
- `chart`: the chart block inside the formula card (`chartData` / `paintChart`, see the chart note); a calculator with neither formula nor chart gets no formula card and a one-column `.ec-main`.

```go
// The page extensions of phase 2 are wired where the contract puts them: the unit whitelist, the dimmed fields of an
// `ignore` list, the radix keyboard, the combiner block and the chart block.
func TestECalcPageExtensionsAreWired(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	page := ecalcScripts(t)["ecalc-calc-page.js"]
	for _, marker := range []string{
```

```javascript
    // The unit choices of a field: every choice of its dimension, narrowed by the `units` list of the variable when it
    // has one. "" in the list admits the automatic prefix and the fixed prefixes of the base symbol; every other entry
    // is an explicit unit of the dimension.
    function unitChoices(v, units) {
        const all = units.options(v.dim), allowed = Array.isArray(v.units) && v.units.length ? v.units : null;
        if (!allowed) return all;
        const list = all.filter(option => (option.kind === 'explicit' ? allowed.includes(option.id) : allowed.includes('')));
        return list.length ? list : all;

    // The display unit of every variable of a calculator as a function of the variable id: the stored choice when this
    // catalog still offers it ('auto' is the automatic prefix), else the default unit of the variable (else the first
    // unit its list offers).
    function unitFor(calc, store, units) {
        const varById = new Map(calc.vars.map(v => [v.id, v]));
        return id => {
            const v = varById.get(id);
            if (!v) return '';

            if (v.unit) return v.unit;
            return offered.some(option => option.id === '') || !offered.length ? '' : offered[0].id;
```

```javascript
        // The standard-value combinations of the target of a `finder: combine` calculator for the E series of the settings:
        // the nearest single value, then the best series and the best parallel pairs, each with its deviation. Finding them
        // takes up to a few hundred milliseconds in the finest series, so the search waits for a pause in the typing and is
        // not repeated while series and target stay the same (a change of the digits only draws the texts again).
        function paintCombos() {
            if (!combosBlock) return;
            const series = store.prefs().eseries, target = result.values[comboVar.id], key = series + '|' + target;
            if (!(Number.isFinite(target) && target > 0)) {
                clearTimeout(comboTimer);
                comboKey = '';
                combos = { series, list: [] };
            } else if (key !== comboKey) {
                clearTimeout(comboTimer);
                comboTimer = setTimeout(() => {
                    comboKey = key;
                    let list = [];
                    try { list = typeof core.eseries.combine === 'function' ? core.eseries.combine(series, target, COMBO_LIMIT) || [] : []; } catch (error) { list = []; }
                    combos = { series, list };
                    drawCombos();
                }, COMBO_PAUSE_MS);
                return;
            }
            drawCombos();
        }
        function drawCombos() {
            const { series, list } = combos;
            combosBlock.hidden = !list.length;
            if (!list.length) return;
            const show = x => esc(display(comboVar, x, ''));
            const rowOf = combo => {
                const size = Math.abs(combo.devPct), tone = size < 1 ? 'ok' : size >= 5 ? 'warn' : 'mid';
                const parts = combo.kind === 'single' ? '–' : show(combo.r1) + (combo.kind === 'series' ? ' + ' : ' ∥ ') + show(combo.r2);
                return '<tr><th scope="row" class="ec-combo-parts">' + parts + '</th><td class="ec-row-val">' + show(combo.value) + '</td><td class="ec-row-dev" data-tone="' + tone + '">' + esc(percent(combo.devPct)) + '</td></tr>';
            };
            const groups = [['single', 'desktop.ecalc_combo_single'], ['series', 'desktop.ecalc_combo_series'], ['parallel', 'desktop.ecalc_combo_parallel']];
            const body = groups.map(([kind, key]) => {
                const rows = list.filter(combo => combo.kind === kind);
                return rows.length ? '<tbody data-kind="' + kind + '"><tr class="ec-combo-group"><th scope="rowgroup" colspan="3">' + esc(t(key)) + '</th></tr>' + rows.map(rowOf).join('') + '</tbody>' : '';
            }).join('');
            const title = t('desktop.ecalc_combos', { series });
            combosBlock.querySelector('[data-label="combos"]').textContent = title;
            combosWrap.innerHTML = '<table class="ec-combo-table"><thead><tr><th scope="col" class="ec-sr">' + esc(title) + '</th><th scope="col">' + esc(t('desktop.ecalc_combo_value')) + '</th><th scope="col">' + esc(t('desktop.ecalc_combo_deviation')) + '</th></tr></thead>' + body + '</table>';
```

### Task U5: Launch hook for the pre-fill bridge

**Files:**
- Modify: `ui/js/desktop/apps/ecalc/ecalc-calc-page.js`, `ui/js/desktop/apps/ecalc/ecalc-shell.js`, `ui/js/desktop/apps/ecalc/ecalc.js`, `ui/desktop_ecalc_test.go`

The hook Part B calls (contract §2 / §7), with no change to the desktop core:

- `ECalcApp.render(host, id, ctx)` reads `ctx.launch` (an object or undefined); `ECalcApp.launch(windowId, payload)` applies a payload to an open window and returns whether it was accepted (deviation 5). Payload: `{page: "<item id>", values: {"<var>": "<raw text>"}, choices: {"<choice>": "<option>"}}`.
- `ECalcShell.create({..., launch})` opens the launched page instead of the remembered one; `shell.launch(payload)` opens a page of the open window. `ECalcCalcPage.launchState(calc, payload, units, unitOf)` builds the state: the defaults, the given options, then every given value entered through `ECalcCore.solve.applyEdit` exactly as if typed (so `recency` follows the given order, the inputs that are not given keep their defaults, a computed variable that becomes an input keeps its value, no lock is set). The shell stores it with `store.saveCalc` before the page is mounted, so the page restores it like any stored state and the next open shows it too. A payload with only a page id opens the page and keeps what it holds.
- A payload that arrives before the catalog has loaded waits in `pending` and is handed to `ECalcShell.create` as `launch`.

```go
// The launch hook is wired where the contract puts it: ctx.launch at render time and ECalcApp.launch for an open window
// reach the shell, which stores the pre-filled state (ECalcCalcPage.launchState) and opens the page. The desktop core
// itself is not touched by this part.
func TestECalcLaunchHookIsWired(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	scripts := ecalcScripts(t)
	for file, markers := range map[string][]string{
		"ecalc-calc-page.js": {"function launchState(calc, payload, units, unitOf)", "window.ECalcCalcPage = { create, launchState, unitFor };"},
		"ecalc-shell.js":     {"function launch(payload)", "Page.launchState(item, payload, units, Page.unitFor(item, store, units))", "if (wanted) launch(options.launch);"},
		"ecalc.js":           {"ctx.launch", "function launch(id, payload)", "if (shell) shell.launch(payload); else pending = payload;", "uid, launch: pending"},
	} {
		for _, marker := range markers {
			if !strings.Contains(scripts[file], marker) {
				t.Errorf("%s is missing %q", file, marker)
			}
		}
	}
}
```


with:

```javascript
    // The state a launch payload ({values: {var: raw text}, choices: {choice: option}}) opens a page with: the defaults,
    // then the given options, then the given values entered one after the other exactly as if they were typed (so the
    // recency follows the given order, the inputs that are not given keep their defaults, nothing is locked). Unknown
    // variables, choices and options, variables that cannot be inputs and texts that do not read as a value of their
    // variable are skipped.
    function launchState(calc, payload, units, unitOf) {
        const given = payload && typeof payload === 'object' ? payload : {};
        const plain = object => (object && typeof object === 'object' && !Array.isArray(object) ? object : {});
        let state = S.defaultState(calc, units, unitOf);
        const wanted = plain(given.choices);
        for (const choice of calc.choices || []) {
            if (has(wanted, choice.id) && typeof wanted[choice.id] === 'string' && choice.options.some(option => option.id === wanted[choice.id])) state.choices[choice.id] = wanted[choice.id];
        }
        for (const [name, raw] of Object.entries(plain(given.values))) {
            const v = calc.vars.find(entry => entry.id === name);
            if (!v || v.input === false || typeof raw !== 'string') continue;
            try {
                if (v.list) units.parseList(raw, v.dim, unitOf(name)); else units.parse(raw, v.dim, unitOf(name));
            } catch (error) {
                continue;
            }
            const shown = S.solve(calc, S.readInputs(calc, state, units, unitOf).values, state.choices, units).values;
            state = S.applyEdit(calc, state, name, raw, units, unitOf, shown);
        }
        return state;
    }

    // options: {calc, units, store, t, icon, uid, decimalComma, schematics, onFavorite}
    function create(options) {
```

```javascript
    function dispose(id) {
        const entry = instances.get(id);
        instances.delete(id);
        if (entry) entry.stop();
    }

    // Applies a launch payload to an already open window. Returns false when there is no such window or no payload.
    function launch(id, payload) {
        const entry = instances.get(id);
        if (!entry || !payload || typeof payload !== 'object' || Array.isArray(payload)) return false;
        entry.launch(payload);
        return true;
    }
```

### Task U6: Browser test for the phase 2 UI, DOX note and final verification

**Files:**
- Modify: `ui/desktop_ecalc_browser_test.go`, `ui/js/desktop/apps/AGENTS.md`

This task needs Part A's files in the tree (`ECalcCore.eseries.combine`, the `integer` radix units, the new dimensions, the real `eseries_combiner`). The browser test is extended, in the real desktop shell with the catalog of the server route (German desktop, decimal commas):

- **units list**: V_out (patched `units: ["", "dBV"]`) offers 8 choices, dBV and the prefixes but not dBu; V_in has no list and offers every choice of the voltage dimension (the count comes from the catalog).
- **chart** (patched into the divider): five ticks per axis with units (`0 Ω`, `5,5 kΩ`, `11 kΩ`, `16,5 kΩ`, `22 kΩ` / `0 V`, `2,5 V`, `5 V`, `7,5 V`, `10 V`), 101 curve points, the dot at (83, 101.97), heading and accessible name, under the formula and inside its card; it follows R_2 (`100 kΩ` at 10 kΩ), disappears for R_2 = 0 (the end of the range is 0) and returns after reset; it fits the phone-sized page.
- **ignore** (patched into the decibel calculator): with the "power" option A_2 is dimmed with the hint as its title, stays `input` although it is the computed value, is left out of the copied text, and is tinted again with the other option.
- **combiner** (the real `eseries_combiner`): the German heading and columns, the three groups, 5.1 kΩ (+2.0 %) as the single value for 5 kΩ in E24, five series and five parallel rows ordered by the size of their deviation, below the fields; E12 gives 4.7 kΩ and E192 still lists five of each (the search is debounced); 4k7 gives an exact single value and an exact best series pair; the table fits the phone-sized page.
- **radix** (fixture `fx_radix`): `0xFF` and `255`, the text keyboard, typing `0x10`, `300`, the unit switch to `bin` (`0b1_00101100`) and `oct` (`0o454`), `dead_beef` in a hex field (`0xDEAD_BEEF` after blur, `3735928559` as decimal), the text of an input is rewritten when its unit changes, an unreadable text shows the error.
- **symbols**: the pins of `switch` and `pot`, both symbol standards, a screenshot of both.
- **schematic split**: `window.ECalcSchematics` holds exactly the drawings the catalog names, and the chips of every drawing of the catalog (all categories) stay inside it and apart.
- **launch hook**: on the open window a payload with values (V_in = 9 V then V_out = 3 V leaves R_2 at its default and computes R_1 = 4,4 kΩ; the stored texts, order and absence of locks are read back from `localStorage`), unknown variables and choices and unreadable texts are skipped, an unknown page changes nothing, an unknown choice option keeps the default, a page id alone keeps the stored state, an unknown window and an empty payload are refused; at render time `ctx.launch` opens the page pre-filled; a payload that arrives while the catalog is loading is applied after it.

## Part B — Agent tool `ecalc` and the desktop pre-fill bridge

Part B gives the agent the ECalc catalog: the tool `ecalc` with `search`, `describe`, `calculate` and `open`, and the bridge that lets `open` show a calculator on the desktop pre-filled with the agent's values. It is one query API in `internal/ecalc` (`query.go`), one tool implementation in `internal/tools`, the agent registration (schema, dispatch, discovery, policies, manual), the audit entry, the desktop core bridge (Go event payload, JavaScript sanitizer, second-open branch, bundle) and the documentation.

How this part was made and verified: every code block below is generated from the files of the Part B scratch worktree (`git diff` against the base commit for edits of tracked files, the file itself for new files). Every expected-FAIL output was captured by taking the implementation out of that worktree (new files removed, edited files restored to the base commit) and running the new test. The old-to-new replacements of the Go and JavaScript files were replayed mechanically on the base commit (10 files, 12 replacements) and gave the worktree files byte for byte. The worktree held Part A's and Part U's final files. The plan text itself was not replayed on a fresh checkout.

### Contract deviations

1. **The tool parameter is `inputs`, not `values` (§7.2).** `ToolCall` owns a top-level field `Values [][]interface{}` (`json:"values"`, the Google Sheets matrix). An array of `{name, value}` objects under that name makes `json.Unmarshal` fail, and `NativeToolCallToToolCall` then marks the call `NativeArgsMalformed` (verified: `json: cannot unmarshal object into toolCallAlias.values.0 of type []interface {}`). The parameter is therefore called `inputs`; `choices` and `eseries` do not clash. The desktop event payload keeps `values` and `choices` (§7.4), because that is a separate JSON document. A test (`TestECalcSchemaIsStrictCompactAndNamedSafely`) forbids the name `values` in the schema, and the decoder accepts the shapes models send instead of the array of pairs: an object of name to value, a JSON text of either, numbers as values.
2. **`open` details (§7.1, §7.4).** Both desktop gates answer `policy_denied` (`desktop_unavailable` when the desktop is off, `desktop_agent_control_disabled` when agent control or the desktop agent tool is off); `retro_games` answers `error` for the first gate. `id` is optional for `open`: without `id`, `inputs` and `choices` it only opens the app (`open_app` with `{"app_id":"ecalc"}`).
3. **The launch sanitizer is stricter than §7.4.** Names and options must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$` and the page `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$` (they start with a letter, like every catalog id) instead of `^[a-z0-9_]{1,32}$`: the contract's pattern admits `__proto__`. `TestCatalogIDsFitTheDesktopBridge` keeps every calculator, variable, choice and option id inside the patterns, so the stricter rule cannot drop a real id.
4. **Query API shape (§7.3).** Besides `Search`, `Describe` and `Calculate` the package exports `SearchAll`, `Overview` (categories with counts), `Check` (validation without solving, used by `open`), `QueryError` with stable `Code…` constants, `AsQueryError`, `NamedValue`, `CalcRequest{Values, Choices []NamedValue; ESeries string}` (ordered pairs, so the order of typing survives), and the result structs with JSON tags. `Search` also matches the category id and its names (as a tag-level match), so a query such as `filters` lists a category; an empty query at the tool answers the category overview.
5. **`calculate` semantics worth knowing.** A bare number is read in the variable's default display unit (`describe` shows it; the SI unit when empty). List values are written without a space before the unit (`4.7kΩ, 10kΩ`) because `ParseList` splits at white space, and `describe`/`calculate` format lists that way. A variable can be named by id or, when unambiguous, by label (`V_in`). Redundant values that differ from the computed one by more than 1 % (relative to the larger of the two) are reported in `contradictions`, the answer stays `status: ok` with a `message`; a quantity with an `error` (range, nonfinite) makes the answer `status: error`, `code: calculation_failed` with the full result. Variables that the selected choice option ignores need no value: when the given values alone do not make a solvable set, their defaults complete it (`defaulted: true`); given values always win. `calculate` for a `finder: combine` calculator adds `combos` (the single nearest value, up to 5 series and 5 parallel pairs of the chosen series).
6. **Registration choices (§7.1).** Discovery category `infrastructure` (where the other desktop-app tools live), terms in `tool_search_terms/infrastructure_b.yaml`, chat icon alias on the `system_metrics` gauge. The A2A restriction needed no handler check: `a2aDesktopWrite` already works per operation and discovery trims the `operation` enum of a peer to `search`, `describe`, `calculate`.
7. **Test file names owned by Part B.** `ui/desktop_ecalc_launch_test.go`, `ui/desktop_ecalc_launch_browser_test.go`, `ui/desktop_ecalc_tool_icon_test.go`, `internal/audit/ecalc_manifest_test.go`, `internal/agent/ecalc_tool_test.go`, `internal/agent/ecalc_policy_test.go`. Part U must not reuse their identifiers (`ecalcLaunch…`).
8. **`npm run build:ui` rebuilds two bundles** in this part: `main.bundle.js` (desktop core, task B6) and `chat-runtime.bundle.js` (the tool icon alias, task B8).
9. **No change to `menus-and-routing.js`.** Part U expected the core to fill `ctx.launch` for a new window there; `renderAppContent` already passes the whole window context to `ECalcApp.render`, so `launch.launch` from the `open_app` branch arrives as `ctx.launch` without an edit (task B7 proves it in the real shell).

### What Part B needs from the other parts

- **Part A (engine), before B1:** `Var.Units`, `ChoiceOption.Ignore`, `Calculator.Finder`, `Calculator.Chart` (`X`, `Y`, `To Expr`, `Samples`), the constant `finderCombine`, `Combine`, `Combo`, `ComboSingle`, the `integer` dimension with radix units, and the catalog item `eseries_combiner`. B1's tests use all of them.
- **Part U (UI), only for B7:** `window.ECalcApp.launch(windowId, payload)` (returns true or false) and `ctx.launch` in `render` (contract §2); the launch starts from the calculator's defaults, so values the payload does not name keep them. Tasks B1–B6 and B8 do not need it.

### Execution order

B1 → B2 → B3 → B4 → B5 → B6 → B7 → B8 → B9 (each task ends with a commit except B9). B3 registers the tool, so run it only after B1 and B2; B4 needs B3 (its discovery test uses the registered tool).

### How to run Part B

Run every command from the repository root. Go commands need a short backslash `GOTMPDIR` (for example in PowerShell `$env:GOTMPDIR='C:\tmp\go-build-ecalc-p2-b'`). The browser test needs `AURAGO_RUN_BROWSER_SMOKE=1` and, on this box, a shell started without the sandbox (Chrome cannot start from a sandboxed agent shell). Code blocks contain the literal characters `Ω` (U+03A9), `×`, `…`, `°` and `µ`; paste them as they are, never as backslash-u escapes that your editor tool might decode. `ui/js/desktop/core/window-shell-runtime.js` has CRLF line endings in a Windows working tree (git normalizes them); use an editor that keeps them.

GitNexus (project rule): before editing an existing function run `node .gitnexus/run.cjs impact "<symbol>" --direction upstream --repo .` from the main checkout. The records are in the tasks; where the graph was unavailable they say so and name the grep that confirms the callers.

### Task B1: The query API (`internal/ecalc/query.go`)

**Runs after Part A.** It uses Part A's schema fields and `Combine`. No existing function is modified: the file adds methods and types to the package; `Default`, `Calculator`, `Solve`, `SolvableSets`, `Nearest`, `Combine` and `Units.Parse/ParseList/Format` are only called. GitNexus: not applicable (new symbols).

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/ecalc/query.go`
- Create: `internal/ecalc/query_test.go`

The tests run against the real catalog (the basics calculators and `eseries_combiner`); the extension tests (display units, `ignore`, chart, radix) load two small fixture calculators through `Load` and the test helpers `fixtureFS` and `flow16` that already exist in `catalog_test.go`. Every expected number is worked out by hand in a comment (divider 12 V · 2.2k / 6.9k = 3.826 V; 3.3 V · 10k / 8.7 V = 3793.1 Ω with E24 neighbours 3.6k and 3.9k; the combiner vectors of Part A for 5k). The search tests pin the ranking rules and not the size of the catalog, because Part C adds dozens of calculators: an exact id (also written with spaces) must rank first, names, tags and German terms must be among the first hits, equal ranks keep the catalog order, and a category query must list every calculator of the category; no test pins a total number of matches.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

Create `internal/ecalc/query_test.go`:

```go
package ecalc

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"regexp"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func queryCatalog(t *testing.T) *Catalog {
	t.Helper()
	cat, err := Default()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("default catalog: %v", err)
	}
	return cat
}

func hitIDs(hits []SearchHit) []string {
	ids := make([]string, len(hits))
	for i, h := range hits {
		ids[i] = h.ID
	}
	return ids
}

func nv(pairs ...string) []NamedValue {
	var out []NamedValue
	for i := 0; i+1 < len(pairs); i += 2 {
		out = append(out, NamedValue{Name: pairs[i], Value: pairs[i+1]})
	}
	return out
}

func quantity(t *testing.T, res CalcResult, id string) Quantity {
	t.Helper()
	for _, q := range res.Quantities {
		if q.ID == id {
			return q
		}
	}
	t.Fatalf("result has no quantity %q", id)
	return Quantity{}
}

func wantQueryError(t *testing.T, err error, code string, contains ...string) *QueryError {
	t.Helper()
	qe := AsQueryError(err)
	if qe == nil {
		t.Fatalf("error = %v, want a QueryError with code %s", err, code)
	}
	if qe.Code != code {
		t.Fatalf("code = %s (%s), want %s", qe.Code, qe.Message, code)
	}
	for _, want := range contains {
		if !strings.Contains(qe.Message, want) {
			t.Fatalf("message %q lacks %q", qe.Message, want)
		}
	}
	return qe
}

// ---- search ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// The search tests pin the ranking rules, not the size of the catalog: calculators come and go, so a query is only
// expected to find "its" calculator first when the id matches exactly and among the first few otherwise.
func TestSearchRanksExactIDBeforeNamesTagsAndSubstrings(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryCatalog(t)
	// An exact id (also written with spaces) beats every other kind of match.
	for query, want := range map[string]string{
		"voltage_divider": "voltage_divider", // exact id
		"voltage divider": "voltage_divider", // the id with spaces
		"wheatstone":      "wheatstone",      // exact one-word id
		"star delta":      "star_delta",      // the id of two words
	} {
		hits := cat.Search(query, 5)
		if len(hits) == 0 || hits[0].ID != want {
			t.Errorf("Search(%q) = %v, want %s first", query, hitIDs(hits), want)
		}
	}
	// Names (prefix, word), tags and the German names are matched too: the calculator is among the first hits.
	for query, want := range map[string]string{
		"ohm":              "ohms_law",        // name prefix
		"spannungsteiler":  "voltage_divider", // German name
		"messbrücke":       "wheatstone",      // German tag
		"ersatzwiderstand": "series_parallel", // German tag
	} {
		hits := cat.Search(query, 5)
		found := false
		for _, h := range hits[:min(3, len(hits))] {
			found = found || h.ID == want
		}
		if !found {
			t.Errorf("Search(%q) = %v, want %s among the first three", query, hitIDs(hits), want)
		}
	}
	// The case of the query does not matter.
	if got, want := hitIDs(cat.SearchAll("OHM")), hitIDs(cat.SearchAll("ohm")); strings.Join(got, ",") != strings.Join(want, ",") {
		t.Errorf("SearchAll(OHM) = %v, SearchAll(ohm) = %v", got, want)
	}
}

func TestSearchOrdersEqualRanksByCatalogPosition(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryCatalog(t)
	// All three have "divider" as a word of their name; equal ranks keep the order of the catalog.
	position := map[string]int{}
	for i, h := range cat.SearchAll("divider") {
		position[h.ID] = i
	}
	order := []string{"voltage_divider", "loaded_divider", "current_divider"}
	for i, id := range order {
		if _, ok := position[id]; !ok {
			t.Fatalf("SearchAll(divider) does not list %s", id)
		}
		if i > 0 && position[order[i-1]] > position[id] {
			t.Errorf("%s ranks after %s although it comes first in the catalog (positions %v)", order[i-1], id, position)
		}
	}
	all := cat.SearchAll("")
	if len(all) != len(cat.Calculators) || all[0].ID != cat.Calculators[0].ID || all[1].ID != cat.Calculators[1].ID {
		t.Fatalf("an empty query must list the catalog in order, got %v", hitIDs(all))
	}
}

func TestSearchMatchesNamesOfEveryLocale(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryCatalog(t)
	vd := cat.Calculator("voltage_divider")
	for _, lang := range Locales {
		name := vd.Name[lang]
		hits := cat.Search(name, 5)
		found := false
		for _, h := range hits {
			found = found || h.ID == "voltage_divider"
		}
		if !found {
			t.Errorf("Search(%q) in %s = %v, want voltage_divider among the first five", name, lang, hitIDs(hits))
		}
	}
}

func TestSearchLimitsAndEmptyResults(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryCatalog(t)
	if hits := cat.Search("", 3); len(hits) != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("limit 3 gave %d hits", len(hits))
	}
	if hits := cat.Search("", 0); len(hits) != min(DefaultSearchLimit, len(cat.Calculators)) {
		t.Fatalf("limit 0 gave %d hits, want the default %d", len(hits), DefaultSearchLimit)
	}
	if hits := cat.Search("", 500); len(hits) != min(MaxSearchLimit, len(cat.Calculators)) {
		t.Fatalf("limit 500 gave %d hits, want at most %d", len(hits), MaxSearchLimit)
	}
	none := cat.Search("zzzz no such thing", 5)
	if none == nil || len(none) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("no match must be an empty, non-nil list, got %#v", none)
	}
	data, _ := json.Marshal(none)
	if string(data) != "[]" {
		t.Fatalf("no match encodes as %s", data)
	}
}

func TestSearchAnswersWithEnglishNameAndFirstSentence(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryCatalog(t)
	hit := cat.Search("ohms_law", 1)[0]
	if hit.Kind != "calculator" || hit.Category != "basics" || hit.Name != "Ohm's law and power" {
		t.Fatalf("hit = %+v", hit)
	}
	want := "Ohm's law relates voltage, current and resistance (U = R × I); the electrical power is P = U × I."
	if hit.Summary != want {
		t.Fatalf("summary = %q, want %q", hit.Summary, want)
	}
	for _, calc := range cat.Calculators {
		for _, h := range cat.SearchAll(calc.ID)[:1] {
			if h.ID != calc.ID {
				t.Errorf("searching the id %q finds %s first", calc.ID, h.ID)
			}
			if strings.TrimSpace(h.Summary) == "" || strings.Contains(h.Summary, "\n") {
				t.Errorf("%s has summary %q", calc.ID, h.Summary)
			}
		}
	}
}

func TestSearchMatchesTheCategory(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryCatalog(t)
	// The category id is matched like a tag: every calculator of the category is a hit (another calculator that merely
	// mentions the word may be one too, so the count is not pinned).
	listed := map[string]bool{}
	for _, h := range cat.SearchAll("basics") {
		listed[h.ID] = true
	}
	n := 0
	for _, calc := range cat.Calculators {
		if calc.Category == "basics" {
			n++
			if !listed[calc.ID] {
				t.Errorf("Search(basics) does not list the basics calculator %s", calc.ID)
			}
		}
	}
	overview := cat.Overview()
	if len(overview) != len(cat.Categories) || overview[0].ID != "basics" || overview[0].Name != "Basics" || overview[0].Count != n {
		t.Fatalf("overview = %+v", overview)
	}
}

func TestFirstSentenceSkipsAbbreviationsAndCuts(t *testing.T) {
	cases := map[string]string{
		"One. Two.":                        "One.",
		"Use e.g. 4k7 here. More.":         "Use e.g. 4k7 here.",
		"No period at all":                 "No period at all",
		"  Spaces\n\tand lines  collapse.": "Spaces and lines collapse.",
		"Value is 1.5 V. Next":             "Value is 1.5 V.",
	}
	for in, want := range cases {
		if got := firstSentence(in); got != want {
			t.Errorf("firstSentence(%q) = %q, want %q", in, got, want)
		}
	}
	long := firstSentence(strings.Repeat("word ", 100))
	if n := len([]rune(long)); n != summaryRunes || !strings.HasSuffix(long, "…") {
		t.Fatalf("a long sentence is cut to %d runes with an ellipsis, got %d: %q", summaryRunes, n, long)
	}
}

func TestDescribeVoltageDivider(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryCatalog(t)
	d, err := cat.Describe("voltage_divider")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if d.ID != "voltage_divider" || d.Kind != "calculator" || d.Category != "basics" || d.Name != "Voltage divider" || d.DOF != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("description = %+v", d)
	}
	byID := map[string]VarInfo{}
	for _, v := range d.Vars {
		byID[v.ID] = v
	}
	if len(d.Vars) != 4 || d.Vars[0].ID != "vin" || d.Vars[3].ID != "vout" {
		t.Fatalf("vars = %+v", d.Vars)
	}
	if v := byID["vin"]; v.Default != "12 V" || v.Unit != "V" || !v.Input || v.Dim != "voltage" || v.Label != "V_in" || v.Name != "Input voltage" {
		t.Fatalf("vin = %+v", v)
	}
	if v := byID["r1"]; v.Default != "4.7 kΩ" || !v.ESeries || v.Unit != "Ω" {
		t.Fatalf("r1 = %+v", v)
	}
	if v := byID["vout"]; v.Default != "" {
		t.Fatalf("vout has default %q", v.Default)
	}
	if len(d.Sets) != 4 || strings.Join(d.Sets[0], ",") != "vin,r1,r2" {
		t.Fatalf("sets = %v", d.Sets)
	}
	if len(d.Derived) != 2 || d.Derived[0].ID != "i" || d.Derived[0].Dim != "current" || d.Derived[1].ID != "p" {
		t.Fatalf("derived = %+v", d.Derived)
	}
	if len(d.Checks) != 1 || !strings.HasPrefix(d.Checks[0], "V_out is not below V_in") {
		t.Fatalf("checks = %v", d.Checks)
	}
	if len(d.Formula) != 1 || d.Formula[0] != "vout = vin * r2 / (r1 + r2)" || !strings.HasPrefix(d.Doc, "Two resistors in series") || d.Source == "" {
		t.Fatalf("formula/doc/source = %v / %q / %q", d.Formula, d.Doc, d.Source)
	}
}

func TestCalculateVoltageDividerForward(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryCatalog(t)
	res, err := cat.Calculate("voltage_divider", CalcRequest{Values: nv("vin", "12 V", "r1", "4k7", "r2", "2k2")})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if res.ID != "voltage_divider" || res.Name != "Voltage divider" || strings.Join(res.Basis, ",") != "vin,r1,r2" || res.ESeries != "E24" {
		t.Fatalf("result header = %+v", res)
	}
	if len(res.Contradictions) != 0 || len(res.Warnings) != 0 || res.HasErrors() {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected contradictions/warnings/errors: %+v", res)
	}
	vout := quantity(t, res, "vout")
	// 12 V * 2200 / (4700 + 2200) = 3.8260869...
	if !vout.Computed || vout.Formatted != "3.826 V" || vout.SI == nil || !near(*vout.SI, 3.826086956521739, 1e-12) || vout.Kind != "var" {
		t.Fatalf("vout = %+v", vout)
	}
	if q := quantity(t, res, "r1"); q.Computed || q.Given != "4k7" || q.Formatted != "4.7 kΩ" || q.ESeries != nil {
		t.Fatalf("r1 = %+v", q)
	}
	// i = 12 / 6900 = 1.7391 mA and p = 12 * i = 20.87 mW are derived.
	if i := quantity(t, res, "i"); i.Kind != "derived" || i.Formatted != "1.739 mA" {
		t.Fatalf("i = %+v", i)
	}
	if p := quantity(t, res, "p"); p.Formatted != "20.87 mW" {
		t.Fatalf("p = %+v", p)
	}
}

func TestCalculateSolvesBackwardsWithESeriesSuggestion(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryCatalog(t)
	req := CalcRequest{Values: nv("vout", "3.3 V", "vin", "12 V", "r1", "10k")}
	res, err := cat.Calculate("voltage_divider", req)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// r2 = vout * r1 / (vin - vout) = 3.3 * 10000 / 8.7 = 3793.1 ohm; E24 has 3.6k (-5.1 %) and 3.9k (+2.8 %).
	r2 := quantity(t, res, "r2")
	if !r2.Computed || r2.Formatted != "3.793 kΩ" {
		t.Fatalf("r2 = %+v", r2)
	}
	if h := r2.ESeries; h == nil || h.Series != "E24" || h.Value != 3900 || h.Formatted != "3.9 kΩ" || h.DevPct != 2.82 {
		t.Fatalf("E24 suggestion = %+v", h)
	}
	if strings.Join(res.Basis, ",") != "vin,r1,vout" {
		t.Fatalf("basis = %v", res.Basis)
	}
	// E96 has 3.74k (-1.40 %) and 3.83k (+0.97 %).
	req.ESeries = "e96"
	res, err = cat.Calculate("voltage_divider", req)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if h := quantity(t, res, "r2").ESeries; h == nil || h.Series != "E96" || h.Value != 3830 || h.DevPct != 0.973 || res.ESeries != "E96" {
		t.Fatalf("E96 suggestion = %+v", h)
	}
	if res.Warnings != nil {
		t.Fatalf("warnings = %v", res.Warnings)
	}
}

func TestCalculateReportsContradictionsAboveOnePercent(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryCatalog(t)
	// The first solvable set inside {u, i, r} is {u, i}: r = 10 V / 1 A = 10 ohm.
	res, err := cat.Calculate("ohms_law", CalcRequest{Values: nv("u", "10 V", "i", "1 A", "r", "5")})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if strings.Join(res.Basis, ",") != "u,i" || len(res.Contradictions) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("basis %v, contradictions %+v", res.Basis, res.Contradictions)
	}
	c := res.Contradictions[0]
	if c.Name != "r" || c.Given != "5 Ω" || c.Computed != "10 Ω" || c.GivenSI != 5 || c.ComputedSI != 10 || c.DiffPct != 50 {
		t.Fatalf("contradiction = %+v", c)
	}
	if r := quantity(t, res, "r"); !r.Computed || r.Given != "5" || r.Formatted != "10 Ω" {
		t.Fatalf("the quantity shows the computed value and remembers the given one: %+v", r)
	}
	// 10.1 differs by 0.99 % (below the tolerance), 10.2 by 1.96 %.
	res, _ = cat.Calculate("ohms_law", CalcRequest{Values: nv("u", "10 V", "i", "1 A", "r", "10.1")})
	if len(res.Contradictions) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("0.99 %% is within the tolerance: %+v", res.Contradictions)
	}
	res, _ = cat.Calculate("ohms_law", CalcRequest{Values: nv("u", "10 V", "i", "1 A", "r", "10.2")})
	if len(res.Contradictions) != 1 || res.Contradictions[0].DiffPct != 1.96 {
		t.Fatalf("1.96 %% must be reported: %+v", res.Contradictions)
	}
}

func TestCalculateUnderDeterminedListsTheSolvableSets(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryCatalog(t)
	_, err := cat.Calculate("voltage_divider", CalcRequest{Values: nv("vin", "12 V")})
	qe := wantQueryError(t, err, CodeUnderdetermined, "needs 3 values, got 1", "given: vin", "vin + r1 + r2 (add r1, r2)")
	if len(qe.Sets) != 4 || strings.Join(qe.Sets[0], ",") != "vin,r1,r2" {
		t.Fatalf("sets = %v", qe.Sets)
	}
	_, err = cat.Calculate("voltage_divider", CalcRequest{})
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeUnderdetermined, "needs 3 values, got 0")

	// Enough values, but not a solvable combination: the star needs ra, rb and rc, the delta rab, rbc and rca.
	_, err = cat.Calculate("star_delta", CalcRequest{Values: nv("rab", "10", "rbc", "20", "ra", "5")})
	qe = wantQueryError(t, err, CodeUnderdetermined, "no combination", "rab + rbc + rca (add rca)", "ra + rb + rc (add rb, rc)")
	if strings.Join(qe.Sets[0], ",") != "rab,rbc,rca" {
		t.Fatalf("the set that misses the fewest values comes first: %v", qe.Sets)
	}
}

func TestCalculateRejectsBadNames(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryCatalog(t)
	_, err := cat.Calculate("voltage_divider", CalcRequest{Values: nv("foo", "1")})

	_, err = cat.Calculate("voltage_divider", CalcRequest{Values: nv("i", "1 mA")})
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeNotAnInput, "computed output")
	_, err = cat.Calculate("nope", CalcRequest{})
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeUnknownID, `"nope"`)
	_, err = cat.Calculate("voltage_divider", CalcRequest{Choices: nv("wave", "sine")})
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeUnknownChoice, "has no choices")
	_, err = cat.Calculate("rms_waveform", CalcRequest{Values: nv("vrms", "1"), Choices: nv("shape", "sine")})
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeUnknownChoice, `"shape"`, "wave")
	_, err = cat.Calculate("rms_waveform", CalcRequest{Values: nv("vrms", "1"), Choices: nv("wave", "sawtooth")})
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeUnknownOption, `"sawtooth"`, "sine, square, triangle")
	_, err = cat.Calculate("voltage_divider", CalcRequest{Values: nv("vin", "1", "VIN", "2")})
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeDuplicate, "vin")
	_, err = cat.Calculate("rms_waveform", CalcRequest{Values: nv("vrms", "1"), Choices: nv("wave", "sine", "Waveform", "square")})
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeDuplicate, "wave")
	_, err = cat.Calculate("voltage_divider", CalcRequest{Values: nv("vin", "1"), ESeries: "E7"})
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeUnknownESeries, `"E7"`, "E3, E6, E12, E24, E48, E96, E192")
}

func TestResultsEncodeAsJSONWithoutNaN(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryCatalog(t)
	// vin == vout divides by zero in the rule of r2 (infinite, not finite); the result must still encode.
	res, err := cat.Calculate("voltage_divider", CalcRequest{Values: nv("vin", "12 V", "vout", "12 V", "r1", "1k")})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	data, err := json.Marshal(res)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("encode: %v", err)
	}
	if strings.Contains(string(data), "NaN") || strings.Contains(string(data), "Inf") {
		t.Fatalf("non-finite value in %s", data)
	}
	for _, calc := range cat.Calculators {
		d, err := cat.Describe(calc.ID)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if _, err := json.Marshal(d); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s: %v", calc.ID, err)
		}
	}
}

// Every calculator solves from the (twelve-digit) text of its own defaults, which also proves that the default
// formatting, the unit selection and the parser agree for every unit the catalog uses.
func TestCalculateEveryCalculatorFromItsDefaults(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryCatalog(t)
	for _, calc := range cat.Calculators {
		var values []NamedValue
		for i := range calc.Vars {
			v := &calc.Vars[i]
			switch {
			case v.DefaultList != nil:
				parts := make([]string, len(v.DefaultList))
				for j, x := range v.DefaultList {
					parts[j] = strings.ReplaceAll(cat.Units.Format(x, v.Dim, v.Unit, 12), " ", "")
				}
				values = append(values, NamedValue{Name: v.ID, Value: strings.Join(parts, ", ")})
			case v.Default != nil:
				values = append(values, NamedValue{Name: v.ID, Value: cat.Units.Format(*v.Default, v.Dim, v.Unit, 12)})
			}
		}
		res, err := cat.Calculate(calc.ID, CalcRequest{Values: values})
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: %v (values %v)", calc.ID, err, values)
			continue
		}
		if res.HasErrors() || len(res.Contradictions) != 0 || len(res.Basis) != calc.DOF {
			t.Errorf("%s: result from the defaults has errors or contradictions: %+v", calc.ID, res)
		}
		if _, err := json.Marshal(res); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: %v", calc.ID, err)
		}
	}
}

func TestCheckResolvesNamesWithoutSolving(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryCatalog(t)
	got, err := cat.Check("Voltage_Divider", CalcRequest{Values: nv("V_in", " 12 V ", "r1", "4k7")})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got.ID != "voltage_divider" || len(got.Values) != 2 || got.Values[0] != (NamedValue{Name: "vin", Value: "12 V"}) || got.Values[1] != (NamedValue{Name: "r1", Value: "4k7"}) || got.Choices != nil {
		t.Fatalf("checked = %+v", got)
	}
	got, err = cat.Check("rms_waveform", CalcRequest{Choices: nv("Waveform", "Triangle")})
	if err != nil || len(got.Choices) != 1 || got.Choices[0] != (NamedValue{Name: "wave", Value: "triangle"}) || got.Values != nil {
		t.Fatalf("checked = %+v, %v", got, err)
	}
	if got, err := cat.Check("voltage_divider", CalcRequest{}); err != nil || got.ID != "voltage_divider" {
		t.Fatalf("a bare page id is fine: %+v %v", got, err)
	}
	// more values than the calculator needs, and fewer, are fine: ECalc takes them as typed.
	if _, err := cat.Check("ohms_law", CalcRequest{Values: nv("u", "1", "i", "2", "r", "3", "p", "4")}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	_, err = cat.Check("voltage_divider", CalcRequest{Values: nv("vin", "12 V", "r1", "4x7")})
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeParse, "r1")
	_, err = cat.Check("voltage_divider", CalcRequest{Values: nv("nope", "1")})
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeUnknownVariable)
	_, err = cat.Check("nope", CalcRequest{})
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeUnknownID)
}

// The desktop bridge sanitizes the launch payload with these patterns (sdk-events-bootstrap.js): a longer id would
// be dropped silently, so the catalog must stay inside them.
func TestCatalogIDsFitTheDesktopBridge(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryCatalog(t)
	page := regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$`)
	name := regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$`)
	for _, calc := range cat.Calculators {
		if !page.MatchString(calc.ID) {
			t.Errorf("calculator id %q does not fit the bridge", calc.ID)
		}
		for _, v := range calc.Vars {
			if !name.MatchString(v.ID) {
				t.Errorf("%s: variable id %q does not fit the bridge", calc.ID, v.ID)
			}
		}
		for _, ch := range calc.Choices {
			if !name.MatchString(ch.ID) {
				t.Errorf("%s: choice id %q does not fit the bridge", calc.ID, ch.ID)
			}
			for _, o := range ch.Options {
				if !name.MatchString(o.ID) {
					t.Errorf("%s: option id %q does not fit the bridge", calc.ID, o.ID)
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

// ---- phase 2 extensions: combiner, display units, ignored variables, chart, number systems ---------------------

// ignoreCalc exercises the schema extensions of phase 2: a display-unit whitelist (a is shown in dBV), a choice option
// that ignores b (which has a default), a derived power in dBm and a chart.
var ignoreCalc = strings.ReplaceAll(`- id: t_ign
  kind: calculator
  category: basics
  name: NAME16
  doc: {en: "Doc.", de: "Doku."}
  tags: [test]
  source: "Textbook"
  vars:
    a: {dim: voltage, label: A, name: {en: "A", de: "A"}, default: "10 V", unit: dBV, units: ["", dBV, dBu]}
    b: {dim: resistance, label: B, name: {en: "B", de: "B"}, default: "100"}
    c: {dim: current, label: C, name: {en: "C", de: "C"}}
  choices:
    q:
      name: NAME16
      default: o
      options:
        o: {name: NAME16, consts: {k: 1}, ignore: [b]}
        p: {name: NAME16, consts: {k: 2}}
  dof: 2
  rules:
    c: ["a/b*k"]
    a: ["c*b/k"]
    b: ["a*k/c"]
  derived:
    p: {dim: power, label: P, name: {en: "P", de: "P"}, expr: "a*c", unit: dBm, units: [dBm, ""]}
  chart: {x: a, y: c, to: "10", samples: 21}
  formula: ["c = a / b * k"]

- id: t_num
  kind: calculator
  category: basics
  name: NAME16
  doc: {en: "Doc.", de: "Doku."}
  tags: [test]
  source: "Textbook"
  vars:
    n: {dim: integer, label: N, name: {en: "N", de: "N"}, default: "0xFF", unit: hex}
    m: {dim: integer, label: M, name: {en: "M", de: "M"}, unit: dec}
  dof: 1
  rules:
    m: ["n*2"]
    n: ["m/2"]
  formula: ["m = n * 2"]
`, "NAME16", flow16("T"))

func extensionCatalog(t *testing.T) *Catalog {
	t.Helper()
	cat, err := Load(fixtureFS(t, map[string]string{"t.yaml": ignoreCalc}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Load: %v", err)
	}
	return cat
}

func TestCalculateCombinerListsTheBestCombinations(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryCatalog(t)
	res, err := cat.Calculate("eseries_combiner", CalcRequest{Values: nv("target", "5k"), ESeries: "E24"})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// Hand-checked like the vectors of the combiner: 4.7k is 6 % below 5k and 5.1k is 2 % above; 3k + 2k, 3.9k + 1.1k,
	// 7.5k || 15k and 10k || 10k are exactly 5k.
	if len(res.Combos) != 1+2*comboLimit {
		t.Fatalf("%d combos, want the single and %d of each group: %+v", len(res.Combos), comboLimit, res.Combos)
	}
	want := []ComboInfo{
		{Kind: "single", R1: "5.1 kΩ", Value: "5.1 kΩ", DevPct: 2},
		{Kind: "series", R1: "3 kΩ", R2: "2 kΩ", Value: "5 kΩ", DevPct: 0},
		{Kind: "series", R1: "3.9 kΩ", R2: "1.1 kΩ", Value: "5 kΩ", DevPct: 0},
	}
	for i, w := range want {
		if res.Combos[i] != w {
			t.Errorf("combos[%d] = %+v, want %+v", i, res.Combos[i], w)
		}
	}
	parallel := res.Combos[1+comboLimit]
	if parallel != (ComboInfo{Kind: "parallel", R1: "7.5 kΩ", R2: "15 kΩ", Value: "5 kΩ", DevPct: 0}) {
		t.Fatalf("first parallel combination = %+v", parallel)
	}
	if q := quantity(t, res, "target"); q.Computed || q.Given != "5k" || q.Formatted != "5 kΩ" {
		t.Fatalf("target = %+v", q)
	}
	// E96 has 4.99k, 0.2 % below.
	res, err = cat.Calculate("eseries_combiner", CalcRequest{Values: nv("target", "5k"), ESeries: "E96"})
	if err != nil || res.Combos[0] != (ComboInfo{Kind: "single", R1: "4.99 kΩ", Value: "4.99 kΩ", DevPct: -0.2}) {
		t.Fatalf("E96: %v %+v", err, res.Combos)
	}
	// An invalid target has no combinations, only its error.
	res, err = cat.Calculate("eseries_combiner", CalcRequest{Values: nv("target", "-5")})
	if err != nil || res.Combos != nil || !res.HasErrors() {
		t.Fatalf("a negative target: %v %+v", err, res)
	}
	// Other calculators have none.
	if res, _ := cat.Calculate("ohms_law", CalcRequest{Values: nv("u", "1", "i", "1")}); res.Combos != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ohms_law combos = %+v", res.Combos)
	}
	d, err := cat.Describe("eseries_combiner")
	if err != nil || d.Finder != "combine" || len(d.Formula) != 0 || d.Vars[0].Default != "5 kΩ" || d.Chart != nil {
		t.Fatalf("description = %+v, %v", d, err)
	}
	if encoded, _ := json.Marshal(d); strings.Contains(string(encoded), `"formula"`) || strings.Contains(string(encoded), `"chart"`) {
		t.Fatalf("empty formula and no chart are left out: %s", encoded)
	}
}

func TestDescribeExposesUnitsIgnoreAndChart(t *testing.T) {
	cat := extensionCatalog(t)
	d, err := cat.Describe("t_ign")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	a := d.Vars[0]
	// The whitelist "", dBV, dBu offers the base symbol and the two explicit units; a bare number is read in dBV, the
	// default 10 V = 20 dBV is shown in it.
	if a.Unit != "dBV" || strings.Join(a.Units, ",") != "V,dBV,dBu" || a.Default != "20 dBV" {
		t.Fatalf("a = %+v", a)
	}
	if b := d.Vars[1]; strings.Join(b.Units, ",") != "Ω" || b.Unit != "Ω" {
		t.Fatalf("b = %+v", b)
	}
	opts := d.Choices[0].Options
	if len(opts) != 2 || strings.Join(opts[0].Ignore, ",") != "b" || opts[1].Ignore != nil {
		t.Fatalf("options = %+v", opts)
	}
	if d.Chart == nil || *d.Chart != (ChartInfo{X: "a", Y: "c", To: "10", Samples: 21}) || d.Finder != "" {
		t.Fatalf("chart = %+v finder %q", d.Chart, d.Finder)
	}
	if d.Derived[0].Unit != "dBm" {
		t.Fatalf("derived = %+v", d.Derived)
	}
}

func TestCalculateTakesTheDefaultsOfIgnoredVariables(t *testing.T) {
	cat := extensionCatalog(t)
	// Option o ignores b, which has a default of 100 ohm: a alone is enough. c = a / b * k = 10 V / 100 ohm = 0.1 A.
	res, err := cat.Calculate("t_ign", CalcRequest{Values: nv("a", "10 V")})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	b := quantity(t, res, "b")
	if strings.Join(res.Basis, ",") != "a,b" || !b.Ignored || !b.Defaulted || b.Computed || b.Given != "" || b.Formatted != "100 Ω" {
		t.Fatalf("basis %v, b = %+v", res.Basis, b)
	}
	if c := quantity(t, res, "c"); !c.Computed || c.Formatted != "100 mA" || c.Ignored {
		t.Fatalf("c = %+v", c)
	}
	// The bare number reads in dBV: 20 dBV is 10 V, and p = a * c = 1 W = 30 dBm.
	res, err = cat.Calculate("t_ign", CalcRequest{Values: nv("a", "20")})
	if err != nil || quantity(t, res, "c").Formatted != "100 mA" || quantity(t, res, "p").Formatted != "30 dBm" || quantity(t, res, "a").Formatted != "20 dBV" {
		t.Fatalf("dBV: %v %+v", err, res.Quantities)
	}
	// Two values of the request win over a default: {a, c} is a set, so b is computed (10 V / 0.2 A = 50 ohm) and
	// stays marked as ignored but not as a default.
	res, err = cat.Calculate("t_ign", CalcRequest{Values: nv("a", "10 V", "c", "0.2 A")})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if b := quantity(t, res, "b"); !b.Ignored || b.Defaulted || !b.Computed || b.Formatted != "50 Ω" || strings.Join(res.Basis, ",") != "a,c" || len(res.Contradictions) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("basis %v, b = %+v", res.Basis, b)
	}
	// An ignored variable that is given is used like any other and keeps its mark: c = 10 V / 50 ohm = 0.2 A.
	res, _ = cat.Calculate("t_ign", CalcRequest{Values: nv("a", "10 V", "b", "50")})
	if b := quantity(t, res, "b"); !b.Ignored || b.Defaulted || b.Given != "50" || quantity(t, res, "c").Formatted != "200 mA" {
		t.Fatalf("b = %+v", b)
	}
	// Option p ignores nothing: one value is not enough, as without the extension.
	_, err = cat.Calculate("t_ign", CalcRequest{Values: nv("a", "10 V"), Choices: nv("q", "p")})
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeUnderdetermined, "needs 2 values, got 1")
	// With option p, k = 2: c = a / b * 2 = 10 V / 100 ohm * 2 = 0.2 A.
	res, err = cat.Calculate("t_ign", CalcRequest{Values: nv("a", "10 V", "b", "100"), Choices: nv("q", "p")})
	if err != nil || quantity(t, res, "c").Formatted != "200 mA" || quantity(t, res, "b").Ignored {
		t.Fatalf("option p: %v %+v", err, res.Quantities)
	}
}

func TestCalculateFormatsNumberSystemsWithoutAUnit(t *testing.T) {
	cat := extensionCatalog(t)
	d, _ := cat.Describe("t_num")
	if n := d.Vars[0]; n.Unit != "hex" || n.Default != "0xFF" || strings.Join(n.Units, ",") != "dec,hex,bin,oct" {
		t.Fatalf("n = %+v", n)
	}
	// 0xFF = 255; m = 2 * 255 = 510 is shown in decimal, n in hex; a bare "ff" reads in the unit of the variable.
	for _, text := range []string{"0xFF", "ff", "0xff", "FF"} {
		res, err := cat.Calculate("t_num", CalcRequest{Values: nv("n", text)})
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%q: %v", text, err)
		}
		if n, m := quantity(t, res, "n"), quantity(t, res, "m"); n.Formatted != "0xFF" || m.Formatted != "510" || n.SI == nil || *n.SI != 255 {
			t.Errorf("%q: n = %+v, m = %+v", text, n, m)
		}
	}
	// A value above 2^53 - 1 does not parse; half of an odd number is no whole number, which is a range error.
	_, err := cat.Calculate("t_num", CalcRequest{Values: nv("n", "0x20000000000000")})
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeParse, "n")
	res, err := cat.Calculate("t_num", CalcRequest{Values: nv("m", "255")})
	if err != nil || !res.HasErrors() || !strings.Contains(quantity(t, res, "n").Error, "range") {
		t.Fatalf("255 / 2 is no whole number: %v %+v", err, res.Quantities)
	}
}
```
