```go
package ecalc

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"math"
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"unicode"
)

// The query API behind the agent tool ecalc: Search, Describe, Calculate and Check. Output texts are English; the
// structs carry JSON tags because the tool sends them as they are. Nothing here touches the server, the file system
// or the network.

const (
	// DefaultSearchLimit and MaxSearchLimit bound the number of hits of Search.
	DefaultSearchLimit = 10
	MaxSearchLimit     = 25
	// MaxQueryValues is the largest number of values (and of choices) in one request. The desktop bridge that opens
	// ECalc pre-filled accepts the same number, so a request that passes Check is never cut there.
	MaxQueryValues = 32
	// ContradictionTolerance is the relative difference |given - computed| / max(|given|, |computed|) above which a
	// redundant value contradicts the computed one.
	ContradictionTolerance = 0.01
	// DefaultESeries is the series of the suggestions when the request names none.
	DefaultESeries = "E24"

	querySig     = 4   // significant digits of every formatted value
	summaryRunes = 200 // longest summary of a search hit
)

// Error codes of QueryError.
const (
	CodeUnknownID       = "unknown_id"
	CodeUnknownVariable = "unknown_variable"
	CodeNotAnInput      = "not_an_input"
	CodeUnknownChoice   = "unknown_choice"
	CodeUnknownOption   = "unknown_option"
	CodeUnknownESeries  = "unknown_eseries"
	CodeParse           = "parse_error"
	CodeUnderdetermined = "underdetermined"
	CodeDuplicate       = "duplicate_name"
	CodeTooMany         = "too_many_values"
)

// QueryError is a problem with a request. Message names the valid alternatives; Sets is filled for
// CodeUnderdetermined (the solvable input sets, closest first).
type QueryError struct {
	Code    string
	Message string
	Sets    [][]string
}

func (e *QueryError) Error() string { return e.Message }

func queryErr(code, format string, args ...any) *QueryError {
	return &QueryError{Code: code, Message: fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)}
}

// AsQueryError returns err as a *QueryError, or nil when it is none.
func AsQueryError(err error) *QueryError {
	var qe *QueryError
	if errors.As(err, &qe) {
		return qe
	}
	return nil
}

// ---- search ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// SearchHit is one result of Search.
type SearchHit struct {
	ID       string `json:"id"`
	Kind     string `json:"kind"`
	Category string `json:"category"`
	Name     string `json:"name"`
	Summary  string `json:"summary"`
}

// CategorySummary is one category with the number of its calculators.
type CategorySummary struct {
	ID    string `json:"id"`
	Name  string `json:"name"`
	Count int    `json:"count"`
}

// Overview lists the categories of the catalog (English names) with their calculator counts.
func (c *Catalog) Overview() []CategorySummary {
	out := make([]CategorySummary, 0, len(c.Categories))
	for _, cat := range c.Categories {
		n := 0
		for _, calc := range c.Calculators {
			if calc.Category == cat.ID {
				n++
			}
		}
		out = append(out, CategorySummary{ID: cat.ID, Name: cat.Name.in("en"), Count: n})
	}
	return out
}

// Ranking tiers of a search token, best first.
const (
	tierID         = iota // the id (or the whole query is the id)
	tierNamePrefix        // a name starts with it
	tierNameWord          // a word of a name or of the id starts with it
	tierTag               // a tag or the category starts with it
	tierSubstring         // it occurs anywhere
	tierNone
)

type searchFields struct {
	id        string
	idWords   []string
	names     []string
	nameWords [][]string
	tags      []string
	tagWords  [][]string
	cats      []string
}

func isWordRune(r rune) bool { return unicode.IsLetter(r) || unicode.IsNumber(r) || unicode.IsMark(r) }

func wordsOf(s string) []string {
	return strings.FieldsFunc(strings.ToLower(s), func(r rune) bool { return !isWordRune(r) })
}

func (c *Catalog) searchFieldsOf(calc *Calculator) searchFields {
	f := searchFields{id: strings.ToLower(calc.ID), idWords: wordsOf(calc.ID)}
	for _, lang := range Locales {
		if n := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(calc.Name[lang])); n != "" {
			f.names = append(f.names, n)
			f.nameWords = append(f.nameWords, wordsOf(n))
		}
	}
	for _, tag := range calc.Tags {
		t := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(tag))
		f.tags = append(f.tags, t)
		f.tagWords = append(f.tagWords, wordsOf(t))
	}
	f.cats = append(f.cats, strings.ToLower(calc.Category))
	for _, cat := range c.Categories {
		if cat.ID == calc.Category {
			for _, lang := range Locales {
				if n := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(cat.Name[lang])); n != "" {
					f.cats = append(f.cats, n)
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return f
}

func (f *searchFields) wholeTier(query string) int {
	if query == strings.Join(f.idWords, " ") {
		return tierID
	}
	for _, words := range f.nameWords {
		if strings.HasPrefix(strings.Join(words, " "), query) {
			return tierNamePrefix
		}
	}
	return tierNone
}

func (f *searchFields) tokenTier(tok string) int {
	best := tierNone
	set := func(t int) {
		if t < best {
			best = t
		}
	}
	if tok == f.id {
		set(tierID)
	}
	for i, n := range f.names {
		if strings.HasPrefix(n, tok) {
			set(tierNamePrefix)
		}
		for _, w := range f.nameWords[i] {
			if strings.HasPrefix(w, tok) {
				set(tierNameWord)
			}
		}
		if strings.Contains(n, tok) {
			set(tierSubstring)
		}
	}
	for _, w := range f.idWords {
		if strings.HasPrefix(w, tok) {
			set(tierNameWord)
		}
	}
	if strings.Contains(f.id, tok) {
		set(tierSubstring)
	}
	for i, t := range f.tags {
		if strings.HasPrefix(t, tok) {
			set(tierTag)
		}
		for _, w := range f.tagWords[i] {
			if strings.HasPrefix(w, tok) {
				set(tierTag)
			}
		}
		if strings.Contains(t, tok) {
			set(tierSubstring)
		}
	}
	for _, cat := range f.cats {
		if strings.HasPrefix(cat, tok) {
			set(tierTag)
		}
	}
	return best
}

// SearchAll returns every calculator that matches the query, best match first. The query is split into words that
// must all match (case-insensitively) the id, one of the names in the 16 locales, a tag or the category. A hit ranks by
// its weakest word: exact id, then name prefix, name word, tag or category, substring; equal ranks keep the order of
// the catalog. An empty query matches everything in catalog order.
func (c *Catalog) SearchAll(query string) []SearchHit {
	tokens := wordsOf(query)
	whole := strings.Join(tokens, " ")
	type ranked struct {
		calc     *Calculator
		pri, sum int
		position int
	}
	var hits []ranked
	for i, calc := range c.Calculators {
		if len(tokens) == 0 {
			hits = append(hits, ranked{calc: calc, position: i})
			continue
		}
		f := c.searchFieldsOf(calc)
		pri, sum, ok := 0, 0, true
		for _, tok := range tokens {
			t := f.tokenTier(tok)
			if t == tierNone {
				ok = false
				break
			}
			pri = max(pri, t)
			sum += t
		}
		w := f.wholeTier(whole)
		switch {
		case w < pri:
			pri, sum, ok = w, 0, true
		case !ok:
			continue
		}
		hits = append(hits, ranked{calc: calc, pri: pri, sum: sum, position: i})
	}
	sort.SliceStable(hits, func(a, b int) bool {
		if hits[a].pri != hits[b].pri {
			return hits[a].pri < hits[b].pri
		}
		if hits[a].sum != hits[b].sum {
			return hits[a].sum < hits[b].sum
		}
		return hits[a].position < hits[b].position
	})
	out := make([]SearchHit, 0, len(hits))
	for _, h := range hits {
		out = append(out, SearchHit{
			ID: h.calc.ID, Kind: h.calc.Kind, Category: h.calc.Category,
			Name: h.calc.Name.in("en"), Summary: firstSentence(h.calc.Doc.in("en")),
		})
	}
	return out
}

// Search returns the best limit matches of SearchAll. A limit below 1 means DefaultSearchLimit; the largest is
// MaxSearchLimit.
func (c *Catalog) Search(query string, limit int) []SearchHit {
	if limit < 1 {
		limit = DefaultSearchLimit
	}
	limit = min(limit, MaxSearchLimit)
	all := c.SearchAll(query)
	if len(all) > limit {
		all = all[:limit]
	}
	return all
}

// firstSentence is the text up to the first sentence end (a period followed by a space), cut to summaryRunes.
func firstSentence(doc string) string {
	doc = strings.Join(strings.Fields(doc), " ")
	end := len(doc)
	for i := 0; i+1 < len(doc); i++ {
		if doc[i] != '.' || doc[i+1] != ' ' {
			continue
		}
		before := strings.ToLower(doc[:i])
		abbreviation := false
		for _, ab := range []string{"e.g", "i.e", "approx", "vs", "cf", "etc"} {
			if strings.HasSuffix(before, " "+ab) || before == ab {
				abbreviation = true
			}
		}
		if !abbreviation {
			end = i + 1
			break
		}
	}
	s := doc[:end]
	if r := []rune(s); len(r) > summaryRunes {
		s = strings.TrimSpace(string(r[:summaryRunes-1])) + "…"
	}
	return s
}

// ---- describe -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// VarInfo describes one variable. Unit is the display unit a bare number is read in (empty: the SI unit with an
// automatic prefix); Units are the units a value may carry.
type VarInfo struct {
	ID      string   `json:"id"`
	Label   string   `json:"label"`
	Name    string   `json:"name"`
	Dim     string   `json:"dim"`
	Unit    string   `json:"unit,omitempty"`
	Units   []string `json:"units,omitempty"`
	Input   bool     `json:"input"`
	List    bool     `json:"list,omitempty"`
	ESeries bool     `json:"eseries,omitempty"`
	Default string   `json:"default,omitempty"`
}

// OptionInfo is one option of a choice. Ignore lists the variables the option does not use (a value for them is not
// needed: Calculate takes their defaults).
type OptionInfo struct {
	ID     string   `json:"id"`
	Name   string   `json:"name"`
	Ignore []string `json:"ignore,omitempty"`
}

// ChoiceInfo is a selector with its options.
type ChoiceInfo struct {
	ID      string       `json:"id"`
	Name    string       `json:"name"`
	Default string       `json:"default"`
	Options []OptionInfo `json:"options"`
}

// DerivedInfo is a computed-only quantity.
type DerivedInfo struct {
	ID    string `json:"id"`
	Label string `json:"label"`
	Name  string `json:"name"`
	Dim   string `json:"dim"`
	Unit  string `json:"unit,omitempty"`
}

// ChartInfo is the chart of a calculator: y over x from 0 to To (an expression), drawn with Samples points.
type ChartInfo struct {
	X       string `json:"x"`
	Y       string `json:"y"`
	To      string `json:"to"`
	Samples int    `json:"samples"`
}

// Description is what Describe returns for a calculator. Finder is "combine" for the standard-value combiner, whose
// result lists combinations of E-series values (see Calculate).
type Description struct {
	ID       string        `json:"id"`
	Kind     string        `json:"kind"`
	Category string        `json:"category"`
	Name     string        `json:"name"`
	Doc      string        `json:"doc"`
	Source   string        `json:"source"`
	DOF      int           `json:"dof"`
	Vars     []VarInfo     `json:"vars"`
	Choices  []ChoiceInfo  `json:"choices,omitempty"`
	Derived  []DerivedInfo `json:"derived,omitempty"`
	Sets     [][]string    `json:"sets"`
	Checks   []string      `json:"checks,omitempty"`
	Formula  []string      `json:"formula,omitempty"`
	Finder   string        `json:"finder,omitempty"`
	Chart    *ChartInfo    `json:"chart,omitempty"`
}

// unitSymbol is the symbol of an explicit unit of the dimension, or the base symbol when unitID is "".
func (c *Catalog) unitSymbol(dimID, unitID string) string {
	d := c.Units.Dim(dimID)
	if d == nil {
		return ""
	}
	if un := d.Unit(unitID); un != nil {
		return un.Symbol
	}
	return d.Symbol
}

// unitSymbols lists the units a value of the variable may carry: the units its catalog entry offers ("" is the base
// symbol with automatic prefixes) or, when it names none, the base symbol and every explicit unit of the dimension.
func (c *Catalog) unitSymbols(v *Var) []string {
	d := c.Units.Dim(v.Dim)
	if d == nil {
		return nil
	}
	var out []string
	add := func(symbol string) {
		if symbol != "" {
			out = append(out, symbol)
		}
	}
	if len(v.Units) > 0 {
		for _, id := range v.Units {
			add(c.unitSymbol(v.Dim, id))
		}
		return out
	}
	add(d.Symbol)
	for _, un := range d.Units {
		add(un.Symbol)
	}
	return out
}

func (c *Catalog) formatValue(x float64, dimID, unitID string) string {
	return c.Units.Format(x, dimID, unitID, querySig)
}

// formatList writes a list the way it is typed: items separated by a comma and a space, each item without a space
// before its unit ("4.7kΩ, 10kΩ"), because ParseList splits at white space.
func (c *Catalog) formatList(list []float64, dimID, unitID string) string {
	parts := make([]string, len(list))
	for i, x := range list {
		parts[i] = strings.ReplaceAll(c.formatValue(x, dimID, unitID), " ", "")
	}
	return strings.Join(parts, ", ")
}

// Describe returns the structure of a calculator: variables with units and defaults, choices, the solvable input
// sets, derived quantities, checks and the display formulas.
func (c *Catalog) Describe(id string) (Description, error) {
	calc, err := c.lookup(id)
	if err != nil {
		return Description{}, err
	}
	d := Description{
		ID: calc.ID, Kind: calc.Kind, Category: calc.Category, Name: calc.Name.in("en"), Doc: calc.Doc.in("en"),
		Source: calc.Source, DOF: calc.DOF, Sets: calc.Sets, Formula: calc.Formula,
		Vars: make([]VarInfo, 0, len(calc.Vars)),
	}
	if d.Sets == nil {
		d.Sets = [][]string{}
	}
	for i := range calc.Vars {
		v := &calc.Vars[i]
		info := VarInfo{
			ID: v.ID, Label: v.Label, Name: v.Name.in("en"), Dim: v.Dim, Unit: c.unitSymbol(v.Dim, v.Unit),
			Units: c.unitSymbols(v), Input: v.Input, List: v.List, ESeries: v.ESeries,
		}
		switch {
		case v.DefaultList != nil:
			info.Default = c.formatList(v.DefaultList, v.Dim, v.Unit)
		case v.Default != nil:
			info.Default = c.formatValue(*v.Default, v.Dim, v.Unit)
		}
		d.Vars = append(d.Vars, info)
	}
	for _, ch := range calc.Choices {
		info := ChoiceInfo{ID: ch.ID, Name: ch.Name.in("en"), Default: ch.Default}
		for _, o := range ch.Options {
			info.Options = append(info.Options, OptionInfo{ID: o.ID, Name: o.Name.in("en"), Ignore: o.Ignore})
		}
		d.Choices = append(d.Choices, info)
	}
	for _, dv := range calc.Derived {
		d.Derived = append(d.Derived, DerivedInfo{
			ID: dv.ID, Label: dv.Label, Name: dv.Name.in("en"), Dim: dv.Dim, Unit: c.unitSymbol(dv.Dim, dv.Unit),
		})
	}
	for _, check := range calc.Checks {
		d.Checks = append(d.Checks, check.Warn.in("en"))
	}
	d.Finder = calc.Finder
	if ch := calc.Chart; ch != nil {
		d.Chart = &ChartInfo{X: ch.X, Y: ch.Y, To: ch.To.Src, Samples: ch.Samples}
	}
	return d, nil
}

// lookup finds a calculator by id (case-insensitive). The error of an unknown id suggests the best search hits.
func (c *Catalog) lookup(id string) (*Calculator, error) {
	key := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(id))
	if key == "" {
		return nil, queryErr(CodeUnknownID, "id is required; use search to find a calculator id")
	}
	if calc := c.Calculator(key); calc != nil {
		return calc, nil
	}
	msg := fmt.Sprintf("unknown calculator %q; use search to find a calculator id", id)
	if hits := c.Search(strings.NewReplacer("_", " ", "-", " ").Replace(key), 3); len(hits) > 0 {
		ids := make([]string, len(hits))
		for i, h := range hits {
			ids[i] = h.ID
		}
		msg += "; did you mean " + strings.Join(ids, ", ") + "?"
	}
	return nil, &QueryError{Code: CodeUnknownID, Message: msg}
}

// ---- calculate ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// NamedValue is a name with a text: a variable id with a value as a person would type it ("4k7", "12 V", "25 °C"),
// or a choice id with an option id.
type NamedValue struct {
	Name  string `json:"name"`
	Value string `json:"value"`
}

// CalcRequest is the input of Calculate and Check. Values are read with the dimension of their variable; a bare
// number is in the variable's default display unit (the SI unit when it has none). Choices not given use their
// default. ESeries ("" = DefaultESeries) is the series of the standard-value suggestions.
type CalcRequest struct {
	Values  []NamedValue
	Choices []NamedValue
	ESeries string
}

// Checked is a request whose names were resolved: ids are canonical, texts are as typed (trimmed).
type Checked struct {
	ID      string
	Values  []NamedValue
	Choices []NamedValue
}

// ESeriesHint is the nearest standard value of a computed quantity.
type ESeriesHint struct {
	Series    string  `json:"series"`
	Value     float64 `json:"value"`
	Formatted string  `json:"formatted"`
	DevPct    float64 `json:"dev_pct"`
}

// Quantity is one variable or derived quantity of a result. SI is nil when the value is unknown or not finite. Label,
// Name and Dim are omitted when the tool has to shorten an answer to fit its output budget. Ignored marks a variable
// the selected choice option does not use; Defaulted that its value is the default because none was given.
type Quantity struct {
	ID        string       `json:"id"`
	Label     string       `json:"label,omitempty"`
	Name      string       `json:"name,omitempty"`
	Kind      string       `json:"kind"`
	Dim       string       `json:"dim,omitempty"`
	SI        *float64     `json:"si,omitempty"`
	SIList    []float64    `json:"si_list,omitempty"`
	Formatted string       `json:"formatted"`
	Computed  bool         `json:"computed"`
	Given     string       `json:"given,omitempty"`
	Ignored   bool         `json:"ignored,omitempty"`
	Defaulted bool         `json:"defaulted,omitempty"`
	Error     string       `json:"error,omitempty"`
	ESeries   *ESeriesHint `json:"eseries,omitempty"`
}

// Contradiction is a redundant given value that differs from the computed one by more than ContradictionTolerance.
type Contradiction struct {
	Name       string  `json:"name"`
	Given      string  `json:"given"`
	Computed   string  `json:"computed"`
	GivenSI    float64 `json:"given_si"`
	ComputedSI float64 `json:"computed_si"`
	DiffPct    float64 `json:"diff_pct"`
}

// ChoiceState is the option that was used for a choice.
type ChoiceState struct {
	ID         string `json:"id"`
	Option     string `json:"option"`
	OptionName string `json:"option_name"`
}

// ComboInfo is one combination of the standard-value combiner: the single nearest value (Kind "single", R1 only), two
// values in series or two in parallel. Values are formatted; DevPct is the deviation from the target in percent.
type ComboInfo struct {
	Kind   string  `json:"kind"`
	R1     string  `json:"r1"`
	R2     string  `json:"r2,omitempty"`
	Value  string  `json:"value"`
	DevPct float64 `json:"dev_pct"`
}

// CalcResult is what Calculate returns. Basis are the input variables the result was computed from.
type CalcResult struct {
	ID             string          `json:"id"`
	Name           string          `json:"name"`
	Choices        []ChoiceState   `json:"choices,omitempty"`
	Basis          []string        `json:"basis"`
	Quantities     []Quantity      `json:"quantities"`
	Contradictions []Contradiction `json:"contradictions,omitempty"`
	Warnings       []string        `json:"warnings,omitempty"`
	ESeries        string          `json:"eseries"`
	Combos         []ComboInfo     `json:"combos,omitempty"`
}

// HasErrors reports whether any quantity carries an error (a value out of range, not finite or undetermined).
func (r *CalcResult) HasErrors() bool {
	for _, q := range r.Quantities {
		if q.Error != "" {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

type givenValue struct {
	v      *Var
	text   string
	si     float64
	list   []float64
	filled bool // the default of a variable that the selected option ignores, not a value of the request
}

type resolvedRequest struct {
	calc    *Calculator
	given   []givenValue
	choices []ChoiceState
	checked Checked
	series  string
}

// alnum lowercases s and drops separators, so that "V_in", "v in" and "vin" compare equal.
func alnum(s string) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	for _, r := range strings.ToLower(s) {
		if r != '_' && r != ' ' && r != '-' && r != '{' && r != '}' && r != '$' {
			b.WriteRune(r)
		}
	}
	return b.String()
}

func idsOf[T any](items []T, id func(T) string) string {
	parts := make([]string, len(items))
	for i, it := range items {
		parts[i] = id(it)
	}
	return strings.Join(parts, ", ")
}

// findVar resolves a variable name: the id (case-insensitive) or, when that is unambiguous, the label.
func findVar(calc *Calculator, name string) (*Var, *QueryError) {
	key := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(name))
	if v := calc.Var(key); v != nil {
		return v, nil
	}
	var byLabel []*Var
	for i := range calc.Vars {
		if v := &calc.Vars[i]; alnum(v.ID) == alnum(key) || alnum(v.Label) == alnum(key) {
			byLabel = append(byLabel, v)
		}
	}
	if len(byLabel) == 1 {
		return byLabel[0], nil
	}
	for _, d := range calc.Derived {
		if d.ID == key {
			return nil, queryErr(CodeNotAnInput, "%q of %s is a computed output (%s), not an input; input variables: %s", name, calc.ID, d.Name.in("en"), inputList(calc))
		}
	}
	return nil, queryErr(CodeUnknownVariable, "unknown variable %q for %s; input variables: %s", name, calc.ID, inputList(calc))
}

func inputList(calc *Calculator) string {
	var parts []string
	for _, v := range calc.Vars {
		if v.Input {
			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s)", v.ID, v.Name.in("en")))
		}
	}
	return strings.Join(parts, ", ")
}

func findChoice(calc *Calculator, name string) (*Choice, *QueryError) {
	key := alnum(name)
	for i := range calc.Choices {
		ch := &calc.Choices[i]
		if alnum(ch.ID) == key || alnum(ch.Name.in("en")) == key {
			return ch, nil
		}
	}
	if len(calc.Choices) == 0 {
		return nil, queryErr(CodeUnknownChoice, "%s has no choices, so %q cannot be set", calc.ID, name)
	}
	return nil, queryErr(CodeUnknownChoice, "unknown choice %q for %s; choices: %s", name, calc.ID, idsOf(calc.Choices, func(c Choice) string { return c.ID }))
}

func findOption(calc *Calculator, ch *Choice, name string) (*ChoiceOption, *QueryError) {
	key := alnum(name)
	for i := range ch.Options {
		o := &ch.Options[i]
		if alnum(o.ID) == key || alnum(o.Name.in("en")) == key {
			return o, nil
		}
	}
	return nil, queryErr(CodeUnknownOption, "unknown option %q of choice %s in %s; options: %s", name, ch.ID, calc.ID, idsOf(ch.Options, func(o ChoiceOption) string { return o.ID }))
}

// resolve validates a request: the calculator, every name, the number of values, the E-series and the text of every
// value (it must parse with the dimension of its variable).
func (c *Catalog) resolve(id string, req CalcRequest) (*resolvedRequest, error) {
	calc, err := c.lookup(id)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if len(req.Values) > MaxQueryValues || len(req.Choices) > MaxQueryValues {
		return nil, queryErr(CodeTooMany, "at most %d values and %d choices per request", MaxQueryValues, MaxQueryValues)
	}
	rr := &resolvedRequest{calc: calc, checked: Checked{ID: calc.ID}, series: DefaultESeries}
	if s := strings.ToUpper(strings.TrimSpace(req.ESeries)); s != "" {
		rr.series = s
	}
	if _, ok := ESeriesValues(rr.series); !ok {
		return nil, queryErr(CodeUnknownESeries, "unknown E-series %q; use one of %s", req.ESeries, strings.Join(ESeriesIDs, ", "))
	}

	chosen := map[string]string{}
	for _, nv := range req.Choices {
		ch, qe := findChoice(calc, nv.Name)
		if qe != nil {
			return nil, qe
		}
		if _, dup := chosen[ch.ID]; dup {
			return nil, queryErr(CodeDuplicate, "choice %s is given twice", ch.ID)
		}
		opt, qe := findOption(calc, ch, nv.Value)
		if qe != nil {
			return nil, qe
		}
		chosen[ch.ID] = opt.ID
		rr.checked.Choices = append(rr.checked.Choices, NamedValue{Name: ch.ID, Value: opt.ID})
	}
	for i := range calc.Choices {
		ch := &calc.Choices[i]
		opt := ch.option(chosen[ch.ID])
		rr.choices = append(rr.choices, ChoiceState{ID: ch.ID, Option: opt.ID, OptionName: opt.Name.in("en")})
	}

	seen := map[string]bool{}
	for _, nv := range req.Values {
		v, qe := findVar(calc, nv.Name)
		if qe != nil {
			return nil, qe
		}
		if !v.Input {
			return nil, queryErr(CodeNotAnInput, "%q of %s is only ever computed; input variables: %s", nv.Name, calc.ID, inputList(calc))
		}
		if seen[v.ID] {
			return nil, queryErr(CodeDuplicate, "variable %s is given twice", v.ID)
		}
		seen[v.ID] = true
		text := strings.TrimSpace(nv.Value)
		g := givenValue{v: v, text: text}
		var perr error
		if v.List {
			g.list, perr = c.Units.ParseList(text, v.Dim, v.Unit)
		} else {
			g.si, perr = c.Units.Parse(text, v.Dim, v.Unit)
		}
		if perr != nil {
			shape := v.Dim
			if v.List {
				shape = "list of " + v.Dim + " values such as 4k7, 10k, 2k2"
			}
			return nil, queryErr(CodeParse, "cannot read %q for %s as a %s: %v", text, v.ID, shape, perr)
		}
		rr.given = append(rr.given, g)
		rr.checked.Values = append(rr.checked.Values, NamedValue{Name: v.ID, Value: text})
	}
	return rr, nil
}

// Check validates a request exactly like Calculate does for names, units and the E-series, without solving. It is
// what opening ECalc pre-filled uses: the values are sent as typed, so a request with fewer or more values than the
// calculator needs is fine.
func (c *Catalog) Check(id string, req CalcRequest) (Checked, error) {
	rr, err := c.resolve(id, req)
	if err != nil {
		return Checked{}, err
	}
	return rr.checked, nil
}

// firstSetWithin is the first solvable input set (catalog order) whose variables are all in names, or nil.
func firstSetWithin(calc *Calculator, names map[string]bool) []string {
	for _, set := range calc.Sets {
		inside := true
		for _, id := range set {
			if !names[id] {
				inside = false
				break
			}
		}
		if inside {
			return set
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// underdetermined builds the error of a request whose values contain no solvable input set. The sets are listed
// closest first (fewest missing values), so the message says what to add.
func underdetermined(calc *Calculator, given []givenValue, names map[string]bool) *QueryError {
	type scored struct {
		set     []string
		missing []string
	}
	var all []scored
	for _, set := range calc.Sets {
		s := scored{set: set}
		for _, id := range set {
			if !names[id] {
				s.missing = append(s.missing, id)
			}
		}
		all = append(all, s)
	}
	sort.SliceStable(all, func(a, b int) bool { return len(all[a].missing) < len(all[b].missing) })
	have := make([]string, len(given))
	for i, g := range given {
		have[i] = g.v.ID
	}
	var b strings.Builder
	if len(given) < calc.DOF {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "under-determined: %s needs %d values, got %d", calc.ID, calc.DOF, len(given))
	} else {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "the values do not determine %s: no combination of the values is a solvable input set", calc.ID)
	}
	if len(have) > 0 {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, " (given: %s)", strings.Join(have, ", "))
	}
	b.WriteString("; solvable input sets, closest first: ")
	qe := &QueryError{Code: CodeUnderdetermined}
	for i, s := range all {
		if i == 6 {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "; and %d more (see describe)", len(all)-i)
			break
		}
		if i > 0 {
			b.WriteString("; ")
		}
		b.WriteString(strings.Join(s.set, " + "))
		if len(s.missing) > 0 && len(s.missing) < len(s.set) {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, " (add %s)", strings.Join(s.missing, ", "))
		}
		qe.Sets = append(qe.Sets, s.set)
	}
	qe.Message = b.String()
	return qe
}

func finitePtr(x float64) *float64 {
	if math.IsNaN(x) || math.IsInf(x, 0) {
		return nil
	}
	return &x
}

func errorText(code string) string {
	switch code {
	case ErrUndetermined:
		return "undetermined: the given values do not fix this quantity"
	case ErrNonFinite:
		return "nonfinite: the result is not a finite number (division by zero or overflow)"
	case ErrRange:
		return "range: the value must be greater than zero"
	}
	return code
}

// Calculate solves a calculator from the values of the request. It uses the first solvable input set (catalog order)
// whose variables are all given; every other given value is compared with the computed one and listed as a
// contradiction when it differs by more than ContradictionTolerance. The error of a request that cannot be solved
// is a *QueryError.
func (c *Catalog) Calculate(id string, req CalcRequest) (CalcResult, error) {
	rr, err := c.resolve(id, req)
	if err != nil {
		return CalcResult{}, err
	}
	calc := rr.calc
	names := map[string]bool{}
	for _, g := range rr.given {
		names[g.v.ID] = true
	}
	ignored := map[string]bool{}
	filled := ignoredDefaults(calc, rr.choices, names, ignored)
	basis := firstSetWithin(calc, names)
	if basis == nil && len(filled) > 0 {
		// The values of the request are not enough, but a variable the selected option ignores may still complete a
		// set with its default.
		for _, g := range filled {
			names[g.v.ID] = true
		}
		basis = firstSetWithin(calc, names)
	}
	if basis == nil {
		return CalcResult{}, underdetermined(calc, rr.given, names)
	}
	inBasis := map[string]bool{}
	for _, id := range basis {
		inBasis[id] = true
	}

	in := Inputs{Values: map[string]float64{}, Lists: map[string][]float64{}, Choices: map[string]string{}}
	for _, ch := range rr.choices {
		in.Choices[ch.ID] = ch.Option
	}
	givenByID := map[string]givenValue{}
	for _, g := range append(append([]givenValue{}, rr.given...), filled...) {
		givenByID[g.v.ID] = g
		if !inBasis[g.v.ID] {
			continue
		}
		if g.v.List {
			in.Lists[g.v.ID] = g.list
		} else {
			in.Values[g.v.ID] = g.si
		}
	}
	res := calc.Solve(in)
	computed := map[string]bool{}
	for _, id := range res.Computed {
		computed[id] = true
	}

	out := CalcResult{ID: calc.ID, Name: calc.Name.in("en"), Choices: rr.choices, Basis: append([]string{}, basis...), ESeries: rr.series}
	for i := range calc.Vars {
		v := &calc.Vars[i]
		q := Quantity{ID: v.ID, Label: v.Label, Name: v.Name.in("en"), Kind: "var", Dim: v.Dim, Computed: computed[v.ID]}
		if g, ok := givenByID[v.ID]; ok {
			q.Given, q.Defaulted = g.text, g.filled && inBasis[v.ID]
		}
		q.Ignored = ignored[v.ID]
		if v.List {
			q.SIList = in.Lists[v.ID]
			q.Formatted = c.formatList(q.SIList, v.Dim, v.Unit)
		} else {
			x := res.Values[v.ID]
			q.SI = finitePtr(x)
			q.Formatted = c.formatValue(x, v.Dim, v.Unit)
			if q.Computed && v.ESeries && q.SI != nil && *q.SI > 0 {
				if val, dev, err := Nearest(rr.series, *q.SI); err == nil {
					q.ESeries = &ESeriesHint{Series: rr.series, Value: val, Formatted: c.formatValue(val, v.Dim, v.Unit), DevPct: roundSig(dev, 3)}
				}
			}
			// A redundant given value is compared with the computed one.
			if g, ok := givenByID[v.ID]; ok && !g.filled && !inBasis[v.ID] && q.SI != nil {
				diff := math.Abs(g.si-x) / math.Max(math.Abs(g.si), math.Abs(x))
				if diff > ContradictionTolerance {
					out.Contradictions = append(out.Contradictions, Contradiction{
						Name: v.ID, Given: c.formatValue(g.si, v.Dim, v.Unit), Computed: q.Formatted,
						GivenSI: g.si, ComputedSI: x, DiffPct: roundSig(diff*100, 3),
					})
				}
			}
		}
		if code := res.Errors[v.ID]; code != "" {
			q.Error = errorText(code)
		}
		out.Quantities = append(out.Quantities, q)
	}
	for _, d := range calc.Derived {
		x := res.Values[d.ID]
		q := Quantity{ID: d.ID, Label: d.Label, Name: d.Name.in("en"), Kind: "derived", Dim: d.Dim, Computed: true}
		q.SI = finitePtr(x)
		q.Formatted = c.formatValue(x, d.Dim, d.Unit)
		out.Quantities = append(out.Quantities, q)
	}
	for _, i := range res.Warnings {
		out.Warnings = append(out.Warnings, calc.Checks[i].Warn.in("en"))
	}
	if calc.Finder == finderCombine {
		out.Combos = c.combos(calc, res, rr.series)
	}
	return out, nil
}

// ignoredDefaults marks the variables that the selected choice options ignore in ignored and returns the defaults of
// those the request does not give, so that a value for a variable an option does not use is not asked for. They are
// only used when the given values alone do not make a solvable set. A variable without a default is not filled in.
func ignoredDefaults(calc *Calculator, choices []ChoiceState, names, ignored map[string]bool) []givenValue {
	var out []givenValue
	for _, st := range choices {
		for i := range calc.Choices {
			ch := &calc.Choices[i]
			if ch.ID != st.ID {
				continue
			}
			for _, id := range ch.option(st.Option).Ignore {
				ignored[id] = true
				v := calc.Var(id)
				if v == nil || !v.Input || names[id] {
					continue
				}
				switch {
				case v.DefaultList != nil:
					out = append(out, givenValue{v: v, list: v.DefaultList, filled: true})
				case v.Default != nil:
					out = append(out, givenValue{v: v, si: *v.Default, filled: true})
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return out
}

// comboLimit is the number of series and of parallel combinations the combiner lists, like the app.
const comboLimit = 5

// combos lists the nearest single value and the best series and parallel pairs of the series for the target of a
// standard-value combiner (its one resistance variable). A target that is not a valid resistance has none.
func (c *Catalog) combos(calc *Calculator, res Result, series string) []ComboInfo {
	var target *Var
	for i := range calc.Vars {
		if v := &calc.Vars[i]; v.Dim == "resistance" && !v.List {
			target = v
			break
		}
	}
	if target == nil {
		return nil
	}
	list, err := Combine(series, res.Values[target.ID], comboLimit)
	if err != nil {
		return nil
	}
	out := make([]ComboInfo, len(list))
	for i, cb := range list {
		info := ComboInfo{Kind: cb.Kind, R1: c.formatValue(cb.R1, target.Dim, target.Unit), Value: c.formatValue(cb.Value, target.Dim, target.Unit), DevPct: roundSig(cb.DevPct, 3)}
		if cb.Kind != ComboSingle {
			info.R2 = c.formatValue(cb.R2, target.Dim, target.Unit)
		}
		out[i] = info
	}
	return out
}
```

### Task B2: The tool implementation (`internal/tools/ecalc.go`)

**Runs after B1.** No existing function is modified. The implementation follows `retro_games` (`VirtualDesktopExecution{Output, Event}`, `virtualDesktopEvent`) and `local_wikipedia` (answers sized to an `OutputBudget`). `open` sends the values as an ordered JSON object (`ecalcOrdered`): the app reads their order as the order of typing, and a Go `map` would sort the keys. The search tests do not pin totals that grow with the catalog (the first hit, `returned <= limit`, and `truncated` meaning "more matches than listed" are pinned); a hit is only dropped for size when the answer would exceed the budget, which these small result sets never do.

```go
package tools

	"aurago/internal/ecalc"

func ecalcDesktopConfig() *config.Config {
	cfg := &config.Config{}
	cfg.VirtualDesktop.Enabled = true
	cfg.VirtualDesktop.AllowAgentControl = true
	cfg.Tools.VirtualDesktop.Enabled = true
	return cfg
}

func ecalcPairs(pairs ...string) []ecalc.NamedValue {
	var out []ecalc.NamedValue
	for i := 0; i+1 < len(pairs); i += 2 {
		out = append(out, ecalc.NamedValue{Name: pairs[i], Value: pairs[i+1]})
	}
	return out
}

// ecalcDecode decodes the JSON output of the tool into a generic map.
func ecalcDecode(t *testing.T, exec VirtualDesktopExecution) map[string]any {
	t.Helper()
	var out map[string]any
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(exec.Output), &out); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("output is not JSON: %v\n%s", err, exec.Output)
	}
	return out
}

func TestECalcSearchListsRankedResults(t *testing.T) {
	// The catalog grows with its content, so the totals are not pinned: what matters is the order of the top hit, that
	// the answer never lists more than the limit, and what truncated means (more matches exist than are listed).
	exec := ExecuteECalc(nil, ECalcRequest{Operation: "search", Query: "voltage divider", Limit: 1})
	if exec.Event != nil {
		t.Fatal("search must not emit a desktop event")
	}
	out := ecalcDecode(t, exec)
	results, _ := out["results"].([]any)
	total, _ := out["total"].(float64)
	// voltage_divider and loaded_divider always match, so a limit of 1 cuts the list: the single hit that fits is
	// listed (the default budget is far from reached) and the answer says it is truncated.
	if out["status"] != "ok" || out["operation"] != "search" || out["query"] != "voltage divider" || len(results) != 1 || out["returned"] != float64(1) || total < 2 || out["truncated"] != true {
		t.Fatalf("output = %s", exec.Output)
	}
	first := results[0].(map[string]any)
	if first["id"] != "voltage_divider" || first["kind"] != "calculator" || first["category"] != "basics" || first["name"] != "Voltage divider" || first["summary"] == "" {
		t.Fatalf("first result = %v", first)
	}
	// A larger limit lists at most that many; truncated is set exactly when more matches exist than are listed.
	for _, limit := range []int{0, 3, 25, 500} {
		out = ecalcDecode(t, ExecuteECalc(nil, ECalcRequest{Operation: "search", Query: "voltage divider", Limit: limit}))
		results, _ = out["results"].([]any)
		returned, _ := out["returned"].(float64)
		total, _ = out["total"].(float64)
		most := limit
		if limit < 1 {
			most = 10 // the default
		}
		most = min(most, 25)
		// This query has a handful of matches that are far from the budget, so the limit and the number of matches are
		// the only things that can cut the list (a hit is not dropped for size too early).
		if int(returned) != min(most, int(total)) || int(returned) != len(results) || len(results) < 1 || len(results) > most || total < returned || (out["truncated"] == true) != (total > returned) {
			t.Errorf("limit %d: returned %v of %v with %d results and truncated=%v: %s", limit, returned, total, len(results), out["truncated"], ecalcMarshalForLog(out))
		}
		// The exact id ranks first whatever else matches.
		if ids := resultIDs(results); len(ids) == 0 || ids[0] != "voltage_divider" {
			t.Errorf("limit %d: the ranking starts with %v", limit, ids)
		}
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement the tool**

Create `internal/tools/ecalc.go`:

```go
package tools

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"strings"
	"unicode/utf8"

	"aurago/internal/config"
	"aurago/internal/desktop"
	"aurago/internal/ecalc"
)

// The ecalc tool: search, describe and calculate on the embedded ECalc catalog (pure computation, no I/O) and open
// the ECalc desktop app pre-filled. Only open touches the desktop and is gated like the other desktop-opening tools.

const (
	// ecalcDefaultBudget is the agent's inline floor in bytes, used when the caller passes none.
	ecalcDefaultBudget = 6000
	// ecalcBudgetSlack is kept free for the wrapper the agent puts around a tool answer.
	ecalcBudgetSlack = 600
	ecalcMinBudget   = 1500
	// ecalcSetsLimit is the number of solvable input sets that describe and the under-determined error list when
	// the answer has to be shortened.
	ecalcSetsLimit = 12
	ecalcQueryEcho = 100
)

// ECalcRequest is a decoded ecalc tool call. Inputs are variable ids with the values as a person would type them
// ("4k7", "12 V"); Choices pair a choice id with an option id. OutputBudget is the agent's inline limit in bytes
// (0 = 6,000): search results, descriptions and results are shortened to stay below it.
type ECalcRequest struct {
	Operation    string
	Query        string
	ID           string
	Inputs       []ecalc.NamedValue
	Choices      []ecalc.NamedValue
	ESeries      string
	Limit        int
	OutputBudget int
}

// ExecuteECalc runs the ecalc tool. Output is a JSON string with status ok, error or policy_denied; open also
// carries the desktop event that opens the app.
func ExecuteECalc(cfg *config.Config, req ECalcRequest) VirtualDesktopExecution {
	cat, err := ecalc.Default()
	if err != nil {
		return ecalcFailure("error", "ecalc_unavailable", "The ECalc catalog could not be loaded.")
	}
	budget := ecalcBudget(req.OutputBudget)
	switch op := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(req.Operation)); op {
	case "search":
		return ecalcSearch(cat, req, budget)
	case "describe":
		return ecalcDescribe(cat, req, budget)
	case "calculate":
		return ecalcCalculate(cat, req, budget)
	case "open":
		return ecalcOpen(cfg, cat, req)
	default:
		return ecalcFailure("error", "invalid_operation", "operation must be search, describe, calculate or open.")
	}
}

func ecalcBudget(requested int) int {
	if requested <= 0 {
		requested = ecalcDefaultBudget
	}
	return max(requested-ecalcBudgetSlack, ecalcMinBudget)
}

// ecalcEncode writes v as one line of JSON without HTML escaping, so that formulas keep their < and > readable.
func ecalcEncode(v any) (string, bool) {
	var buf bytes.Buffer
	enc := json.NewEncoder(&buf)
	enc.SetEscapeHTML(false)
	if err := enc.Encode(v); err != nil {
		return `{"status":"error","code":"ecalc_failed","message":"result could not be encoded"}`, false
	}
	return strings.TrimRight(buf.String(), "\n"), true
}

func ecalcResult(v any, event *desktop.Event) VirtualDesktopExecution {
	out, _ := ecalcEncode(v)
	return VirtualDesktopExecution{Output: out, Event: event}
}

// ecalcFit encodes the answer and applies the shortening steps one after the other until it fits the budget.
func ecalcFit(budget int, build func() any, steps ...func()) VirtualDesktopExecution {
	out, _ := ecalcEncode(build())
	for _, step := range steps {
		if len(out) <= budget {
			break
		}
		step()
		out, _ = ecalcEncode(build())
	}
	return VirtualDesktopExecution{Output: out}
}

type ecalcFailureOut struct {
	Status  string     `json:"status"`
	Code    string     `json:"code"`
	Message string     `json:"message"`
	Sets    [][]string `json:"sets,omitempty"`
}

func ecalcFailure(status, code, message string) VirtualDesktopExecution {
	return ecalcResult(ecalcFailureOut{Status: status, Code: code, Message: message}, nil)
}

// ecalcQueryFailure turns a request error of the ecalc package into the answer, with the solvable sets of an
// under-determined request.
func ecalcQueryFailure(err error) VirtualDesktopExecution {
	qe := ecalc.AsQueryError(err)
	if qe == nil {
		return ecalcFailure("error", "ecalc_failed", "ECalc could not answer this request.")
	}
	out := ecalcFailureOut{Status: "error", Code: qe.Code, Message: qe.Message, Sets: qe.Sets}
	if len(out.Sets) > ecalcSetsLimit {
		out.Sets = out.Sets[:ecalcSetsLimit]
	}
	return ecalcResult(out, nil)
}

func ecalcClip(s string, maxRunes int) string {
	s = strings.Join(strings.Fields(strings.ToValidUTF8(s, "")), " ")
	if utf8.RuneCountInString(s) <= maxRunes {
		return s
	}
	return strings.TrimSpace(string([]rune(s)[:maxRunes-1])) + "…"
}

// ---- search ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

type ecalcSearchOut struct {
	Status     string                  `json:"status"`
	Operation  string                  `json:"operation"`
	Query      string                  `json:"query,omitempty"`
	Total      int                     `json:"total"`
	Returned   int                     `json:"returned"`
	Results    []ecalc.SearchHit       `json:"results,omitempty"`
	Categories []ecalc.CategorySummary `json:"categories,omitempty"`
	Truncated  bool                    `json:"truncated,omitempty"`
	Note       string                  `json:"note,omitempty"`
}

func ecalcSearch(cat *ecalc.Catalog, req ECalcRequest, budget int) VirtualDesktopExecution {
	query := strings.TrimSpace(req.Query)
	if query == "" {
		return ecalcResult(ecalcSearchOut{
			Status: "ok", Operation: "search", Total: len(cat.Calculators), Categories: cat.Overview(),
			Note: "Give a query (a topic, part, formula or category name, in English or German) to list calculators; the categories are above.",
		}, nil)
	}
	all := cat.SearchAll(query)
	limit := req.Limit
	if limit < 1 {
		limit = ecalc.DefaultSearchLimit
	}
	limit = min(limit, ecalc.MaxSearchLimit)
	out := ecalcSearchOut{Status: "ok", Operation: "search", Query: ecalcClip(query, ecalcQueryEcho), Total: len(all)}
	if len(all) > limit {
		out.Results = all[:limit]
		out.Truncated = true
	} else {
		out.Results = all
	}
	if len(all) == 0 {
		out.Note = "No calculator matches. Try other words, an English or German term, or a category name; an empty query lists the categories."
	}
	// One step per result: each drops the last hit until the answer fits.
	cut := func() {
		if len(out.Results) > 1 {
			out.Results = out.Results[:len(out.Results)-1]
			out.Truncated = true
		}
	}
	steps := make([]func(), len(out.Results))
	for i := range steps {
		steps[i] = cut
	}
	return ecalcFit(budget, func() any { out.Returned = len(out.Results); return out }, steps...)
}

// ---- describe -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

type ecalcDescribeOut struct {
	Status    string `json:"status"`
	Operation string `json:"operation"`
	ecalc.Description
	SetsTotal int  `json:"sets_total,omitempty"`
	Truncated bool `json:"truncated,omitempty"`
}

func ecalcDescribe(cat *ecalc.Catalog, req ECalcRequest, budget int) VirtualDesktopExecution {
	d, err := cat.Describe(req.ID)
	if err != nil {
		return ecalcQueryFailure(err)
	}
	out := ecalcDescribeOut{Status: "ok", Operation: "describe", Description: d}
	return ecalcFit(budget, func() any { return out },
		func() { out.Doc, out.Truncated = ecalcClip(out.Doc, 240), true },
		func() { out.Formula, out.Source = nil, ecalcClip(out.Source, 120) },
		func() {
			if len(out.Sets) > ecalcSetsLimit {
				out.SetsTotal, out.Sets = len(out.Sets), out.Sets[:ecalcSetsLimit]
			}
		},
		func() {
			out.Checks = nil
			vars := make([]ecalc.VarInfo, len(out.Vars))
			copy(vars, out.Vars)
			for i := range vars {
				vars[i].Units = nil
			}
			out.Vars = vars
		},
	)
}

// ---- calculate ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

type ecalcCalcOut struct {
	Status    string `json:"status"`
	Operation string `json:"operation"`
	Code      string `json:"code,omitempty"`
	Message   string `json:"message,omitempty"`
	ecalc.CalcResult
}

func ecalcRequestOf(req ECalcRequest) ecalc.CalcRequest {
	return ecalc.CalcRequest{Values: req.Inputs, Choices: req.Choices, ESeries: req.ESeries}
}

func ecalcCalculate(cat *ecalc.Catalog, req ECalcRequest, budget int) VirtualDesktopExecution {
	res, err := cat.Calculate(req.ID, ecalcRequestOf(req))
	if err != nil {
		return ecalcQueryFailure(err)
	}
	out := ecalcCalcOut{Status: "ok", Operation: "calculate", CalcResult: res}
	var notes []string
	if n := len(res.Contradictions); n > 0 {
		names := make([]string, n)
		for i, c := range res.Contradictions {
			names[i] = c.Name
		}
		notes = append(notes, fmt.Sprintf("Redundant values contradict the result by more than %g %%: %s. The result was computed from %s; see contradictions.",
			ecalc.ContradictionTolerance*100, strings.Join(names, ", "), strings.Join(res.Basis, ", ")))
	}
	if res.HasErrors() {
		var bad []string
		for _, q := range res.Quantities {
			if q.Error != "" {
				bad = append(bad, q.ID+" ("+q.Error+")")
			}
		}
		out.Status, out.Code = "error", "calculation_failed"
		notes = append(notes, "Some quantities could not be computed: "+strings.Join(bad, "; ")+".")
	}
	out.Message = strings.Join(notes, " ")
	quantities := func(f func(q *ecalc.Quantity)) func() {
		return func() {
			qs := make([]ecalc.Quantity, len(out.Quantities))
			copy(qs, out.Quantities)
			for i := range qs {
				f(&qs[i])
			}
			out.Quantities = qs
		}
	}
	return ecalcFit(budget, func() any { return out },
		quantities(func(q *ecalc.Quantity) { q.Label = "" }),
		quantities(func(q *ecalc.Quantity) { q.Name = "" }),
		quantities(func(q *ecalc.Quantity) { q.Dim, q.SIList = "", nil }),
		func() { out.Combos = ecalcTrimCombos(out.Combos, 2) },
	)
}

// ecalcTrimCombos keeps the single value and the first per entries of every other kind of the combiner's list.
func ecalcTrimCombos(combos []ecalc.ComboInfo, per int) []ecalc.ComboInfo {
	var out []ecalc.ComboInfo
	count := map[string]int{}
	for _, c := range combos {
		if count[c.Kind]++; c.Kind == ecalc.ComboSingle || count[c.Kind] <= per {
			out = append(out, c)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// ---- open -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// ecalcOrdered is a JSON object whose keys keep their order: the app takes the order of the values as the order in
// which they were typed (the most recent ones win when more values are given than the calculator needs).
type ecalcOrdered []ecalc.NamedValue

func (o ecalcOrdered) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error) {
	var buf bytes.Buffer
	buf.WriteByte('{')
	for i, nv := range o {
		if i > 0 {
			buf.WriteByte(',')
		}
		key, _ := json.Marshal(nv.Name)
		val, _ := json.Marshal(nv.Value)
		buf.Write(key)
		buf.WriteByte(':')
		buf.Write(val)
	}
	buf.WriteByte('}')
	return buf.Bytes(), nil
}

type ecalcOpenOut struct {
	Status    string             `json:"status"`
	Operation string             `json:"operation"`
	Page      string             `json:"page,omitempty"`
	Values    []ecalc.NamedValue `json:"values,omitempty"`
	Choices   []ecalc.NamedValue `json:"choices,omitempty"`
	Message   string             `json:"message"`
}

func ecalcOpen(cfg *config.Config, cat *ecalc.Catalog, req ECalcRequest) VirtualDesktopExecution {
	if cfg == nil || !cfg.VirtualDesktop.Enabled {
		return ecalcFailure("policy_denied", "desktop_unavailable", "The virtual desktop is switched off, so ECalc cannot be opened.")
	}
	if !cfg.VirtualDesktop.AllowAgentControl || !cfg.Tools.VirtualDesktop.Enabled {
		return ecalcFailure("policy_denied", "desktop_agent_control_disabled", "The user has not allowed the agent to control the desktop, so ECalc cannot be opened. Give the user the numbers from calculate instead.")
	}
	if strings.TrimSpace(req.ID) == "" && len(req.Inputs) == 0 && len(req.Choices) == 0 {
		event := virtualDesktopEvent("open_app", map[string]interface{}{"app_id": "ecalc"})
		return ecalcResult(ecalcOpenOut{Status: "ok", Operation: "open", Message: "Asked the desktop to open the ECalc app."}, event)
	}
	checked, err := cat.Check(req.ID, ecalcRequestOf(req))
	if err != nil {
		return ecalcQueryFailure(err)
	}
	launch := map[string]interface{}{
		"page":    checked.ID,
		"values":  ecalcOrdered(checked.Values),
		"choices": ecalcOrdered(checked.Choices),
	}
	event := virtualDesktopEvent("open_app", map[string]interface{}{"app_id": "ecalc", "ecalc": launch})
	message := "Asked the desktop to open ECalc at the " + cat.Calculator(checked.ID).Name["en"] + " calculator"
	switch n := len(checked.Values); {
	case n == 1:
		message += ", pre-filled with 1 value"
	case n > 1:
		message += fmt.Sprintf(", pre-filled with %d values", n)
	}
	message += ". Nothing was computed; use calculate to get the numbers yourself."
	return ecalcResult(ecalcOpenOut{
		Status: "ok", Operation: "open", Page: checked.ID, Values: checked.Values, Choices: checked.Choices, Message: message,
	}, event)
}
```

````go
package agent

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"

	"aurago/internal/config"

	openai "github.com/sashabaranov/go-openai"
)

type ecalcJSONBroker struct {
	captureBroker
	mu   sync.Mutex
	json []string
}

func (b *ecalcJSONBroker) SendJSON(s string) {
	b.mu.Lock()
	b.json = append(b.json, s)
	b.mu.Unlock()
}

func ecalcAgentConfig() *config.Config {
	cfg := &config.Config{}
	cfg.VirtualDesktop.Enabled = true
	cfg.VirtualDesktop.AllowAgentControl = true
	cfg.Tools.VirtualDesktop.Enabled = true
	return cfg
}

func ecalcNativeCall(t *testing.T, arguments string) ToolCall {
	t.Helper()
	tc := NativeToolCallToToolCall(openai.ToolCall{ID: "call-1", Type: "function", Function: openai.FunctionCall{Name: "ecalc", Arguments: arguments}}, nil)
	if tc.NativeArgsMalformed {
		t.Fatalf("native arguments flagged malformed: %s (%s)", tc.NativeArgsError, arguments)
	}
	return tc
}

func TestECalcSchemaIsStrictCompactAndNamedSafely(t *testing.T) {
	s := ecalcSchema()
	if s.Function.Name != "ecalc" {
		t.Fatalf("name = %q", s.Function.Name)
	}
	params := s.Function.Parameters.(map[string]interface{})
	props := params["properties"].(map[string]interface{})
	if got := props["operation"].(map[string]interface{})["enum"]; !slices.Equal(got.([]string), []string{"search", "describe", "calculate", "open"}) {
		t.Fatalf("operations = %v", got)
	}
	if got := props["eseries"].(map[string]interface{})["enum"]; !slices.Equal(got.([]string), []string{"E3", "E6", "E12", "E24", "E48", "E96", "E192"}) {
		t.Fatalf("series = %v", got)
	}
	if required := params["required"].([]string); !slices.Equal(required, []string{"operation"}) {
		t.Fatalf("required = %v", required)
	}
	for _, key := range []string{"inputs", "choices"} {
		items := props[key].(map[string]interface{})["items"].(map[string]interface{})
		if items["additionalProperties"] != false || len(items["properties"].(map[string]interface{})) != 2 {
			t.Fatalf("%s items = %v", key, items)
		}
	}
	// ToolCall owns "values" for spreadsheets (an array of arrays), so an array of objects under that name would
	// mark every call malformed. The variable values travel as inputs.
	if _, clash := props["values"]; clash {
		t.Fatal("the schema must not use the parameter name values")
	}
	// A name with one of these words is read as a network destination by the action policy.
	for name := range props {
		for _, word := range []string{"url", "uri", "link", "host", "domain", "endpoint"} {
			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(name), word) {
				t.Errorf("parameter %q contains %q", name, word)
			}
		}
	}
	if got := estimateSingleToolSchemaTokens(s); got > 450 {
		t.Fatalf("the ecalc schema is %d tokens, keep it at most 450", got)
	}
}

func TestECalcIsAlwaysOnAndFoundThroughDiscovery(t *testing.T) {
	if !slices.Contains(builtinToolNames(ToolFeatureFlags{}), "ecalc") {
		t.Fatal("ecalc needs no switch: it must be in the schemas of the zero feature flags")
	}
	if got := ToolCategoryForName("ecalc"); got != "infrastructure" {
		t.Fatalf("category = %q", got)
	}
	if terms := toolSearchTermsFor("ecalc"); len(terms) < 6 || !slices.Contains(terms, "electronics calculator") || !slices.Contains(terms, "Elektronik Rechner") {
		t.Fatalf("search terms = %q", terms)
	}
	catalog := BuildToolCatalog(BuildNativeToolSchemas("", nil, ToolFeatureFlags{}, nil), nil, "")
	for _, query := range []string{"electronics calculator", "Spannungsteiler berechnen", "LED Vorwiderstand", "ohms law"} {
		matches := catalog.Search(query)
		found := false
		for _, entry := range matches[:min(5, len(matches))] {
			found = found || entry.Name == "ecalc"

		if !found {
			t.Errorf("%q did not find ecalc in the top five", query)

	}
}

func TestECalcNativeCallDecodesInputsAndChoices(t *testing.T) {
	tc := ecalcNativeCall(t, `{"operation":"calculate","id":"rms_waveform","inputs":[{"name":"vrms","value":"230 V"},{"name":"vpk","value":325}],"choices":[{"name":"wave","option":"triangle"}],"eseries":"E96","limit":5,"query":"x"}`)
	req := decodeECalcArgs(tc)
	if req.Operation != "calculate" || req.ID != "rms_waveform" || req.Query != "x" || req.ESeries != "E96" || req.Limit != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("request = %+v", req)
	}
	if len(req.Inputs) != 2 || req.Inputs[0].Name != "vrms" || req.Inputs[0].Value != "230 V" || req.Inputs[1].Value != "325" {
		t.Fatalf("inputs = %+v", req.Inputs)
	}
	if len(req.Choices) != 1 || req.Choices[0].Name != "wave" || req.Choices[0].Value != "triangle" {
		t.Fatalf("choices = %+v", req.Choices)
	}
	// The shapes models send instead of the array of pairs.
	for name, arguments := range map[string]string{
		"object":      `{"operation":"calculate","id":"x","inputs":{"vrms":"230 V"},"choices":{"wave":"sine"}}`,
		"JSON text":   `{"operation":"calculate","id":"x","inputs":"[{\"name\":\"vrms\",\"value\":\"230 V\"}]","choices":"{\"wave\":\"sine\"}"}`,
		"value alias": `{"operation":"calculate","id":"x","inputs":[{"name":"vrms","value":"230 V"}],"choices":[{"name":"wave","value":"sine"}]}`,
	} {
		got := decodeECalcArgs(ecalcNativeCall(t, arguments))
		if len(got.Inputs) != 1 || got.Inputs[0].Name != "vrms" || got.Inputs[0].Value != "230 V" || len(got.Choices) != 1 || got.Choices[0].Value != "sine" {
			t.Errorf("%s: %+v", name, got)
		}
	}
	// Text-mode calls carry the generic fields.
	req = decodeECalcArgs(ToolCall{Action: "ecalc", Operation: " Search ", Query: "ohm", Limit: 3, ID: "ohms_law"})
	if req.Operation != "search" || req.Query != "ohm" || req.Limit != 3 || req.ID != "ohms_law" {
		t.Fatalf("text-mode request = %+v", req)
	}
}

		} `json:"payload"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(broker.json[0]), &msg); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	p := msg.Payload
	if msg.Type != "virtual_desktop_event" || p.Type != "open_app" || p.ID == "" || p.Payload.AppID != "ecalc" ||
		p.Payload.ECalc.Page != "voltage_divider" || p.Payload.ECalc.Values["vin"] != "12 V" || p.Payload.ECalc.Values["r1"] != "4k7" || len(p.Payload.ECalc.Choices) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("broadcast = %s", broker.json[0])
	}
	// The order of the values is the order in the call.
	if !strings.Contains(broker.json[0], `"values":{"vin":"12 V","r1":"4k7"}`) {
		t.Fatalf("the values lost their order: %s", broker.json[0])
	}
}

func TestECalcDispatchOpenIsDeniedWhileTheDesktopGatesAreClosed(t *testing.T) {
	for name, mutate := range map[string]func(*config.Config){
		"desktop off":            func(c *config.Config) { c.VirtualDesktop.Enabled = false },
		"agent control off":      func(c *config.Config) { c.VirtualDesktop.AllowAgentControl = false },
		"desktop tools disabled": func(c *config.Config) { c.Tools.VirtualDesktop.Enabled = false },
	} {
		cfg := ecalcAgentConfig()
		mutate(cfg)
		broker := &ecalcJSONBroker{}
		dc := &DispatchContext{Cfg: cfg, Logger: testLogger, Broker: broker}
		out, ok := dispatchPlatform(context.Background(), ecalcNativeCall(t, `{"operation":"open","id":"ohms_law"}`), dc)
		if !ok || !strings.Contains(out, `"status":"policy_denied"`) || len(broker.json) != 0 {
			t.Errorf("%s: %v %s broadcasts=%d", name, ok, out, len(broker.json))
		}
	}
}

// The runnable examples of the manual must be valid calls: known parameters, schema enums, and they run.
func TestECalcManualExamplesAreValidCalls(t *testing.T) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join("..", "..", "prompts", "tools_manuals", "ecalc.md"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	examples := regexp.MustCompile("(?s)```json\\s*\\n(.*?)\\n```").FindAllSubmatch(data, -1)
	if len(examples) < 4 {
		t.Fatalf("the manual has %d JSON examples, want at least 4", len(examples))
	}
	props := ecalcSchema().Function.Parameters.(map[string]interface{})["properties"].(map[string]interface{})
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	for _, example := range examples {
		var call map[string]any
		if err := json.Unmarshal(example[1], &call); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%v\n%s", err, example[1])
		}
		if call["action"] != "ecalc" {
			t.Fatalf("example for %v", call["action"])
		}
		for key, value := range call {
			if key == "action" {
				continue
			}
			property, ok := props[key].(map[string]interface{})
			if !ok {
				t.Fatalf("unknown parameter %q in %s", key, example[1])
			}
			if enum, ok := property["enum"].([]string); ok && !slices.Contains(enum, value.(string)) {
				t.Fatalf("%s=%v is not in %v", key, value, enum)
			}
		}
		seen[call["operation"].(string)] = true
		raw, _ := json.Marshal(call)
		tc := ecalcNativeCall(t, string(raw))
		out, ok := dispatchPlatform(context.Background(), tc, &DispatchContext{Cfg: ecalcAgentConfig(), Logger: testLogger, Broker: &ecalcJSONBroker{}})
		if !ok || !strings.Contains(out, `"status":"ok"`) {
			t.Errorf("the example does not run: %s\n%s", example[1], out)
		}
	}
	for _, op := range []string{"search", "describe", "calculate", "open"} {
		if !seen[op] {
			t.Errorf("the manual has no example for %s", op)
		}
	}
}
````

```go
package agent

import (
	"aurago/internal/ecalc"

	openai "github.com/sashabaranov/go-openai"
)

// ecalcSchema describes the ecalc tool: electronics calculators from the embedded ECalc catalog. It is always
// present (pure computation, no switch); only the open operation needs the Virtual Desktop. The schema stays small
// because the manual (prompts/tools_manuals/ecalc.md) carries the details. The variable values are called inputs:
// ToolCall already owns a "values" field for spreadsheets that only decodes arrays of arrays, so an array of
// objects under that name would mark every call malformed.
func ecalcSchema() openai.Tool {
	pairs := func(description, valueKey, valueHelp string) map[string]interface{} {
		return map[string]interface{}{
			"type":        "array",
			"description": description,
			"items": map[string]interface{}{
				"type": "object",
				"properties": map[string]interface{}{
					"name":   prop("string", "Id from describe."),
					valueKey: prop("string", valueHelp),
				},
				"required":             []string{"name", valueKey},
				"additionalProperties": false,
			},
		}
	}
	return tool("ecalc",
		"Electronics calculators from the ECalc catalog (Ohm's law, dividers, filters, op-amps, E-series): search them, describe one, calculate with units, or open one pre-filled in the ECalc app.",
		schema(map[string]interface{}{
			"operation": operationProperty("search finds calculators, describe lists variables and solvable inputs, calculate solves, open shows one in the ECalc desktop app.", []string{"search", "describe", "calculate", "open"}),
			"query":     prop("string", "search: topic, part or formula, English or German. Empty lists the categories."),
			"id":        prop("string", "describe, calculate, open: calculator id from search."),
			"inputs":    pairs("calculate, open: known values as {name, value}, for example 4k7, 12 V or 25 °C. A bare number is in the variable's default unit.", "value", "Value as typed."),
			"choices":   pairs("calculate, open: choice selections as {name, option}.", "option", "Option id from describe."),
			"eseries": map[string]interface{}{
				"type":        "string",
				"description": "calculate: E-series for standard-value suggestions (default E24).",
				"enum":        append([]string(nil), ecalc.ESeriesIDs...),
			},
			"limit": prop("integer", "search: 1-25, default 10."),
		}, "operation"),
	)
}
```

Create `internal/agent/tool_args_ecalc.go`:

```go
package agent

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"aurago/internal/ecalc"
	"aurago/internal/tools"
)

// decodeECalcArgs reads an ecalc call from native params first and falls back to the generic ToolCall fields of
// text-mode calls. The variable values are called inputs on the wire because ToolCall already owns a "values" field
// for spreadsheets, which only decodes arrays of arrays.
func decodeECalcArgs(tc ToolCall) tools.ECalcRequest {
	return tools.ECalcRequest{
		Operation: strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(firstNonEmptyToolString(tc.Operation, toolArgString(tc.Params, "operation")))),
		Query:     firstNonEmptyToolString(toolArgString(tc.Params, "query"), tc.Query),
		ID:        firstNonEmptyToolString(toolArgString(tc.Params, "id"), tc.ID),
		Inputs:    ecalcPairs(tc.Params["inputs"], "value"),
		Choices:   ecalcPairs(tc.Params["choices"], "option"),
		ESeries:   toolArgString(tc.Params, "eseries", "e_series", "series"),
		Limit:     firstNonEmptyInt(toolArgInt(tc.Params, 0, "limit"), tc.Limit),
	}
}

// ecalcPairs reads {name, <valueKey>} pairs. The schema asks for an array of objects; a JSON object of name to
// value pairs and a JSON text of either are accepted too, because models send them. Numbers are taken as typed.
func ecalcPairs(raw interface{}, valueKey string) []ecalc.NamedValue {
	if text, ok := raw.(string); ok {
		var decoded interface{}
		if json.Unmarshal([]byte(text), &decoded) != nil {
			return nil
		}
		raw = decoded
	}
	var out []ecalc.NamedValue
	switch v := raw.(type) {
	case []interface{}:
		for _, item := range v {
			m, ok := item.(map[string]interface{})
			if !ok {
				continue
			}
			name := strings.TrimSpace(toolArgString(m, "name", "id", "var"))
			if name == "" {
				continue
			}
			value, _ := ecalcScalarText(m[valueKey])
			if value == "" {
				value, _ = ecalcScalarText(m["value"])
			}
			out = append(out, ecalc.NamedValue{Name: name, Value: value})
		}
	case map[string]interface{}:
		keys := make([]string, 0, len(v))
		for k := range v {
			keys = append(keys, k)
		}
		sort.Strings(keys)
		for _, k := range keys {
			if value, ok := ecalcScalarText(v[k]); ok {
				out = append(out, ecalc.NamedValue{Name: k, Value: value})
			}
		}
	}
	return out
}

// ecalcScalarText is the text of a string or a number.
func ecalcScalarText(raw interface{}) (string, bool) {
	switch v := raw.(type) {
	case string:
		return strings.TrimSpace(v), true
	case float64:
		return strconv.FormatFloat(v, 'g', -1, 64), true
	case json.Number:
		return v.String(), true
	case int:
		return strconv.Itoa(v), true
	case int64:
		return strconv.FormatInt(v, 10), true
	}
	return "", false
}
```

Create `internal/agent/ecalc_tool.go`:

```go
package agent

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"

	"aurago/internal/desktop"
	"aurago/internal/tools"
)

// dispatchECalc runs the ecalc tool and forwards the open_app event of an open to the desktop exactly like
// virtual_desktop and retro_games do. The answer is sized to the inline budget so the output vault never archives
// it. The gate of open (desktop, agent control) lives in tools.ExecuteECalc; the A2A restriction of open is the role
// policy's (a2aDesktopWrite).
func dispatchECalc(_ context.Context, tc ToolCall, dc *DispatchContext) string {
	req := decodeECalcArgs(tc)
	req.OutputBudget = toolResultInlineBudget(dc)
	if dc.Logger != nil {
		dc.Logger.Info("LLM requested ECalc", "operation", req.Operation)
	}
	exec := tools.ExecuteECalc(dc.Cfg, req)
	if exec.Event != nil && dc.Broker != nil {
		payload, err := json.Marshal(struct {
			Type    string         `json:"type"`
			Payload *desktop.Event `json:"payload"`
		}{"virtual_desktop_event", exec.Event})
		if err == nil {
			dc.Broker.SendJSON(string(payload))
		}
	}
	return "Tool Output: " + exec.Output
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Create the manual**

Create `prompts/tools_manuals/ecalc.md` (its JSON examples are run by `TestECalcManualExamplesAreValidCalls`; the manual is plain Markdown, the fences below are longer than the ones inside it):

````markdown
# ECalc (electronics calculators)

Use `ecalc` for electronics formulas: Ohm's law, voltage dividers, filters, timers, op-amp stages, power supplies, RF, standard resistor values and more. It computes with the same catalog and formulas as the ECalc desktop app, exactly and with units; use it instead of calculating by hand. It reads nothing from the network or from files.

## Workflow

1. `search` with a few words (English or German): a topic, a part or a formula. An empty `query` lists the categories.
2. `describe` the calculator you picked: its variables with units and defaults, the choices, how many values are needed (`dof`), which input combinations work (`sets`), the computed outputs (`derived`), the checks and the formula.
3. `calculate` with the values you know. Any complete input set works, so you can solve for whichever quantity is missing.
4. `open` only when the user wants to see or play with the calculator; it opens the ECalc app on the desktop, pre-filled with your values.

```json
{"action":"ecalc","operation":"search","query":"voltage divider"}
```

```json
{"action":"ecalc","operation":"describe","id":"voltage_divider"}
```

```json
{"action":"ecalc","operation":"calculate","id":"voltage_divider","inputs":[{"name":"vout","value":"3.3 V"},{"name":"vin","value":"12 V"},{"name":"r1","value":"10k"}],"eseries":"E96"}
```

```json
{"action":"ecalc","operation":"calculate","id":"eseries_combiner","inputs":[{"name":"target","value":"5k"}],"eseries":"E24"}
```

```json
{"action":"ecalc","operation":"open","id":"rms_waveform","inputs":[{"name":"vrms","value":"230 V"}],"choices":[{"name":"wave","option":"triangle"}]}
```

## Operations

- `search`: `query`, optional `limit` (1-25, default 10). Results hold `id`, `name`, `category` and a one-sentence `summary`, best match first; `total` is the number of matches and `truncated: true` means more exist than were returned.
- `describe`: `id`. Vars have `id`, `label`, `name`, `dim`, `unit` (the unit a bare number is read in; empty means the SI unit), `units` (units a value may carry), `input`, `eseries` and the `default`.
- `calculate`: `id`, `inputs`, optional `choices` and `eseries` (E3, E6, E12, E24, E48, E96 or E192; default E24).
- `open`: `id` (optional), optional `inputs` and `choices`. Without `id` it only opens the app. The values are not checked against each other; the app shows them as typed.

## Values

- Write values the way a person types them: `4700`, `4.7k`, `4k7`, `4R7` (resistance), `2u2`, `10mA`, `12 V`, `25 °C`, `-10 dBm`. A decimal comma works too.
- A bare number is in the variable's default unit from `describe` (`unit`; the SI unit when it is empty). `2` for a capacity shown in Ah is 2 Ah; write `2000 mAh` to be explicit.
- A list variable takes `"4k7, 10k, 2k2"`: separate the items with a comma and no space between a number and its unit.
- `name` is a variable id from `describe`; case does not matter and the label (`V_in`) works too. Choices (a waveform, a material) are `{name, option}` with ids from `describe`; a choice you leave out uses its default.
- A number system (`dim: integer`, units `dec`, `hex`, `bin`, `oct`) is read in the unit of its variable: a `hex` variable takes hex digits with or without `0x`, a `bin` variable binary digits with or without `0b`; the result is shown the same way (`0xFF`). Whole numbers up to 2^53 - 1 only.
- Give at least `dof` values forming one of the `sets`. With more values the first solvable combination is used and the others are checked against the result.

## Reading the result

- `quantities` lists every variable and computed output with `si` (SI base units), `formatted` (4 significant digits in the variable's display unit) and `computed` (false for what you gave). Report `formatted` to the user.
- `eseries` on a computed resistor is the nearest standard value of the chosen series with its deviation in percent; offer that value when the user wants to buy or build the circuit.
- A choice option may ignore variables (`ignore` in `describe`, `ignored: true` in the result): you need not give them, and when the values you give do not make a solvable set their defaults complete it (`defaulted: true`).
- `combos` (the standard-value combiner `eseries_combiner`, finder `combine`) lists the nearest single standard value and the best series and parallel pairs of the chosen series for the target resistance: `kind` single, series or parallel, `r1`, `r2`, the combined `value` and `dev_pct`, the deviation from the target in percent.
- `warnings` are the calculator's own checks (for example a divider output above its input); mention them.
- `contradictions` lists a redundant value that differs from the computed one by more than 1 %; tell the user their numbers do not agree and which one you computed from (`basis`).
- A quantity with `error` (`range`, `nonfinite`) could not be computed from these values, for example a division by zero; the answer has `status: error` and `code: calculation_failed` then.

## Errors

- `unknown_id`: the message suggests close matches; search first.
- `unknown_variable`, `not_an_input` (a computed output cannot be given), `unknown_choice`, `unknown_option`, `unknown_eseries`, `duplicate_name`, `too_many_values`: the message lists the valid names; fix the call.
- `parse_error`: the text of one value could not be read with the unit of its variable; the message names the variable and its dimension.
- `underdetermined`: too few values, or no combination of them is a solvable set; `sets` lists the input sets closest first and the message says what to add.
- `invalid_operation`: use `search`, `describe`, `calculate` or `open`.
- `policy_denied` with `desktop_unavailable` or `desktop_agent_control_disabled` (open only): the desktop is off or the user has not allowed the agent to control it. Give the numbers from `calculate` instead and say that the user can open ECalc themselves.
- Answers are shortened to fit the output limit; `truncated: true` marks it. Search again with more specific words or fewer results rather than asking for more.
````

```go
package agent

// The ecalc tool is pure computation except for open: only open mutates, and an A2A peer (a remote agent whose

func TestECalcActionPolicyOnlyOpenMutates(t *testing.T) {
	for op, want := range map[string]bool{"search": false, "describe": false, "calculate": false, "open": true} {
		a := DescribeAction(ToolCall{Action: "ecalc", Operation: op}, nil)
		if a.Mutating != want || a.HighRisk || a.Tool != "ecalc" || a.Operation != op {
			t.Errorf("%s: %+v, want mutating=%v and no high risk", op, a, want)
		}
	}
	// The operation may also come in the params of a native call.
	if a := DescribeAction(ecalcNativeCall(t, `{"operation":"open","id":"ohms_law"}`), nil); !a.Mutating {
		t.Fatalf("native open = %+v", a)
	}
	if a := DescribeAction(ecalcNativeCall(t, `{"operation":"describe","id":"ohms_law"}`), nil); a.Mutating {
		t.Fatalf("native describe = %+v", a)
	}
}

func TestECalcRoleRestrictionKeepsComputationForPeersButNotOpen(t *testing.T) {
	main := &DispatchContext{SessionID: "default"}
	local := &DispatchContext{SessionID: "coagent-1", IsCoAgent: true, MessageSource: "co_agent", CoAgentSpecialist: "coder"}
	a2a := &DispatchContext{SessionID: "a2a-task-1", IsCoAgent: true, MessageSource: "a2a"}
	prefixOnly := &DispatchContext{SessionID: "a2a-task-2", IsCoAgent: true}

	for _, op := range []string{"search", "describe", "calculate"} {
		for name, dc := range map[string]*DispatchContext{"main": main, "local": local, "a2a": a2a, "a2a prefix": prefixOnly} {
			if got := roleToolRestriction(ToolCall{Action: "ecalc", Operation: op}, dc); got != "" {
				t.Errorf("%s run is denied ecalc %s: %q", name, op, got)
			}
		}
	}
	for name, dc := range map[string]*DispatchContext{"main": main, "local": local} {
		if got := roleToolRestriction(ToolCall{Action: "ecalc", Operation: "open"}, dc); got != "" {
			t.Errorf("%s run is denied ecalc open: %q", name, got)
		}
	}
	for _, op := range []string{"open", "", "table", "OPEN_APP"} {
		for name, dc := range map[string]*DispatchContext{"a2a": a2a, "a2a prefix": prefixOnly} {
			if got := roleToolRestriction(ToolCall{Action: "ecalc", Operation: op}, dc); !strings.Contains(got, "policy_denied") || !strings.Contains(got, "cannot change the virtual desktop") {
				t.Errorf("%s run may call ecalc %q: %q", name, op, got)
			}
		}
	}
}

func TestECalcDiscoveryOffersAPeerOnlyTheReadOperations(t *testing.T) {
	catalog := BuildToolCatalog(BuildNativeToolSchemas("", nil, ToolFeatureFlags{}, nil), nil, "")
	a2a := &DispatchContext{Cfg: &config.Config{}, SessionID: "a2a-task-1", IsCoAgent: true, MessageSource: "a2a"}
	applyCatalogEntryPolicies(catalog, a2a)
	entry, ok := catalog.Get("ecalc")
	if !ok || !entry.Enabled {
		t.Fatalf("ecalc must stay discoverable for a peer: %+v", entry)
	}
	if ops := toolCatalogOperationField(entry, "operation"); !slices.Equal(ops, []string{"search", "describe", "calculate"}) {
		t.Fatalf("a peer is offered %v", ops)
	}
	local := BuildToolCatalog(BuildNativeToolSchemas("", nil, ToolFeatureFlags{}, nil), nil, "")
	applyCatalogEntryPolicies(local, &DispatchContext{Cfg: &config.Config{}, SessionID: "default"})
	entry, _ = local.Get("ecalc")
	if ops := toolCatalogOperationField(entry, "operation"); !slices.Equal(ops, []string{"search", "describe", "calculate", "open"}) {
		t.Fatalf("the main agent is offered %v", ops)
	}
}
```
