### Task B6: The desktop bridge (core sanitizer, second-open branch, bundle)

**Independent of Part U for the bridge itself.** The Go side (task B2) emits `open_app` with `ecalc: {page, values, choices}`. This task makes the desktop core rebuild that object from checked parts and hand it to `openApp('ecalc', {launch})`, so that a new window gets `ctx.launch` in `render` and an open one gets `ECalcApp.launch(windowId, payload)` (ECalc is single-instance). The launch context is one-shot: it is not added to `SESSION_CONTEXT_KEYS`, so a restored session never overwrites what the user typed since (a test pins that).

**GitNexus impact:** `handleDesktopEvent` (`ui/js/desktop/core/sdk-events-bootstrap.js`) and `openApp` (`ui/js/desktop/core/window-shell-runtime.js`): `UNKNOWN`. The graph was unavailable (store locked, then the CLI crashed), which is not an all-clear. Text search: `handleDesktopEvent` is called from the WebSocket message handler, registered for the SSE event `virtual_desktop_event` and for the `aurago:desktop-event` window event (4 references, all in `sdk-events-bootstrap.js`); `openApp(` has about 100 call sites, which is why the new branch is guarded by `appId === 'ecalc'` and `context.launch`. Both edits are additive.

**Files:**
- Create: `ui/desktop_ecalc_launch_test.go`
- Modify: `ui/js/desktop/core/sdk-events-bootstrap.js` (before `handleDesktopEvent`, and its `open_app` branch)
- Modify: `ui/js/desktop/core/window-shell-runtime.js` (func `openApp`, the existing-window branch)
- Regenerate: `ui/js/desktop/bundles/main.bundle.js`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

Create `ui/desktop_ecalc_launch_test.go`. The first test pins the markers in the source file and in the generated bundle, the one-shot rule and the position of the second-open branch; the second runs the sanitizer block itself in Node (it skips when Node is missing, like the other Node-backed tests) against a table of good and hostile payloads:

```go
package ui

import (
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// The agent tool ecalc opens ECalc pre-filled through an open_app desktop event whose payload carries
// {ecalc: {page, values, choices}}. The core (sdk-events-bootstrap.js) rebuilds it from checked parts and hands it to
// openApp as launch.launch, which reaches the app as ctx.launch (new window) or ECalcApp.launch (window already open,
// window-shell-runtime.js). These tests are source markers plus a Node run of the sanitizer; the browser test
// covers the pre-filled page.

const (
	ecalcLaunchSanitizerStart = "    const ECALC_LAUNCH_PAGE = "
	ecalcLaunchSanitizerEnd   = "    async function handleDesktopEvent("
)

func ecalcLaunchMarkersInOrder(t *testing.T, name, source string, markers []string) {
	t.Helper()
	offset := 0
	for _, marker := range markers {
		index := strings.Index(source[offset:], marker)
		if index < 0 {
			t.Fatalf("%s: marker %q missing after offset %d", name, marker, offset)
		}
		offset += index + len(marker)
	}
}

func TestECalcLaunchBridgeSourceMarkers(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	for _, file := range []string{"js/desktop/core/sdk-events-bootstrap.js", "js/desktop/bundles/main.bundle.js"} {
		source := rawDesktopAssetText(t, file)
		ecalcLaunchMarkersInOrder(t, file, source, []string{
			"const ECALC_LAUNCH_PAGE = /^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$/;",
			"const ECALC_LAUNCH_NAME = /^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$/;",
			"function sanitizeECalcLaunchPairs(raw, valueLimit, valuePattern) {",
			"if (count >= 32) break;",
			"value.length > valueLimit",
			"function sanitizeECalcLaunch(raw) {",
			"values: sanitizeECalcLaunchPairs(raw.values, 256, null),",
			"choices: sanitizeECalcLaunchPairs(raw.choices, 32, ECALC_LAUNCH_NAME)",
			"async function handleDesktopEvent(event) {",
			"if (event.type === 'open_app' && event.payload && event.payload.app_id) {",
			"if (event.payload.app_id === 'ecalc') {",
			"const ecalcLaunch = sanitizeECalcLaunch(event.payload.ecalc);",
			"if (ecalcLaunch) launch.launch = ecalcLaunch;",
			"openApp(event.payload.app_id, Object.keys(launch).length ? launch : undefined);",
		})
	}
	// The launch context is one-shot: a restored session must never overwrite what the user typed since.
	session := rawDesktopAssetText(t, "js/desktop/core/session-runtime.js")
	if start := strings.Index(session, "const SESSION_CONTEXT_KEYS = ["); start < 0 || strings.Contains(session[start:start+strings.Index(session[start:], "]")], "launch") {
		t.Fatal("session-runtime.js must not persist a launch context")
	}
	// The second-open branch sits inside the existing-window branch of openApp, before it returns.
	for _, file := range []string{"js/desktop/core/window-shell-runtime.js", "js/desktop/bundles/main.bundle.js"} {
		shell := strings.ReplaceAll(rawDesktopAssetText(t, file), "\r\n", "\n") // a Windows checkout has CRLF
		ecalcLaunchMarkersInOrder(t, file, shell, []string{
			"if (appId === 'ecalc' && context && context.launch && window.ECalcApp && typeof window.ECalcApp.launch === 'function') window.ECalcApp.launch(existing.id, context.launch);",
		})
		existing := strings.Index(shell, "const existing = (context && context.forceNew) ? null : findExistingAppWindow(appId, context || {});")
		branch := strings.Index(shell, "window.ECalcApp.launch(existing.id, context.launch);")
		ret := strings.Index(shell[existing:], "\n            return;\n        }")
		if existing < 0 || branch < existing || branch > existing+ret {
			t.Fatalf("%s: the ECalc launch must run inside the existing-window branch of openApp", file)
		}
	}
}

func TestECalcLaunchSanitizerRejectsWhatItDoesNotKnow(t *testing.T) {
	node, err := exec.LookPath("node")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skip("Node.js required for the ECalc launch sanitizer check")
	}
	source := rawDesktopAssetText(t, "js/desktop/core/sdk-events-bootstrap.js")
	start := strings.Index(source, ecalcLaunchSanitizerStart)
	end := strings.Index(source, ecalcLaunchSanitizerEnd)
	if start < 0 || end < start {
		t.Fatal("the sanitizer block was not found in sdk-events-bootstrap.js")
	}
	dir := t.TempDir()
	snippet := filepath.Join(dir, "sanitizer.js")
	if err := os.WriteFile(snippet, []byte(source[start:end]), 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	runner := filepath.Join(dir, "check.js")
	script := `
const assert = require('node:assert/strict');
const fs = require('node:fs');
const vm = require('node:vm');
// Same realm as this script, so that prototypes compare equal.
const { sanitizeECalcLaunch } = vm.runInThisContext(fs.readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8') + '\n({ sanitizeECalcLaunch });');
const plain = value => JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value));

// A good payload comes out unchanged, with the values in the order they were given.
const good = sanitizeECalcLaunch(JSON.parse('{"page":"voltage_divider","values":{"vin":"12 V","r1":"4k7"},"choices":{"wave":"triangle"}}'));
assert.deepEqual(plain(good), { page: 'voltage_divider', values: { vin: '12 V', r1: '4k7' }, choices: { wave: 'triangle' } });
assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(good.values), ['vin', 'r1']);
assert.deepEqual(plain(sanitizeECalcLaunch({ page: 'ohms_law' })), { page: 'ohms_law', values: {}, choices: {} });
assert.deepEqual(plain(sanitizeECalcLaunch({ page: 'ohms_law', values: [], choices: 'x' })), { page: 'ohms_law', values: {}, choices: {} });

// No page, no launch.
for (const bad of [null, undefined, 'x', 3, [], {}, { page: 7 }, { page: '' }, { page: 'Voltage' }, { page: '1abc' }, { page: '../x' }, { page: 'a-b' }, { page: 'a b' }, { page: '_x' }, { page: 'a'.repeat(65) }]) {
  assert.equal(sanitizeECalcLaunch(bad), null, JSON.stringify(bad));
}
assert.equal(sanitizeECalcLaunch({ page: 'a'.repeat(64) }).page.length, 64);

// Names: lower-case ids that start with a letter, at most 32 characters.
const names = sanitizeECalcLaunch(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify({ page: 'x', values: { vin: '1', Vin: '2', '1a': '3', 'a-b': '4', ['a'.repeat(32)]: '5', ['a'.repeat(33)]: '6', '': '7', ok_1: '8' } })));
assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(names.values), ['vin', 'a'.repeat(32), 'ok_1']);

// Values: strings of at most 256 characters; nothing else.
const vals = sanitizeECalcLaunch({ page: 'x', values: { a: 'x'.repeat(256), b: 'x'.repeat(257), c: 5, d: null, e: { f: 1 }, f: ['1'], g: true, h: '' } });
assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(vals.values), ['a', 'h']);

// Choices: the option is an id as well.
const ch = sanitizeECalcLaunch({ page: 'x', choices: { wave: 'triangle', mode: 'Fast', kind: 'a'.repeat(33), n: 4, ok: 'a'.repeat(32) } });
assert.deepEqual(plain(ch.choices), { wave: 'triangle', ok: 'a'.repeat(32) });

// At most 32 of each, the first ones.
const many = {};
for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) many['v' + i] = 'o' + i;
const cut = sanitizeECalcLaunch({ page: 'x', values: many, choices: many });
assert.equal(Object.keys(cut.values).length, 32);
assert.equal(Object.keys(cut.values)[31], 'v31');
assert.equal(Object.keys(cut.choices).length, 32);

// A hostile key neither pollutes the prototype nor survives.
const hostile = sanitizeECalcLaunch(JSON.parse('{"page":"x","values":{"__proto__":"x","constructor":"y","vin":"1"},"choices":{"__proto__":"x"}}'));
assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(hostile.values), ['constructor', 'vin']);
assert.equal(Object.keys(hostile.choices).length, 0);
assert.equal(({}).vin, undefined);
assert.equal(Object.getPrototypeOf(hostile.values), Object.prototype);
console.log('ok');
`
	if err := os.WriteFile(runner, []byte(script), 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	out, err := exec.Command(node, runner, snippet).CombinedOutput()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("node check failed: %v\n%s", err, out)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(string(out), "ok") {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected output: %s", out)
	}
}
```

```javascript
    // The launch payload of the agent tool ecalc: a calculator id, variable values as raw text and choice options. It
    // comes from a model, so it is rebuilt here from checked parts and ECalc still ignores ids it does not know. Ids start
    // with a letter like the catalog's (which also keeps "__proto__" out), at most 32 values and 32 choices of at most

    const ECALC_LAUNCH_PAGE = /^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$/;
    const ECALC_LAUNCH_NAME = /^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$/;
    function sanitizeECalcLaunchPairs(raw, valueLimit, valuePattern) {
        const out = {};
        if (!raw || typeof raw !== 'object' || Array.isArray(raw)) return out;
        let count = 0;
        for (const name of Object.keys(raw)) {
            if (count >= 32) break;
            const value = raw[name];
            if (!ECALC_LAUNCH_NAME.test(name) || typeof value !== 'string' || value.length > valueLimit) continue;
            if (valuePattern && !valuePattern.test(value)) continue;
            out[name] = value;
            count++;
        }
        return out;
    }
    function sanitizeECalcLaunch(raw) {
        if (!raw || typeof raw !== 'object' || typeof raw.page !== 'string' || !ECALC_LAUNCH_PAGE.test(raw.page)) return null;
        return {
            page: raw.page,
            values: sanitizeECalcLaunchPairs(raw.values, 256, null),
            choices: sanitizeECalcLaunchPairs(raw.choices, 32, ECALC_LAUNCH_NAME)
        };
    }

        if (desktopEventAlreadyHandled(event.id)) return;
```

### Task B7: Browser test of the bridge and the pre-filled pages

**Runs after B6 and after Part U** (`ECalcApp.launch` and `ctx.launch`). The desktop core needs no further change for a new window: `renderAppContent` in `menus-and-routing.js` already hands the whole window context to `ECalcApp.render` (`Object.assign({}, context || {}, { esc, api, t })`), so `launch.launch` set by B6 arrives as `ctx.launch`; the test proves it.

The test reuses the fixture shell of `TestDesktopECalcBrowser` (German desktop, real catalog route) with `handleDesktopEvent` exported, wraps `ECalcApp.render` and `ECalcApp.launch` to record what they receive and sends the JSON text of the events the tool emits. It checks, with the real Part U app:

- the first event opens a window, the payload arrives as `ctx.launch` with the values in the order sent, and the page is pre-filled: `vin=12 V`, `r1=4,7 kΩ` (decimal comma), `r2` at its default `2,2 kΩ`, `vout` computed `3,826 V`;
- the second event reaches `ECalcApp.launch` of the open window, opens no second window and switches the page to Ohm's law with `u=5 V`, `i=10 mA`, computed `r=500 Ω`, `p=50 mW`;
- a repeated event id is handled once; a bad page id, a missing or non-object `ecalc`, or another app's event never reaches ECalc;
- bad names, non-string and over-long values and a `__proto__` key are cut out of an otherwise good payload, and the page starts from its defaults for the rest (`u=12 V`, `i=2 mA`, `r=6 kΩ`, `p=24 mW`);
- a launch for the open window brings it back to the front when another window (the calculator) is active; a list value pre-fills (`rs=4.7kΩ, 10kΩ`, totals `14,7 kΩ` and `3,197 kΩ`);
- a closed window opens again with a fresh launch (`vin=9 V`, `r1=1 kΩ`, `r2=2 kΩ`, computed `vout=6 V`).

**Files:**
- Create: `ui/desktop_ecalc_launch_browser_test.go`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the browser test**

Create `ui/desktop_ecalc_launch_browser_test.go`:

```go
package ui

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"regexp"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"aurago/internal/desktop"
	"aurago/internal/ecalc"
)

// TestDesktopECalcLaunchBrowser sends the open_app events the agent tool ecalc emits through the real desktop core and
// follows the launch payload: the first event opens a window and the payload reaches ECalcApp.render as ctx.launch, a
// second event for the open window reaches ECalcApp.launch (no second window), everything the sanitizer rejects never
// arrives, a repeated event id is handled once. The fixture shell of TestDesktopECalcBrowser is reused with
// handleDesktopEvent exported; the app's entry points are wrapped to record what they receive.
func TestDesktopECalcLaunchBrowser(t *testing.T) {
	requirePrecisionBrowserSmoke(t)
	catalog, err := ecalc.Default()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	html := regexp.MustCompile(`(?s)<script\b[^>]*>.*?</script>`).ReplaceAllString(readDesktopAssetText(t, "desktop.html"), "")
	html = regexp.MustCompile(`\{\{[^}]*\}\}`).ReplaceAllString(html, "")
	html = strings.Replace(html, "</body>", `<script src="/js/shared/lazy-assets.js"></script><script src="/js/desktop/core/module-loader.js"></script><script src="/ecalc-launch-shell.js"></script><script src="/testdata/aurora-fixture.js"></script></body>`, 1)
	shell := readDesktopAssetText(t, "js/desktop/bundles/main.bundle.js")
	cut := strings.LastIndex(shell, "    ensureDesktopRadialMenuAnchor();")
	if cut < 0 {
		t.Fatal("desktop startup seam missing")
	}
	shell = shell[:cut] + `window.aurora={state,loadIconManifest,applyDesktopSettings,renderIcons,renderStartApps,renderStartButtonIcon,wireShellChromeControls,bindViewportMetrics,handleDesktopKeydown,closeContextMenu,openApp,closeWindow,handleDesktopEvent};})();`

	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	mux.Handle("/", http.FileServer(http.FS(Content)))
	mux.HandleFunc("/fixture", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { fmt.Fprint(w, html) })
	mux.HandleFunc("/ecalc-launch-shell.js", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/javascript")
		fmt.Fprint(w, shell)
	})
	mux.HandleFunc("/ecalc-catalog.json", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		body, _, err := catalog.LocalizedJSON(r.URL.Query().Get("lang"))
		if err != nil {
			http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusInternalServerError)
			return
		}
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		_, _ = w.Write(body)
	})
	mux.HandleFunc("/fixture-words", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		fmt.Fprint(w, readDesktopAssetText(t, "lang/desktop/de.json"))
	})
	mux.HandleFunc("/fixture-apps", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(desktop.BuiltinApps()) })
	server := httptest.NewServer(mux)
	defer server.Close()
	page := newSmokeBrowser(t).MustPage(server.URL + "/fixture").Timeout(90 * time.Second)
	defer page.Close()
	page.MustWaitLoad()
	page.MustSetViewport(1366, 900, 1, false)
	page.MustEval(`async()=>{
		await fixtureReady;
		fixtureTheme('standard');
		const base=window.fetch;
		window.fetch=(url,options)=>String(url).startsWith('/api/ecalc/catalog')
			?base('/ecalc-catalog.json'+String(url).slice('/api/ecalc/catalog'.length))
			:base(url,options);
		await AuraDesktopModules.loadAppAssets('ecalc');
		// Record what the shell hands to the app. A window that is already open reaches launch(windowId, payload),
		// a new one render(host, windowId, ctx) with ctx.launch.
		window.launchLog=[];
		const copy=v=>v===undefined?null:JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(v));
		const app=window.ECalcApp;
		const render=app.render.bind(app);
		app.render=(host,id,ctx)=>{window.launchLog.push({kind:'render',id,launch:copy(ctx.launch),hasLaunchKey:'launch' in ctx});return render(host,id,ctx);};
		const launch=typeof app.launch==='function'?app.launch.bind(app):()=>{};
		app.launch=(id,payload)=>{window.launchLog.push({kind:'launch',id,payload:copy(payload)});return launch(id,payload);};
		window.sendDesktopEvent=json=>aurora.handleDesktopEvent(JSON.parse(json));
	}`)

	wait := func(expr string) {
		t.Helper()
		waitForJSBool(t, page, expr)
	}
	send := func(event map[string]any) {
		t.Helper()
		raw, err := json.Marshal(event)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		page.MustEval(`json=>sendDesktopEvent(json)`, string(raw))
	}
	sendRaw := func(raw string) {
		t.Helper()
		page.MustEval(`json=>sendDesktopEvent(json)`, raw)
	}
	log := func() string { return page.MustEval(`()=>JSON.stringify(window.launchLog)`).Str() }
	windows := func() int {
		return page.MustEval(`()=>document.querySelectorAll('.vd-window[data-app-id="ecalc"]').length`).Int()
	}
	windowID := func() string {
		return page.MustEval(`()=>document.querySelector('.vd-window[data-app-id="ecalc"]').dataset.windowId`).Str()
	}
	// fields reads the fields of the open page as var=text(state) in page order, title the name of the page.
	fields := func() string {
		return page.MustEval(`()=>[...document.querySelectorAll('.ec-field')].map(f=>f.dataset.var+'='+f.querySelector('.ec-input').value+'('+f.dataset.state+')').join(' ')`).Str()
	}
	// derived reads the values of the derived quantities of the page.
	derived := func() string {
		return page.MustEval(`()=>[...document.querySelectorAll('[data-rows="derived"] .ec-row-val')].map(e=>e.textContent).join(' ')`).Str()
	}
	title := func() string { return page.MustEval(`()=>document.querySelector('.ec-title').textContent`).Str() }
	deName := func(calc string) string { return catalog.Calculator(calc).Name["de"] }
	activeWindow := func() string { return page.MustEval(`()=>aurora.state.activeWindowId`).Str() }

	// 1. No window yet: the event opens one and the payload arrives as ctx.launch, values in the order they were sent.
	// The events of the ordered cases are written as text: a Go map would sort the keys, the tool does not.
	sendRaw(`{"id":"evt-1","type":"open_app","payload":{"app_id":"ecalc","ecalc":{"page":"voltage_divider","values":{"vin":"12 V","r1":"4k7"},"choices":{}}}}`)
	wait(`()=>document.querySelectorAll('.vd-window[data-app-id="ecalc"]').length===1 && !!document.querySelector('.ec-page[data-calc]')`)
	id := windowID()
	// The page opens pre-filled. The values are what the agent typed (the shell is German, so the fields show a decimal
	// comma); r2 keeps its default because two values are fewer than the three the divider needs; vout is computed.
	if got := title(); got != deName("voltage_divider") {
		t.Fatalf("the page is %q, want %q", got, deName("voltage_divider"))
	}
	if got := fields(); got != "vin=12 V(input) r1=4,7 kΩ(input) r2=2,2 kΩ(input) vout=3,826 V(computed)" {
		t.Fatalf("the first open shows %s", got)
	}
	if got := log(); !strings.HasPrefix(got, `[{"kind":"render","id":"`+id+`","launch":{"page":"voltage_divider","values":{"vin":"12 V","r1":"4k7"},"choices":{}},"hasLaunchKey":true}`) {
		t.Fatalf("the first open handed over %s", got)
	}

	// 2. The window is open: the next event goes to ECalcApp.launch of that window; no second window opens.
	before := page.MustEval(`()=>window.launchLog.length`).Int()
	sendRaw(`{"id":"evt-2","type":"open_app","payload":{"app_id":"ecalc","ecalc":{"page":"ohms_law","values":{"u":"5 V","i":"10 mA"},"choices":{"wave":"triangle"}}}}`)
	wait(fmt.Sprintf(`()=>window.launchLog.length===%d`, before+1))
	want := `{"kind":"launch","id":"` + id + `","payload":{"page":"ohms_law","values":{"u":"5 V","i":"10 mA"},"choices":{"wave":"triangle"}}}`
	if got := page.MustEval(`()=>JSON.stringify(window.launchLog[window.launchLog.length-1])`).Str(); got != want {
		t.Fatalf("the second event handed over %s, want %s", got, want)
	}
	if n := windows(); n != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("ECalc is single-instance, %d windows are open", n)
	}
	// The open window switched to the calculator of the event with its values: 5 V / 10 mA = 500 ohm, 5 V * 10 mA = 50 mW.
	wait(`()=>document.querySelector('.ec-page')?.dataset.calc==='ohms_law'`)
	if got := title(); got != deName("ohms_law") {
		t.Fatalf("the page is %q, want %q", got, deName("ohms_law"))
	}
	if got := fields(); got != "u=5 V(input) i=10 mA(input) r=500 Ω(computed) p=50 mW(computed)" {
		t.Fatalf("the second event shows %s", got)
	}

	// 3. A repeated event id is handled once.
	send(map[string]any{"id": "evt-2", "type": "open_app", "payload": map[string]any{"app_id": "ecalc", "ecalc": map[string]any{"page": "ohms_law", "values": map[string]string{"u": "9 V"}}}})
	// 4. What the sanitizer rejects never reaches the app: a page id that is no catalog id drops the whole launch ...
	send(map[string]any{"id": "evt-3", "type": "open_app", "payload": map[string]any{"app_id": "ecalc", "ecalc": map[string]any{"page": "Voltage Divider", "values": map[string]string{"vin": "1"}}}})
	send(map[string]any{"id": "evt-4", "type": "open_app", "payload": map[string]any{"app_id": "ecalc"}})
	send(map[string]any{"id": "evt-5", "type": "open_app", "payload": map[string]any{"app_id": "ecalc", "ecalc": "voltage_divider"}})
	// ... and bad names, non-string values, over-long text and a hostile key are cut out of an otherwise good one.
	sendRaw(`{"id":"evt-6","type":"open_app","payload":{"app_id":"ecalc","ecalc":{"page":"ohms_law","values":{"__proto__":"x","Vin":"1","r":"` + strings.Repeat("9", 257) + `","u":5,"i":"2 mA","p":null},"choices":{"wave":"Triangle","mode":"fast_plus"}}}}`)
	// The launch is only taken from an ECalc event, never from another app's.
	send(map[string]any{"id": "evt-7", "type": "open_app", "payload": map[string]any{"app_id": "calculator", "ecalc": map[string]any{"page": "ohms_law"}}})
	wait(fmt.Sprintf(`()=>window.launchLog.length===%d`, before+2))
	want = `{"kind":"launch","id":"` + id + `","payload":{"page":"ohms_law","values":{"i":"2 mA"},"choices":{"mode":"fast_plus"}}}`
	if got := page.MustEval(`()=>JSON.stringify(window.launchLog[window.launchLog.length-1])`).Str(); got != want {
		t.Fatalf("the sanitized event handed over %s, want %s", got, want)
	}
	if n := page.MustEval(`()=>window.launchLog.length`).Int(); n != before+2 {
		t.Fatalf("only the two good events may reach the app, the log is %s", log())
	}
	if n := page.MustEval(`()=>document.querySelectorAll('.vd-window[data-app-id="calculator"]').length`).Int(); n != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("the calculator event must still open the calculator, %d windows", n)
	}
	// Only the given value is taken; the page starts from its defaults for the rest: 12 V / 2 mA = 6 kohm, 12 V * 2 mA = 24 mW.
	if got := fields(); got != "u=12 V(input) i=2 mA(input) r=6 kΩ(computed) p=24 mW(computed)" {
		t.Fatalf("the sanitized event shows %s", got)
	}

	// 5. A launch for the open window brings it to the front: the calculator that evt-7 opened is on top now.
	if activeWindow() == id {
		t.Fatal("the calculator window must be the active one before the next launch")
	}
	sendRaw(`{"id":"evt-9","type":"open_app","payload":{"app_id":"ecalc","ecalc":{"page":"series_parallel","values":{"rs":"4k7, 10k"}}}}`)
	wait(fmt.Sprintf(`()=>window.launchLog.length===%d`, before+3))
	wait(`()=>document.querySelector('.ec-page')?.dataset.calc==='series_parallel'`)
	if activeWindow() != id || windows() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("the launch must focus the open ECalc window %s, the active one is %s (%d ECalc windows)", id, activeWindow(), windows())
	}
	// 4.7k + 10k = 14.7k; 4.7k * 10k / 14.7k = 3197.3 ohm.
	if got, sums := fields(), derived(); got != "rs=4.7kΩ, 10kΩ(input)" || sums != "14,7 kΩ 3,197 kΩ" {
		t.Fatalf("the list launch shows %s and the totals %s", got, sums)
	}

	// 6. A closed window opens again with a fresh launch: 9 V * 2k / (1k + 2k) = 6 V.
	page.MustEval(`id=>aurora.closeWindow(id)`, id)
	wait(`()=>document.querySelectorAll('.vd-window[data-app-id="ecalc"]').length===0`)
	sendRaw(`{"id":"evt-8","type":"open_app","payload":{"app_id":"ecalc","ecalc":{"page":"voltage_divider","values":{"vin":"9 V","r1":"1k","r2":"2k"}}}}`)
	wait(`()=>document.querySelectorAll('.vd-window[data-app-id="ecalc"]').length===1 && document.querySelector('.ec-page')?.dataset.calc==='voltage_divider'`)
	if got := page.MustEval(`()=>JSON.stringify(window.launchLog[window.launchLog.length-1].launch)`).Str(); got != `{"page":"voltage_divider","values":{"vin":"9 V","r1":"1k","r2":"2k"},"choices":{}}` {
		t.Fatalf("the reopened window got %s", got)
	}
	if got := fields(); got != "vin=9 V(input) r1=1 kΩ(input) r2=2 kΩ(input) vout=6 V(computed)" {
		t.Fatalf("the reopened window shows %s", got)
	}
	if errors := page.MustEval(`()=>JSON.stringify(fixtureErrors)`).Str(); errors != "[]" {
		t.Fatal(errors)
	}
}
```

```markdown
### `ecalc`
Electronics calculators from the same catalog and formulas as the ECalc desktop app ([Chapter 32](32-ecalc.md)): Ohm's law, dividers, filters, timers, op-amps, power supplies, RF and standard resistor values. Always available, without a config switch: it computes on an embedded catalog and reads no network or files. The agent finds it through `discover_tools` (search terms such as *electronics calculator*, *Widerstand berechnen*, *Spannungsteiler berechnen*). `search` lists calculators (`id`, name, category and a one-sentence summary; an empty `query` lists the categories); `describe` returns the variables with units and defaults, the choices, `dof`, the solvable input sets, the computed outputs, the checks and the formulas; `calculate` solves from the given `inputs` (a bare number is read in the variable's default unit) and answers SI and formatted values, E-series suggestions for computed resistors (the standard-value combiner lists `combos`: the nearest single value and the best series and parallel pairs), the calculator's warnings and `contradictions` when a redundant value differs from the computed one by more than 1 %; a request that cannot be solved answers `underdetermined` and lists the input sets closest first. `open` shows a calculator in the ECalc app, pre-filled with the given values, and needs the Virtual Desktop, **Allow agent control** and the desktop agent tool (otherwise `policy_denied` with `desktop_unavailable` or `desktop_agent_control_disabled`). A2A requests may search, describe and calculate but not open. Answers are shortened to the inline output limit.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `operation` | string | `search`, `describe`, `calculate` or `open` |
| `query` | string | Topic, part or formula in English or German (`search`; empty lists the categories) |
| `id` | string | Calculator id from `search` (`describe`, `calculate`, `open`) |
| `inputs` | array | `{name, value}` pairs: variable id and the value as typed, for example `4k7`, `12 V`, `25 °C` (`calculate`, `open`) |
| `choices` | array | `{name, option}` pairs for choices such as the waveform (`calculate`, `open`) |
| `eseries` | string | `E3`, `E6`, `E12`, `E24` (default), `E48`, `E96` or `E192` (`calculate`) |
| `limit` | integer | Number of results, 1–25 (default 10; `search`) |
```

```markdown
### `ecalc`
Elektronik-Rechner aus demselben Katalog und mit denselben Formeln wie die Desktop-App ECalc ([Kapitel 32](32-ecalc.md)): Ohmsches Gesetz, Teiler, Filter, Timer, OpAmps, Stromversorgung, HF und Normwerte für Widerstände. Immer verfügbar, ohne Config-Schalter: Das Tool rechnet auf einem eingebetteten Katalog und liest weder Netzwerk noch Dateien. Der Agent findet es über `discover_tools` (Suchbegriffe wie *Elektronik Rechner*, *Widerstand berechnen*, *Spannungsteiler berechnen*). `search` listet Rechner (`id`, Name, Kategorie und ein Satz Zusammenfassung; eine leere `query` listet die Kategorien); `describe` liefert Variablen mit Einheiten und Vorgaben, die Auswahlfelder, `dof`, die lösbaren Eingabekombinationen, die berechneten Ausgaben, die Prüfungen und die Formeln; `calculate` löst aus den angegebenen `inputs` (eine nackte Zahl gilt in der Standardeinheit der Variablen) und antwortet mit SI- und formatierten Werten, E-Reihen-Vorschlägen für berechnete Widerstände (die Normwert-Kombination listet `combos`: den nächsten Einzelwert und die besten Reihen- und Parallelpaare), den Warnungen des Rechners und `contradictions`, wenn ein überzähliger Wert um mehr als 1 % vom berechneten abweicht; eine nicht lösbare Anfrage antwortet mit `underdetermined` und nennt die nächstliegenden Eingabekombinationen zuerst. `open` zeigt einen Rechner in der ECalc-App, mit den Werten vorausgefüllt, und braucht den Virtual Desktop, die Option `allow_agent_control` und das Desktop-Agent-Tool (sonst `policy_denied` mit `desktop_unavailable` oder `desktop_agent_control_disabled`). A2A-Anfragen dürfen suchen, beschreiben und rechnen, aber nichts öffnen. Antworten werden auf das Inline-Ausgabelimit gekürzt.

| Parameter | Typ | Beschreibung |
|-----------|-----|--------------|
| `operation` | string | `search`, `describe`, `calculate` oder `open` |
| `query` | string | Thema, Bauteil oder Formel auf Deutsch oder Englisch (`search`; leer listet die Kategorien) |
| `id` | string | Rechner-ID aus `search` (`describe`, `calculate`, `open`) |
| `inputs` | array | `{name, value}`-Paare: Variablen-ID und der Wert, wie man ihn tippt, zum Beispiel `4k7`, `12 V`, `25 °C` (`calculate`, `open`) |
| `choices` | array | `{name, option}`-Paare für Auswahlfelder wie die Kurvenform (`calculate`, `open`) |
| `eseries` | string | `E3`, `E6`, `E12`, `E24` (Standard), `E48`, `E96` oder `E192` (`calculate`) |
| `limit` | integer | Anzahl der Treffer, 1–25 (Standard 10; `search`) |
```

## Part C1 — Passive calculators (task C1.1)

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal of this part:** the 11 calculators of the category `passive` (capacitive and inductive reactance, series and parallel impedance of RC/RL/RLC, RC time constant with chart, series and parallel capacitors and inductors, capacitor energy, air-core coil by Wheeler, toroid A_L, wire resistance), each with hand-checked vectors, and the eight circuit drawings of the category.

**How this part was made and verified:** every file below was generated from the verified scratch worktree (Part A and Part U applied, the content files uncommitted); the plan text only embeds them. The expected numbers of the vector files come from an independent Python script (`math` formulas written from the cited sources, never the ECalc solver) and every `ref` spells the arithmetic out; the script is `c1-gen/gen_vectors.py` in the drafting scratch folder and is not part of the repository. The drawings were rendered with headless Chrome (a small HTML harness that loads `ecalc-symbols.js` and the schematic file, draws the 128 px field chips at their anchors at 20 and 30 px per grid unit and checks that every wire ends on a pin, every pin is connected and no chip overlaps another chip or the art).

**Environment.** Windows box. Run Go commands with a short backslash `GOTMPDIR` (create the folder once):

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force C:\tmp\go-build-ecalc-p2-c1 | Out-Null
$env:GOTMPDIR = 'C:\tmp\go-build-ecalc-p2-c1'
```

(Git Bash equivalent: `export GOTMPDIR='C:\tmp\go-build-ecalc-p2-c1'`.) Commit messages end with the trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Write the micro sign (U+00B5), the Greek capital omega (U+03A9), φ, τ, ρ, α, Δ, ℓ and the degree sign into the YAML as the characters themselves, never as escapes and never as look-alike code points; the files below already contain them.

**Dependencies.** Part A (dimensions `capacitance`, `inductance`, `frequency`, `time`, `length`, `area`, `temperature`, `tempdiff`, `resistivity`, `tempco`, `ratio`, `angle`, the AWG/degC/degF/mm2/kcmil units, `ceil`, the schema fields `units`, `ignore` and `chart`) and Part U (the ten schematics files, the chart block, the dimmed `ignore` fields) must be applied first. GitNexus: this part only adds new files, it edits no existing function, so no `impact` run is needed.

### Contract deviations

1. **The parallel impedance shows the equivalent parallel reactance X_p = −1/B instead of the susceptance B.** The contract asks for "derived X or B", but `units.yaml` has no siemens dimension and content parts may not add one. X_p has the sign of the inductive/capacitive character (positive: inductive) and is infinite at resonance, where the derived value is shown as "–" (the solver reports a non-finite derived quantity as NaN). The `doc` says so in English and German.
2. **Forward-only calculators** (all inputs, only derived outputs, because an inversion is not meaningful or not unique): `impedance_series` and `impedance_parallel` (dof 4: R, L, C and f; the choice `circuit` only decides which components count and dims the other one through `ignore`), `capacitors_series_parallel` and `inductors_series_parallel` (dof 1, the list). The other seven calculators solve in every direction.
3. **No schematic for `air_coil`, `toroid_al` and `wire_resistance`.** They are geometry and material calculators, not circuits (contract section 3: schematics only for circuits); a coil symbol with dimension arrows would only repeat the field labels. The other eight calculators have one.
4. **`rc_time_constant` models charging and discharging with one formula.** The choice `mode` supplies the constants `ki` (initial voltage as a fraction of V_0) and `kf` (final voltage as a fraction of V_0): charging is `ki = 0, kf = 1`, discharging `ki = 1, kf = 0`. The derived quantities V_i and V_f make the displayed formula the textbook `V_C = V_f + (V_i − V_f) · e^(−t/τ)` without any constant showing up in it. The chart is `{x: t, y: vc, to: "5*r*c", samples: 101}`. Two checks warn about a V_C that no time can reach: check 0 fires when V_C is at or beyond the final voltage (the capacitor only approaches it), check 1 when V_C lies on the far side of V_i (negative time).
5. **`wire_resistance` offers three materials only** (copper, aluminium, silver). The constants (ρ20 in Ω·m, α in 1/K) are: copper 1.7241e-8 and 0.00393 (annealed copper, IEC 60028; 1.7241e-8 is 1/58 Ω·mm²/m rounded), aluminium 2.8264e-8 and 0.00403 (hard-drawn aluminium wire per IEC 60889 (controller check 2026-11-02: the HD 532 S1 text of IEC 60889:1987 and GB/T 17048-2017 give 0.028264 Ω·mm²/m maximum resistivity at 20 °C and a constant-mass temperature coefficient of 0.004 03 /°C); ρ20 is the 61 % IACS value 0.017241 / 0.61 Ω·mm²/m), silver 1.59e-8 and 0.0038 (typical handbook values, CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics). Gold, iron, brass and the resistance alloys were left out because their published values scatter too much to state without a standard. Temperatures are kelvin inside (reference 293.15 K = 20 °C); the derived ΔT (dimension `tempdiff`) lets the displayed formula read `R = ρ20 · (1 + α · ΔT) · ℓ / A` in consistent units.
6. **`air_coil` shows Wheeler's own formula, solves the four directions in SI.** The displayed formula is `L = 1e-6 · N² · r_in² / (9 · r_in + 10 · ℓ_in)` with the derived radius and length in inches (derived `rin`, `lin`), exactly Wheeler's inch/µH form, so the live line can be checked by hand. The rules use the equivalent SI form `L = N² D² / (50800 (9 D + 20 ℓ))` (the vectors prove both agree: the generator asserts the equality for every set) and solve the diameter with the positive root of the quadratic. The check `ℓ < 0.4 D` warns when the coil is shorter than 0.8 radii, outside the range where Wheeler gives about 1 %.
7. **`toroid_al` adds the derived `nw`** (turns rounded up with a tolerance of 1e-6 turns, `ceil(n - 1e-6)`, so that 20.000000000000004 does not become 21).
8. **Engine/UI gaps hit, handled without touching engine files.** (a) The `energy` dimension has no micro prefix, so 1.25 µJ would read 0.00125 mJ; the capacitor energy fields offer `units: [""]` and the default example is 72 mJ. (b) `labelHTML` subscripts everything behind the first underscore, so the derived label of V_C/V_0 is the plain word `level`. (c) The two phase 1 assertions `TestPhaseOneCalculators` (catalog has 12 calculators) and `TestLocalizedJSONLanguagesAndFallback` (12 items) hard-code the size of the basics catalog and fail as soon as any content part is added; they are Part A's files. The assembler must relax them (for example: the first 12 calculators are the basics in this order, and `len(en.Items) >= 12`); the verification below runs the package with `-skip` for exactly these two tests.

`TestCalculatorVectors` walks the catalog, not the vector folder, so the new files are not read yet. Count the passing calculator subtests:

```powershell
go test ./internal/ecalc -count=1 -run TestCalculatorVectors -v 2>&1 | Select-String -Pattern '--- PASS: TestCalculatorVectors/' | Measure-Object | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Count
```

Expected: **12** (the eleven phase 1 calculators and `eseries_combiner`; none of the new ids appears). This is the red state of this task.

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the catalog file**

Create `internal/ecalc/catalog/calculators/passive.yaml` with exactly this content:

```yaml
# Passive-component calculators. Every name is written in all 16 desktop locales; docs, variable names and warnings in
# English and German (other languages fall back to English). Rules are written out for every direction, in the order
# the solver tries them: the first alternative whose variables are all known wins. Calculators without rules
# (impedances, series/parallel lists) are forward-only: an inversion is not meaningful there.

- id: reactance_c
  kind: calculator
  category: passive
  name: {cs: "Kapacitní reaktance", da: "Kapacitiv reaktans", de: "Kapazitiver Blindwiderstand", el: "Χωρητική αντίσταση", en: "Capacitive reactance", es: "Reactancia capacitiva", fr: "Réactance capacitive", hi: "धारितीय प्रतिघात", it: "Reattanza capacitiva", ja: "容量性リアクタンス", nl: "Capacitieve reactantie", no: "Kapasitiv reaktans", pl: "Reaktancja pojemnościowa", pt: "Reatância capacitiva", sv: "Kapacitiv reaktans", zh: "容抗"}
  doc:
    en: "A capacitor opposes an alternating current with the reactance X_C = 1 / (2π × f × C). It falls as the frequency or the capacitance rises: a capacitor blocks DC and passes high frequencies. The current through an ideal capacitor leads the voltage by 90°. Example: 100 nF at 1 kHz has X_C ≈ 1.59 kΩ. ESR, ESL and dielectric losses are ignored."
    de: "Ein Kondensator setzt einem Wechselstrom den Blindwiderstand X_C = 1 / (2π · f · C) entgegen. Er sinkt mit steigender Frequenz oder Kapazität: Ein Kondensator sperrt Gleichstrom und lässt hohe Frequenzen durch. Beim idealen Kondensator eilt der Strom der Spannung um 90° voraus. Beispiel: 100 nF bei 1 kHz haben X_C ≈ 1,59 kΩ. ESR, ESL und dielektrische Verluste bleiben unberücksichtigt."
  tags: [reactance, capacitive reactance, capacitor, xc, impedance, ac, blindwiderstand, kapazitiver blindwiderstand, kondensator, reaktanz, wechselstrom]
  source: "Capacitive reactance X_C = 1/(ωC) with ω = 2πf; P. Horowitz, W. Hill: The Art of Electronics, 3rd ed., ch. 1; C. K. Alexander, M. N. O. Sadiku: Fundamentals of Electric Circuits, ch. 9 (sinusoids and phasors)"
  vars:
    f: {dim: frequency, label: f, name: {en: "Frequency", de: "Frequenz"}, default: "1 kHz"}
    c: {dim: capacitance, label: C, name: {en: "Capacitance", de: "Kapazität"}, default: "100 nF", eseries: true}
    xc: {dim: resistance, label: X_C, name: {en: "Capacitive reactance", de: "Kapazitiver Blindwiderstand"}}
  dof: 2
  rules:
    xc: ["1/(2*pi*f*c)"]
    f: ["1/(2*pi*c*xc)"]
    c: ["1/(2*pi*f*xc)"]
  formula: ["xc = 1 / (2 * pi * f * c)"]
  schematic: reactance_c

- id: reactance_l
  kind: calculator
  category: passive
  name: {cs: "Induktivní reaktance", da: "Induktiv reaktans", de: "Induktiver Blindwiderstand", el: "Επαγωγική αντίσταση", en: "Inductive reactance", es: "Reactancia inductiva", fr: "Réactance inductive", hi: "प्रेरकीय प्रतिघात", it: "Reattanza induttiva", ja: "誘導性リアクタンス", nl: "Inductieve reactantie", no: "Induktiv reaktans", pl: "Reaktancja indukcyjna", pt: "Reatância indutiva", sv: "Induktiv reaktans", zh: "感抗"}
  doc:
    en: "An inductor opposes an alternating current with the reactance X_L = 2π × f × L. It rises with the frequency or the inductance: an inductor passes DC and blocks high frequencies. The current through an ideal inductor lags the voltage by 90°. Example: 10 mH at 1 kHz has X_L ≈ 62.8 Ω. Winding resistance and self-capacitance are ignored."
    de: "Eine Spule setzt einem Wechselstrom den Blindwiderstand X_L = 2π · f · L entgegen. Er steigt mit der Frequenz oder der Induktivität: Eine Spule lässt Gleichstrom durch und sperrt hohe Frequenzen. Beim idealen Induktor eilt der Strom der Spannung um 90° nach. Beispiel: 10 mH bei 1 kHz haben X_L ≈ 62,8 Ω. Wicklungswiderstand und Eigenkapazität bleiben unberücksichtigt."
  tags: [reactance, inductive reactance, inductor, coil, xl, impedance, ac, blindwiderstand, induktiver blindwiderstand, spule, induktivität, reaktanz, wechselstrom]
  source: "Inductive reactance X_L = ωL with ω = 2πf; P. Horowitz, W. Hill: The Art of Electronics, 3rd ed., ch. 1; C. K. Alexander, M. N. O. Sadiku: Fundamentals of Electric Circuits, ch. 9 (sinusoids and phasors)"
  vars:
    f: {dim: frequency, label: f, name: {en: "Frequency", de: "Frequenz"}, default: "1 kHz"}
    l: {dim: inductance, label: L, name: {en: "Inductance", de: "Induktivität"}, default: "10 mH", eseries: true}
    xl: {dim: resistance, label: X_L, name: {en: "Inductive reactance", de: "Induktiver Blindwiderstand"}}
  dof: 2
  rules:
    xl: ["2*pi*f*l"]
    f: ["xl/(2*pi*l)"]
    l: ["xl/(2*pi*f)"]
  formula: ["xl = 2 * pi * f * l"]
  schematic: reactance_l

- id: impedance_series
  kind: calculator
  category: passive
  name: {cs: "Impedance sériového obvodu (RC, RL, RLC)", da: "Impedans, serieforbindelse (RC, RL, RLC)", de: "Impedanz der Reihenschaltung (RC, RL, RLC)", el: "Σύνθετη αντίσταση σε σειρά (RC, RL, RLC)", en: "Series impedance (RC, RL, RLC)", es: "Impedancia en serie (RC, RL, RLC)", fr: "Impédance série (RC, RL, RLC)", hi: "श्रेणी प्रतिबाधा (RC, RL, RLC)", it: "Impedenza serie (RC, RL, RLC)", ja: "直列インピーダンス（RC・RL・RLC）", nl: "Serie-impedantie (RC, RL, RLC)", no: "Impedans i serie (RC, RL, RLC)", pl: "Impedancja szeregowa (RC, RL, RLC)", pt: "Impedância em série (RC, RL, RLC)", sv: "Serieimpedans (RC, RL, RLC)", zh: "串联阻抗（RC、RL、RLC）"}
  doc:
    en: "The impedance of a resistor R in series with an inductor L, a capacitor C or both, at the frequency f. The reactances are X_L = 2π × f × L and X_C = 1 / (2π × f × C); the net reactance is X = X_L − X_C, the magnitude |Z| = √(R² + X²) and the phase φ = arctan(X / R) (positive: inductive, negative: capacitive). Choose the circuit first; the component that is not used is dimmed. At resonance X = 0 and |Z| = R. Example: 100 Ω, 10 mH and 1 µF at 1 kHz give X ≈ −96.3 Ω, |Z| ≈ 138.8 Ω and φ ≈ −43.9°."
    de: "Die Impedanz eines Widerstands R in Reihe mit einer Spule L, einem Kondensator C oder beidem bei der Frequenz f. Die Blindwiderstände sind X_L = 2π · f · L und X_C = 1 / (2π · f · C); der resultierende Blindwiderstand ist X = X_L − X_C, der Betrag |Z| = √(R² + X²) und die Phase φ = arctan(X / R) (positiv: induktiv, negativ: kapazitiv). Zuerst die Schaltung wählen; das nicht benutzte Bauteil wird abgeblendet. Bei Resonanz ist X = 0 und |Z| = R. Beispiel: 100 Ω, 10 mH und 1 µF bei 1 kHz ergeben X ≈ −96,3 Ω, |Z| ≈ 138,8 Ω und φ ≈ −43,9°."
  tags: [impedance, series, rc, rl, rlc, phase, reactance, magnitude, impedanz, reihenschaltung, phasenwinkel, blindwiderstand, betrag, wechselstrom]
  source: "Impedance of series RC, RL and RLC circuits (Z = R + jX, X = ωL − 1/(ωC)); C. K. Alexander, M. N. O. Sadiku: Fundamentals of Electric Circuits, ch. 9 (sinusoids and phasors); P. Horowitz, W. Hill: The Art of Electronics, 3rd ed., ch. 1"
  vars:
    r: {dim: resistance, label: R, name: {en: "Resistance", de: "Widerstand"}, default: "100", eseries: true}
    l: {dim: inductance, label: L, name: {en: "Inductance", de: "Induktivität"}, default: "10 mH", eseries: true}
    c: {dim: capacitance, label: C, name: {en: "Capacitance", de: "Kapazität"}, default: "1 µF", eseries: true}
    f: {dim: frequency, label: f, name: {en: "Frequency", de: "Frequenz"}, default: "1 kHz"}
  choices:
    circuit:
      name: {cs: "Obvod", da: "Kreds", de: "Schaltung", el: "Κύκλωμα", en: "Circuit", es: "Circuito", fr: "Circuit", hi: "परिपथ", it: "Circuito", ja: "回路", nl: "Schakeling", no: "Krets", pl: "Układ", pt: "Circuito", sv: "Krets", zh: "电路"}
      default: rlc
      options:
        rc:
          name: {cs: "RC", da: "RC", de: "RC", el: "RC", en: "RC", es: "RC", fr: "RC", hi: "RC", it: "RC", ja: "RC", nl: "RC", no: "RC", pl: "RC", pt: "RC", sv: "RC", zh: "RC"}
          consts: {ul: 0, uc: 1}
          ignore: [l]
        rl:
          name: {cs: "RL", da: "RL", de: "RL", el: "RL", en: "RL", es: "RL", fr: "RL", hi: "RL", it: "RL", ja: "RL", nl: "RL", no: "RL", pl: "RL", pt: "RL", sv: "RL", zh: "RL"}
          consts: {ul: 1, uc: 0}
          ignore: [c]
        rlc:
          name: {cs: "RLC", da: "RLC", de: "RLC", el: "RLC", en: "RLC", es: "RLC", fr: "RLC", hi: "RLC", it: "RLC", ja: "RLC", nl: "RLC", no: "RLC", pl: "RLC", pt: "RLC", sv: "RLC", zh: "RLC"}
          consts: {ul: 1, uc: 1}
  dof: 4
  derived:
    xl: {dim: resistance, label: X_L, name: {en: "Inductive reactance", de: "Induktiver Blindwiderstand"}, expr: "ul*2*pi*f*l"}
    xc: {dim: resistance, label: X_C, name: {en: "Capacitive reactance", de: "Kapazitiver Blindwiderstand"}, expr: "uc/(2*pi*f*c)"}
    x: {dim: resistance, label: X, name: {en: "Net reactance", de: "Resultierender Blindwiderstand"}, expr: "xl-xc"}
    z: {dim: resistance, label: "|Z|", name: {en: "Impedance magnitude", de: "Impedanzbetrag"}, expr: "sqrt(r^2+x^2)"}
    phi: {dim: angle, label: φ, name: {en: "Phase angle", de: "Phasenwinkel"}, expr: "atan(x/r)", unit: deg, units: [deg, ""]}
  formula: ["x = xl - xc", "z = sqrt(r^2 + x^2)", "phi = atan(x / r)"]
  schematic: impedance_series

- id: impedance_parallel
  kind: calculator
  category: passive
  name: {cs: "Impedance paralelního obvodu (RC, RL, RLC)", da: "Impedans, parallelforbindelse (RC, RL, RLC)", de: "Impedanz der Parallelschaltung (RC, RL, RLC)", el: "Σύνθετη αντίσταση παράλληλα (RC, RL, RLC)", en: "Parallel impedance (RC, RL, RLC)", es: "Impedancia en paralelo (RC, RL, RLC)", fr: "Impédance parallèle (RC, RL, RLC)", hi: "समानांतर प्रतिबाधा (RC, RL, RLC)", it: "Impedenza parallelo (RC, RL, RLC)", ja: "並列インピーダンス（RC・RL・RLC）", nl: "Parallel-impedantie (RC, RL, RLC)", no: "Impedans i parallell (RC, RL, RLC)", pl: "Impedancja równoległa (RC, RL, RLC)", pt: "Impedância em paralelo (RC, RL, RLC)", sv: "Parallellimpedans (RC, RL, RLC)", zh: "并联阻抗（RC、RL、RLC）"}
  doc:
    en: "The impedance of a resistor R in parallel with an inductor L, a capacitor C or both, at the frequency f. The admittance is Y = 1/R + j × B with the susceptance B = 2π × f × C − 1 / (2π × f × L); the magnitude is |Z| = 1 / √((1/R)² + B²) and the phase φ = arctan(R × (1 / (2π × f × L) − 2π × f × C)) (positive: inductive, negative: capacitive). ECalc has no unit for a susceptance, so it shows the equivalent parallel reactance X_p = −1 / B instead; at resonance B = 0, the LC branch is an open circuit and X_p is infinite (shown as –). Choose the circuit first; the component that is not used is dimmed. Example: 100 Ω, 10 mH and 1 µF in parallel at 1 kHz give |Z| ≈ 72.0 Ω and φ ≈ +43.9°."
    de: "Die Impedanz eines Widerstands R parallel zu einer Spule L, einem Kondensator C oder beidem bei der Frequenz f. Die Admittanz ist Y = 1/R + j · B mit dem Blindleitwert B = 2π · f · C − 1 / (2π · f · L); der Betrag ist |Z| = 1 / √((1/R)² + B²) und die Phase φ = arctan(R · (1 / (2π · f · L) − 2π · f · C)) (positiv: induktiv, negativ: kapazitiv). ECalc hat keine Einheit für einen Blindleitwert und zeigt deshalb den äquivalenten Parallelblindwiderstand X_p = −1 / B; bei Resonanz ist B = 0, der LC-Zweig wirkt wie eine Unterbrechung und X_p ist unendlich (angezeigt als –). Zuerst die Schaltung wählen; das nicht benutzte Bauteil wird abgeblendet. Beispiel: 100 Ω, 10 mH und 1 µF parallel bei 1 kHz ergeben |Z| ≈ 72,0 Ω und φ ≈ +43,9°."
  tags: [impedance, parallel, rc, rl, rlc, admittance, susceptance, phase, impedanz, parallelschaltung, admittanz, blindleitwert, phasenwinkel, wechselstrom]
  source: "Impedance of parallel RC, RL and RLC circuits (admittance Y = 1/R + j(ωC − 1/(ωL)), Z = 1/Y); C. K. Alexander, M. N. O. Sadiku: Fundamentals of Electric Circuits, ch. 9 (sinusoids and phasors); P. Horowitz, W. Hill: The Art of Electronics, 3rd ed., ch. 1"
  vars:
    r: {dim: resistance, label: R, name: {en: "Resistance", de: "Widerstand"}, default: "100", eseries: true}
    l: {dim: inductance, label: L, name: {en: "Inductance", de: "Induktivität"}, default: "10 mH", eseries: true}
    c: {dim: capacitance, label: C, name: {en: "Capacitance", de: "Kapazität"}, default: "1 µF", eseries: true}
    f: {dim: frequency, label: f, name: {en: "Frequency", de: "Frequenz"}, default: "1 kHz"}
  choices:
    circuit:
      name: {cs: "Obvod", da: "Kreds", de: "Schaltung", el: "Κύκλωμα", en: "Circuit", es: "Circuito", fr: "Circuit", hi: "परिपथ", it: "Circuito", ja: "回路", nl: "Schakeling", no: "Krets", pl: "Układ", pt: "Circuito", sv: "Krets", zh: "电路"}
      default: rlc

          name: {cs: "RC", da: "RC", de: "RC", el: "RC", en: "RC", es: "RC", fr: "RC", hi: "RC", it: "RC", ja: "RC", nl: "RC", no: "RC", pl: "RC", pt: "RC", sv: "RC", zh: "RC"}
          consts: {ul: 0, uc: 1}
          ignore: [l]
        rl:
          name: {cs: "RL", da: "RL", de: "RL", el: "RL", en: "RL", es: "RL", fr: "RL", hi: "RL", it: "RL", ja: "RL", nl: "RL", no: "RL", pl: "RL", pt: "RL", sv: "RL", zh: "RL"}
          consts: {ul: 1, uc: 0}
          ignore: [c]
        rlc:
          name: {cs: "RLC", da: "RLC", de: "RLC", el: "RLC", en: "RLC", es: "RLC", fr: "RLC", hi: "RLC", it: "RLC", ja: "RLC", nl: "RLC", no: "RLC", pl: "RLC", pt: "RLC", sv: "RLC", zh: "RLC"}
          consts: {ul: 1, uc: 1}
  dof: 4
  derived:
    xp: {dim: resistance, label: X_p, name: {en: "Equivalent parallel reactance", de: "Äquivalenter Parallelblindwiderstand"}, expr: "1/(ul/(2*pi*f*l)-uc*2*pi*f*c)"}
    z: {dim: resistance, label: "|Z|", name: {en: "Impedance magnitude", de: "Impedanzbetrag"}, expr: "1/sqrt(1/r^2+(uc*2*pi*f*c-ul/(2*pi*f*l))^2)"}
    phi: {dim: angle, label: φ, name: {en: "Phase angle", de: "Phasenwinkel"}, expr: "atan(r*(ul/(2*pi*f*l)-uc*2*pi*f*c))", unit: deg, units: [deg, ""]}
  formula: ["z = 1 / sqrt(1 / r^2 + (uc * 2 * pi * f * c - ul / (2 * pi * f * l))^2)", "phi = atan(r * (ul / (2 * pi * f * l) - uc * 2 * pi * f * c))"]
  schematic: impedance_parallel

- id: rc_time_constant
  kind: calculator
  category: passive
  name: {cs: "Časová konstanta RC", da: "RC-tidskonstant", de: "RC-Zeitkonstante", el: "Σταθερά χρόνου RC", en: "RC time constant", es: "Constante de tiempo RC", fr: "Constante de temps RC", hi: "RC समय स्थिरांक", it: "Costante di tempo RC", ja: "RC時定数", nl: "RC-tijdconstante", no: "RC-tidskonstant", pl: "Stała czasowa RC", pt: "Constante de tempo RC", sv: "RC-tidskonstant", zh: "RC时间常数"}
  doc:
    en: "A capacitor C charges or discharges through a resistor R with the time constant τ = R × C. In general V_C = V_f + (V_i − V_f) × e^(−t/τ) with the initial voltage V_i and the final voltage V_f. Charging towards the supply voltage V_0 means V_i = 0 and V_f = V_0, so V_C = V_0 × (1 − e^(−t/τ)); discharging from the initial voltage V_0 means V_i = V_0 and V_f = 0, so V_C = V_0 × e^(−t/τ). After 1 τ the capacitor has covered 63.2 % of the way, after 5 τ 99.3 %. Example: 10 kΩ and 100 µF have τ = 1 s; charging from a 5 V supply, V_C is 3.16 V after 1 s. The chart shows V_C from 0 to 5 τ."
    de: "Ein Kondensator C lädt oder entlädt sich über einen Widerstand R mit der Zeitkonstante τ = R · C. Allgemein gilt V_C = V_f + (V_i − V_f) · e^(−t/τ) mit der Anfangsspannung V_i und der Endspannung V_f. Beim Aufladen auf die Speisespannung V_0 ist V_i = 0 und V_f = V_0, also V_C = V_0 · (1 − e^(−t/τ)); beim Entladen von der Anfangsspannung V_0 ist V_i = V_0 und V_f = 0, also V_C = V_0 · e^(−t/τ). Nach 1 τ hat der Kondensator 63,2 % des Weges zurückgelegt, nach 5 τ 99,3 %. Beispiel: 10 kΩ und 100 µF haben τ = 1 s; beim Aufladen aus einer 5-V-Quelle beträgt V_C nach 1 s 3,16 V. Das Diagramm zeigt V_C von 0 bis 5 τ."
  tags: [rc, time constant, tau, charge, discharge, capacitor, timing, exponential, zeitkonstante, aufladen, entladen, kondensator, ladekurve, entladekurve]
  source: "First-order RC step response V_C(t) = V_f + (V_i − V_f)·e^(−t/RC); P. Horowitz, W. Hill: The Art of Electronics, 3rd ed., ch. 1 (RC circuits); C. K. Alexander, M. N. O. Sadiku: Fundamentals of Electric Circuits, ch. 7 (first-order circuits)"
  vars:
    r: {dim: resistance, label: R, name: {en: "Resistance", de: "Widerstand"}, default: "10k", eseries: true}
    c: {dim: capacitance, label: C, name: {en: "Capacitance", de: "Kapazität"}, default: "100 µF", eseries: true}
    v0: {dim: voltage, label: V_0, name: {en: "Supply or initial voltage", de: "Speise- bzw. Anfangsspannung"}, default: "5 V"}
    t: {dim: time, label: t, name: {en: "Time", de: "Zeit"}, default: "1 s"}
    vc: {dim: voltage, label: V_C, name: {en: "Capacitor voltage", de: "Kondensatorspannung"}}
  choices:
    mode:
      name: {cs: "Děj", da: "Forløb", de: "Vorgang", el: "Διαδικασία", en: "Process", es: "Proceso", fr: "Processus", hi: "प्रक्रिया", it: "Processo", ja: "動作", nl: "Proces", no: "Forløp", pl: "Proces", pt: "Processo", sv: "Förlopp", zh: "过程"}
      default: charge
      options:
        charge:
          name: {cs: "Nabíjení", da: "Opladning", de: "Aufladen", el: "Φόρτιση", en: "Charging", es: "Carga", fr: "Charge", hi: "चार्ज होना", it: "Carica", ja: "充電", nl: "Opladen", no: "Lading", pl: "Ładowanie", pt: "Carga", sv: "Laddning", zh: "充电"}
          consts: {ki: 0, kf: 1}
        discharge:
          name: {cs: "Vybíjení", da: "Afladning", de: "Entladen", el: "Εκφόρτιση", en: "Discharging", es: "Descarga", fr: "Décharge", hi: "डिस्चार्ज होना", it: "Scarica", ja: "放電", nl: "Ontladen", no: "Utlading", pl: "Rozładowanie", pt: "Descarga", sv: "Urladdning", zh: "放电"}
          consts: {ki: 1, kf: 0}
  dof: 4
  rules:
    vc: ["vf+(vi-vf)*exp(-t/(r*c))"]
    v0: ["vc/(kf+(ki-kf)*exp(-t/(r*c)))"]
    t: ["-r*c*ln((vc-vf)/(vi-vf))"]
    r: ["-t/(c*ln((vc-vf)/(vi-vf)))"]
    c: ["-t/(r*ln((vc-vf)/(vi-vf)))"]
  derived:
    tau: {dim: time, label: τ, name: {en: "Time constant", de: "Zeitkonstante"}, expr: "r*c"}
    vi: {dim: voltage, label: V_i, name: {en: "Initial voltage", de: "Anfangsspannung"}, expr: "v0*ki"}
    vf: {dim: voltage, label: V_f, name: {en: "Final voltage", de: "Endspannung"}, expr: "v0*kf"}
    ntau: {dim: number, label: "t / τ", name: {en: "Time in time constants", de: "Zeit in Zeitkonstanten"}, expr: "t/(r*c)"}
    lvl: {dim: ratio, label: "level", name: {en: "Capacitor voltage relative to V_0", de: "Kondensatorspannung bezogen auf V_0"}, expr: "vc/v0", unit: pct, units: [pct, ""]}
  checks:
    - {when: "(vc-vf)/(vi-vf) <= 0", warn: {en: "V_C is at or beyond the final voltage V_f (V_0 when charging, 0 V when discharging). The capacitor only approaches V_f, so no finite time reaches it.", de: "V_C liegt bei oder jenseits der Endspannung V_f (V_0 beim Aufladen, 0 V beim Entladen). Der Kondensator nähert sich V_f nur an, daher erreicht keine endliche Zeit diesen Wert."}}
    - {when: "(vc-vf)/(vi-vf) > 1", warn: {en: "V_C lies on the far side of the initial voltage V_i: the capacitor starts at V_i and moves towards V_f, so this value would need a negative time.", de: "V_C liegt jenseits der Anfangsspannung V_i: Der Kondensator startet bei V_i und bewegt sich auf V_f zu, dieser Wert würde daher eine negative Zeit erfordern."}}
  formula: ["vc = vf + (vi - vf) * exp(-t / tau)", "tau = r * c"]
  chart: {x: t, y: vc, to: "5*r*c", samples: 101}
  schematic: rc_time_constant

- id: capacitors_series_parallel
  kind: calculator
  category: passive
  name: {cs: "Sériové a paralelní zapojení kondenzátorů", da: "Serie- og parallelforbundne kondensatorer", de: "Reihen- und Parallelschaltung von Kondensatoren", el: "Σύνδεση πυκνωτών σε σειρά και παράλληλα", en: "Series and parallel capacitors", es: "Condensadores en serie y en paralelo", fr: "Condensateurs en série et en parallèle", hi: "श्रेणी और समानांतर संधारित्र", it: "Condensatori in serie e in parallelo", ja: "コンデンサの直列・並列接続", nl: "Condensatoren in serie en parallel", no: "Seriekoblede og parallellkoblede kondensatorer", pl: "Kondensatory połączone szeregowo i równolegle", pt: "Condensadores em série e em paralelo", sv: "Seriekopplade och parallellkopplade kondensatorer", zh: "电容串联与并联"}
  doc:
    en: "Capacitors in parallel add up: C_P = C_1 + C_2 + …. Capacitors in series combine like resistors in parallel: 1/C_S = 1/C_1 + 1/C_2 + …, so the total is smaller than the smallest capacitor. In series the voltage divides in inverse proportion to the capacitance; polarised capacitors in series need balancing resistors. Enter the values as a list, for example 4.7µ, 10µ, 22µ."
    de: "Parallel geschaltete Kondensatoren addieren sich: C_P = C_1 + C_2 + …. In Reihe geschaltete Kondensatoren ergeben sich wie parallele Widerstände: 1/C_S = 1/C_1 + 1/C_2 + …, die Gesamtkapazität ist also kleiner als der kleinste Kondensator. In Reihe teilt sich die Spannung umgekehrt proportional zur Kapazität; gepolte Kondensatoren in Reihe brauchen Symmetrierwiderstände. Die Werte als Liste eingeben, zum Beispiel 4,7µ, 10µ, 22µ."
  tags: [capacitor, series, parallel, combination, total capacitance, kondensator, reihenschaltung, parallelschaltung, gesamtkapazität, ersatzkapazität]
  source: "Series and parallel capacitor combination; C. K. Alexander, M. N. O. Sadiku: Fundamentals of Electric Circuits, ch. 6 (capacitors and inductors); P. Horowitz, W. Hill: The Art of Electronics, 3rd ed., ch. 1"
  vars:
    cs: {dim: capacitance, label: C, name: {en: "Capacitors", de: "Kondensatoren"}, list: true, default: ["4.7µ", "10µ", "22µ"]}
  dof: 1
  derived:
    cser: {dim: capacitance, label: C_S, name: {en: "Series capacitance", de: "Reihenkapazität"}, expr: "par(cs)"}
    cpar: {dim: capacitance, label: C_P, name: {en: "Parallel capacitance", de: "Parallelkapazität"}, expr: "sum(cs)"}
  formula: ["cser = par(cs)", "cpar = sum(cs)"]
  schematic: capacitors_series_parallel

- id: inductors_series_parallel
  kind: calculator
  category: passive
  name: {cs: "Sériové a paralelní zapojení cívek", da: "Serie- og parallelforbundne spoler", de: "Reihen- und Parallelschaltung von Spulen", el: "Σύνδεση πηνίων σε σειρά και παράλληλα", en: "Series and parallel inductors", es: "Bobinas en serie y en paralelo", fr: "Bobines en série et en parallèle", hi: "श्रेणी और समानांतर प्रेरक", it: "Induttori in serie e in parallelo", ja: "インダクタの直列・並列接続", nl: "Spoelen in serie en parallel", no: "Seriekoblede og parallellkoblede spoler", pl: "Cewki połączone szeregowo i równolegle", pt: "Indutores em série e em paralelo", sv: "Seriekopplade och parallellkopplade spolar", zh: "电感串联与并联"}
  doc:
    en: "Inductors in series add up: L_S = L_1 + L_2 + …. Inductors in parallel combine like resistors in parallel: 1/L_P = 1/L_1 + 1/L_2 + …, so the total is smaller than the smallest inductor. This holds only while the coils do not couple magnetically; mutual inductance is ignored. Enter the values as a list, for example 1m, 2.2m, 4.7m."
    de: "In Reihe geschaltete Spulen addieren sich: L_S = L_1 + L_2 + …. Parallel geschaltete Spulen ergeben sich wie parallele Widerstände: 1/L_P = 1/L_1 + 1/L_2 + …, die Gesamtinduktivität ist also kleiner als die kleinste Spule. Das gilt nur, solange die Spulen nicht magnetisch gekoppelt sind; die Gegeninduktivität bleibt unberücksichtigt. Die Werte als Liste eingeben, zum Beispiel 1m, 2,2m, 4,7m."
  tags: [inductor, coil, series, parallel, combination, total inductance, spule, induktivität, reihenschaltung, parallelschaltung, gesamtinduktivität, ersatzinduktivität]
  source: "Series and parallel inductor combination (no mutual coupling); C. K. Alexander, M. N. O. Sadiku: Fundamentals of Electric Circuits, ch. 6 (capacitors and inductors); P. Horowitz, W. Hill: The Art of Electronics, 3rd ed., ch. 1"
  vars:
    ls: {dim: inductance, label: L, name: {en: "Inductors", de: "Spulen"}, list: true, default: ["1m", "2.2m", "4.7m"]}
  dof: 1
  derived:
    lser: {dim: inductance, label: L_S, name: {en: "Series inductance", de: "Reiheninduktivität"}, expr: "sum(ls)"}
    lpar: {dim: inductance, label: L_P, name: {en: "Parallel inductance", de: "Parallelinduktivität"}, expr: "par(ls)"}
  formula: ["lser = sum(ls)", "lpar = par(ls)"]
  schematic: inductors_series_parallel

- id: capacitor_energy
  kind: calculator
  category: passive
  name: {cs: "Energie a náboj kondenzátoru", da: "Kondensatorens energi og ladning", de: "Kondensatorenergie und -ladung", el: "Ενέργεια και φορτίο πυκνωτή", en: "Capacitor energy and charge", es: "Energía y carga de un condensador", fr: "Énergie et charge d'un condensateur", hi: "संधारित्र की ऊर्जा और आवेश", it: "Energia e carica di un condensatore", ja: "コンデンサのエネルギーと電荷", nl: "Energie en lading van een condensator", no: "Kondensatorens energi og ladning", pl: "Energia i ładunek kondensatora", pt: "Energia e carga de um condensador", sv: "Kondensatorns energi och laddning", zh: "电容器的能量与电荷"}
  doc:
    en: "The energy stored in a capacitor is E = ½ × C × U² and its charge is Q = C × U; also E = ½ × Q × U = Q² / (2 × C). Any two of the four values determine the other two. Example: 1000 µF at 12 V stores 72 mJ and 12 mC. Large or high-voltage capacitors can keep a dangerous charge long after switch-off: discharge them through a suitable resistor before touching them."
    de: "Die in einem Kondensator gespeicherte Energie ist E = ½ · C · U², seine Ladung Q = C · U; außerdem gilt E = ½ · Q · U = Q² / (2 · C). Je zwei der vier Größen bestimmen die beiden anderen. Beispiel: 1000 µF bei 12 V speichern 72 mJ und 12 mC. Große oder hochspannungsführende Kondensatoren können lange nach dem Abschalten eine gefährliche Ladung behalten: vor dem Berühren über einen geeigneten Widerstand entladen."
  tags: [capacitor, energy, charge, joule, coulomb, stored energy, kondensator, energie, ladung, speicherenergie, flash, blitz]
  source: "Energy stored in a capacitor E = ½CU² and charge Q = CU; C. K. Alexander, M. N. O. Sadiku: Fundamentals of Electric Circuits, ch. 6 (capacitors and inductors); P. Horowitz, W. Hill: The Art of Electronics, 3rd ed., ch. 1"
  vars:
    c: {dim: capacitance, label: C, name: {en: "Capacitance", de: "Kapazität"}, default: "1000 µF", eseries: true}
    u: {dim: voltage, label: U, name: {en: "Voltage", de: "Spannung"}, default: "12 V"}
    e: {dim: energy, label: E, name: {en: "Stored energy", de: "Gespeicherte Energie"}, units: [""]}
    q: {dim: charge, label: Q, name: {en: "Charge", de: "Ladung"}, units: [""]}
  dof: 2
  rules:
    e: ["c*u^2/2", "q*u/2", "q^2/(2*c)"]
    q: ["c*u", "2*e/u", "sqrt(2*e*c)"]
    u: ["q/c", "2*e/q", "sqrt(2*e/c)"]
    c: ["q/u", "2*e/u^2", "q^2/(2*e)"]
  formula: ["e = c * u^2 / 2", "q = c * u"]
  schematic: capacitor_energy

- id: air_coil
  kind: calculator
  category: passive
  name: {cs: "Vzduchová cívka (Wheeler)", da: "Luftspole (Wheeler)", de: "Luftspule (Wheeler)", el: "Πηνίο αέρα (Wheeler)", en: "Air-core coil (Wheeler)", es: "Bobina con núcleo de aire (Wheeler)", fr: "Bobine à air (Wheeler)", hi: "वायु-क्रोड कुंडली (व्हीलर)", it: "Bobina in aria (Wheeler)", ja: "空芯コイル（ウィーラー）", nl: "Luchtspoel (Wheeler)", no: "Luftspole (Wheeler)", pl: "Cewka powietrzna (Wheeler)", pt: "Bobina com núcleo de ar (Wheeler)", sv: "Luftspole (Wheeler)", zh: "空心线圈（惠勒公式）"}
  doc:
    en: "Inductance of a single-layer, close-wound air-core coil (solenoid) by Wheeler's formula: L [µH] = N² × r² / (9 × r + 10 × ℓ), with the mean coil radius r and the winding length ℓ both in inches. In the SI units used here this is L = N² × D² / (50800 × (9 × D + 20 × ℓ)) with the mean diameter D (to the centre of the wire) and the length ℓ in metres. It is accurate to about 1 % for ℓ ≥ 0.8 × r (a coil at least 0.4 diameters long) and becomes rough for shorter coils; it assumes an air core and a wire much thinner than the coil. The wire length is the helix at the mean diameter without leads. Example: 25 turns on a 20 mm diameter, 30 mm long winding give about 6.3 µH."
    de: "Induktivität einer einlagigen, dicht gewickelten Luftspule (Zylinderspule) nach der Formel von Wheeler: L [µH] = N² · r² / (9 · r + 10 · ℓ), mit mittlerem Spulenradius r und Wicklungslänge ℓ jeweils in Zoll. In den hier verwendeten SI-Einheiten lautet sie L = N² · D² / (50800 · (9 · D + 20 · ℓ)) mit dem mittleren Durchmesser D (bis zur Drahtmitte) und der Länge ℓ in Metern. Sie ist für ℓ ≥ 0,8 · r (eine Spule von mindestens 0,4 Durchmessern Länge) auf etwa 1 % genau und wird für kürzere Spulen ungenau; sie setzt einen Luftkern und einen Draht voraus, der viel dünner als die Spule ist. Die Drahtlänge ist die Schraubenlinie auf dem mittleren Durchmesser ohne Anschlussdrähte. Beispiel: 25 Windungen auf einer Wicklung von 20 mm Durchmesser und 30 mm Länge ergeben etwa 6,3 µH."
  tags: [coil, air core, inductor, solenoid, wheeler, turns, single layer, inductance, spule, luftspule, zylinderspule, windungen, induktivität, einlagig]
  source: "H. A. Wheeler: Simple Inductance Formulas for Radio Coils, Proceedings of the IRE, vol. 16, no. 10, October 1928 (single-layer coil L = N²r²/(9r + 10ℓ) in inches and microhenries, accurate to about 1 % for ℓ > 0.8r)"
  vars:
    d: {dim: length, label: D, name: {en: "Mean coil diameter", de: "Mittlerer Spulendurchmesser"}, default: "20 mm", units: ["", in]}
    len: {dim: length, label: ℓ, name: {en: "Winding length", de: "Wicklungslänge"}, default: "30 mm", units: ["", in]}
    n: {dim: number, label: N, name: {en: "Turns", de: "Windungen"}, default: 25}
    l: {dim: inductance, label: L, name: {en: "Inductance", de: "Induktivität"}}
  dof: 3
  rules:
    l: ["n^2*d^2/(50800*(9*d+20*len))"]
    n: ["sqrt(l*50800*(9*d+20*len))/d"]
    len: ["(n^2*d^2/(50800*l)-9*d)/20"]
    d: ["(9*50800*l+sqrt((9*50800*l)^2+80*50800*l*n^2*len))/(2*n^2)"]
  derived:
    rin: {dim: number, label: r_in, name: {en: "Mean radius in inches (Wheeler's unit)", de: "Mittlerer Radius in Zoll (Einheit von Wheeler)"}, expr: "d/0.0508"}
    lin: {dim: number, label: ℓ_in, name: {en: "Winding length in inches (Wheeler's unit)", de: "Wicklungslänge in Zoll (Einheit von Wheeler)"}, expr: "len/0.0254"}
    wire: {dim: length, label: ℓ_w, name: {en: "Wire length (without leads)", de: "Drahtlänge (ohne Anschlüsse)"}, expr: "n*sqrt((pi*d)^2+(len/n)^2)", units: ["", in]}
  checks:
    - {when: "len < 0.4*d", warn: {en: "The coil is shorter than 0.4 × its diameter: Wheeler's formula is only a rough estimate here (it is accurate to about 1 % from a length of 0.8 × the radius).", de: "Die Spule ist kürzer als 0,4 × ihr Durchmesser: Die Formel von Wheeler liefert hier nur einen groben Näherungswert (sie ist ab einer Länge von 0,8 × dem Radius auf etwa 1 % genau)."}}
  formula: ["l = 1e-6 * n^2 * rin^2 / (9 * rin + 10 * lin)"]

- id: toroid_al
  kind: calculator
  category: passive
  name: {cs: "Indukčnost toroidu (A_L)", da: "Toroides induktans (A_L)", de: "Ringkerninduktivität (A_L)", el: "Επαγωγή τοροειδούς πυρήνα (A_L)", en: "Toroid inductance (A_L)", es: "Inductancia de toroide (A_L)", fr: "Inductance d'un tore (A_L)", hi: "टॉरॉयड प्रेरकत्व (A_L)", it: "Induttanza di toroide (A_L)", ja: "トロイダルコアのインダクタンス（A_L）", nl: "Inductantie van een ringkern (A_L)", no: "Toroidspolens induktans (A_L)", pl: "Indukcyjność toroidu (A_L)", pt: "Indutância de toroide (A_L)", sv: "Toroidspolens induktans (A_L)", zh: "环形磁芯电感（A_L）"}
  doc:
    en: "The inductance of a winding on a ferrite or powdered-iron core follows from the inductance factor A_L of the core: L = A_L × N². Data sheets print A_L in nH per turn² (1 nH/N² corresponds to 1 mH per 1000 turns); enter it with the unit prefix, for example 250n for 250 nH. N counts the turns through the centre of the core. A_L holds for small signals below saturation and is stated with a tolerance, so the result is only as exact as the core. N_w is the turn count rounded up to whole turns. Example: A_L = 250 nH and 20 turns give 100 µH."
    de: "Die Induktivität einer Wicklung auf einem Ferrit- oder Eisenpulverkern folgt aus dem Induktivitätsfaktor A_L des Kerns: L = A_L · N². Datenblätter geben A_L in nH pro Windung² an (1 nH/N² entsprechen 1 mH pro 1000 Windungen); mit Einheitenvorsatz eingeben, zum Beispiel 250n für 250 nH. N zählt die Windungen durch die Kernmitte. A_L gilt für kleine Signale unterhalb der Sättigung und ist mit einer Toleranz angegeben, das Ergebnis ist also nur so genau wie der Kern. N_w ist die auf ganze Windungen aufgerundete Windungszahl. Beispiel: A_L = 250 nH und 20 Windungen ergeben 100 µH."
  tags: [toroid, ring core, al value, inductance factor, ferrite, powdered iron, turns, nh per turn squared, ringkern, al-wert, induktivitätsfaktor, windungen, ferrit, eisenpulver]
  source: "Definition of the inductance factor A_L of a magnetic core, L = A_L·N² (A_L in nH/N² as printed in the data sheets of ferrite and powdered-iron core makers)"
  vars:
    al: {dim: inductance, label: A_L, name: {en: "Inductance factor (per turn²)", de: "Induktivitätsfaktor (je Windung²)"}, default: "250 nH"}
    n: {dim: number, label: N, name: {en: "Turns", de: "Windungen"}, default: 20}
    l: {dim: inductance, label: L, name: {en: "Inductance", de: "Induktivität"}}
  dof: 2
  rules:
    l: ["al*n^2"]
    al: ["l/n^2"]
    n: ["sqrt(l/al)"]
  derived:
    nw: {dim: number, label: N_w, name: {en: "Whole turns (rounded up)", de: "Ganze Windungen (aufgerundet)"}, expr: "ceil(n-1e-6)"}
  formula: ["l = al * n^2"]

- id: wire_resistance
  kind: calculator
  category: passive
  name: {cs: "Odpor vodiče", da: "Ledningsmodstand", de: "Leitungswiderstand", el: "Αντίσταση αγωγού", en: "Wire resistance", es: "Resistencia de un conductor", fr: "Résistance d'un fil", hi: "तार का प्रतिरोध", it: "Resistenza di un conduttore", ja: "電線の抵抗", nl: "Draadweerstand", no: "Ledermotstand", pl: "Rezystancja przewodu", pt: "Resistência de um fio", sv: "Ledningsresistans", zh: "导线电阻"}
  doc:
    en: "DC resistance of a straight conductor: R = ρ(T) × ℓ / A with ρ(T) = ρ20 × (1 + α × (T − 20 °C)). ρ20 and the temperature coefficient α are those of the selected material at 20 °C: annealed copper per IEC 60028 (ρ20 = 0.017241 Ω·mm²/m, α = 0.00393 1/K); aluminium per IEC 60889, hard-drawn aluminium wire (ρ20 = 0.028264 Ω·mm²/m, the 61 % IACS value, α = 0.00403 1/K); silver is a typical handbook value. Values of real wires vary with purity and alloy. The cross-section can be entered in mm², AWG (ASTM B258) or kcmil. For a two-wire run use twice the one-way length. The linear temperature model is reliable only in a moderate range around 20 °C. Example: 10 m of 1.5 mm² copper at 20 °C have 0.115 Ω."
    de: "Gleichstromwiderstand eines geraden Leiters: R = ρ(T) · ℓ / A mit ρ(T) = ρ20 · (1 + α · (T − 20 °C)). ρ20 und der Temperaturkoeffizient α sind die des gewählten Materials bei 20 °C: geglühtes Kupfer nach IEC 60028 (ρ20 = 0,017241 Ω·mm²/m, α = 0,00393 1/K); Aluminium nach IEC 60889, hartgezogener Aluminiumdraht (ρ20 = 0,028264 Ω·mm²/m, der Wert von 61 % IACS, α = 0,00403 1/K); Silber ist ein üblicher Tabellenwert. Werte realer Drähte schwanken mit Reinheit und Legierung. Der Querschnitt kann in mm², AWG (ASTM B258) oder kcmil eingegeben werden. Für eine Hin- und Rückleitung die doppelte einfache Länge einsetzen. Das lineare Temperaturmodell gilt nur in einem mäßigen Bereich um 20 °C. Beispiel: 10 m Kupfer mit 1,5 mm² haben bei 20 °C 0,115 Ω."
  tags: [wire, resistance, conductor, copper, aluminium, silver, awg, cross-section, resistivity, temperature coefficient, leitung, leitungswiderstand, draht, kupfer, aluminium, querschnitt, spezifischer widerstand, temperaturkoeffizient]
  source: "R = ρ·ℓ/A with ρ(T) = ρ20·(1 + α·(T − 20 °C)); annealed copper ρ20 = 1/58 Ω·mm²/m (rounded to 0.017241) and α20 = 0.00393 1/K per IEC 60028; aluminium ρ20 = 0.028264 Ω·mm²/m (the 61 % IACS value) and α = 0.00403 1/K per IEC 60889 (hard-drawn aluminium wire for overhead line conductors); silver 1.59 nΩ·m with α ≈ 0.0038 1/K as typical handbook values (e.g. CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics); AWG per ASTM B258"
  vars:
    len: {dim: length, label: ℓ, name: {en: "Length", de: "Länge"}, default: "10 m", units: ["", ft, in]}
    a: {dim: area, label: A, name: {en: "Cross-section", de: "Querschnitt"}, default: "1.5", unit: mm2, units: [mm2, AWG, kcmil, mil2]}
    t: {dim: temperature, label: T, name: {en: "Temperature", de: "Temperatur"}, default: "20", unit: degC, units: [degC, degF, ""]}
    r: {dim: resistance, label: R, name: {en: "Resistance", de: "Widerstand"}}
  choices:
    material:
      name: {cs: "Materiál", da: "Materiale", de: "Material", el: "Υλικό", en: "Material", es: "Material", fr: "Matériau", hi: "सामग्री", it: "Materiale", ja: "材質", nl: "Materiaal", no: "Materiale", pl: "Materiał", pt: "Material", sv: "Material", zh: "材料"}
      default: copper
      options:
        copper:
          name: {cs: "Měď", da: "Kobber", de: "Kupfer", el: "Χαλκός", en: "Copper", es: "Cobre", fr: "Cuivre", hi: "तांबा", it: "Rame", ja: "銅", nl: "Koper", no: "Kobber", pl: "Miedź", pt: "Cobre", sv: "Koppar", zh: "铜"}
          consts: {rho: 1.7241e-8, alpha: 0.00393}
        aluminium:
          name: {cs: "Hliník", da: "Aluminium", de: "Aluminium", el: "Αλουμίνιο", en: "Aluminium", es: "Aluminio", fr: "Aluminium", hi: "एल्यूमीनियम", it: "Alluminio", ja: "アルミニウム", nl: "Aluminium", no: "Aluminium", pl: "Aluminium", pt: "Alumínio", sv: "Aluminium", zh: "铝"}
          consts: {rho: 2.8264e-8, alpha: 0.00403}
        silver:
          name: {cs: "Stříbro", da: "Sølv", de: "Silber", el: "Ασήμι", en: "Silver", es: "Plata", fr: "Argent", hi: "चाँदी", it: "Argento", ja: "銀", nl: "Zilver", no: "Sølv", pl: "Srebro", pt: "Prata", sv: "Silver", zh: "银"}
          consts: {rho: 1.59e-8, alpha: 0.0038}
  dof: 3
  rules:
    r: ["rho*(1+alpha*(t-293.15))*len/a"]
    len: ["r*a/(rho*(1+alpha*(t-293.15)))"]
    a: ["rho*(1+alpha*(t-293.15))*len/r"]
    t: ["293.15+(r*a/(rho*len)-1)/alpha"]
  derived:
    rho20: {dim: resistivity, label: ρ20, name: {en: "Resistivity at 20 °C", de: "Spezifischer Widerstand bei 20 °C"}, expr: "rho", unit: ohmmm2m}
    tcr: {dim: tempco, label: α, name: {en: "Temperature coefficient at 20 °C", de: "Temperaturkoeffizient bei 20 °C"}, expr: "alpha", unit: pctK}
    dt: {dim: tempdiff, label: ΔT, name: {en: "Temperature difference to 20 °C", de: "Temperaturdifferenz zu 20 °C"}, expr: "t-293.15", unit: degC, units: [degC, degF, ""]}
    rho_t: {dim: resistivity, label: ρ(T), name: {en: "Resistivity at the temperature T", de: "Spezifischer Widerstand bei der Temperatur T"}, expr: "rho*(1+alpha*(t-293.15))", unit: ohmmm2m}
  checks:
    - {when: "(t < 223.15) + (t > 423.15)", warn: {en: "The temperature is far from 20 °C (below −50 °C or above 150 °C): the linear temperature model loses accuracy there.", de: "Die Temperatur liegt weit von 20 °C entfernt (unter −50 °C oder über 150 °C): Das lineare Temperaturmodell wird dort ungenau."}}
  formula: ["r = rho20 * (1 + tcr * dt) * len / a"]
```

Coverage of the vectors: every set is solved back from every solvable input set of its calculator, so each rule direction is covered by as many sets as the file has: `reactance_c`, `reactance_l`, `capacitors_series_parallel`, `inductors_series_parallel`, `capacitor_energy` (all six input pairs), `air_coil` and `toroid_al` have four sets each, `rc_time_constant` four per mode, `wire_resistance` three for copper and two each for aluminium and silver; the forward-only `impedance_series` has two sets per circuit option and `impedance_parallel` two for RC, two for RL and three for RLC. On top come 6 to 17 solve vectors per file with every direction solved singly, and error, range and warning vectors: zero and negative inputs, an unreachable capacitor voltage (both checks), a coil outside Wheeler's range (and a length that comes out negative), a temperature outside the linear range, missing inputs.
