## Part C2 — Filters and timers (tasks C2.1 and C2.2)

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal of this part:** the 13 calculators of the categories `filters` (RC low-pass and high-pass, LC resonance, RLC Q and bandwidth, unity-gain Sallen-Key low-pass, twin-T notch, pi and T attenuator) and `timers` (NE555 astable and monostable, crystal load capacitors, frequency/period/duty, PWM average), each with hand-checked vectors, and the eleven circuit drawings of the two categories.

**How this part was made and verified:** every file below was generated from the verified scratch worktree (Part A and Part U applied, the content files uncommitted); the plan text only embeds them. The expected numbers of the vector files come from an independent Python script (`math` formulas written from the cited sources in a different algebraic form than the catalog rules, never the ECalc solver; for example Q = ω0·L/R instead of √(L/C)/R, the phase by `atan2`, the datasheet form f = 1.4427/((R_1 + 2·R_2)·C) for the 555, and a two-port analysis of every attenuator that checks Z_in = Z_0 and the voltage ratio K); the script asserts every redundant relation of a scenario, and every `ref` spells the arithmetic out (`definition` where a closed form gives the value, `hand (independent script)` where the script computed it). The twin-T zero was verified by solving the nodal equations of the network numerically (|H(f_0)| = 0, and H = (1 − x²)/(1 − x² + 4jx) at four more frequencies). A mutation check (one expected value changed) made `TestCalculatorVectors` fail in every direction that uses it.

**Environment.** Windows box. Run Go commands with a short backslash `GOTMPDIR` (create the folder once):

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force C:\tmp\go-build-ecalc-p2-c2 | Out-Null
$env:GOTMPDIR = 'C:\tmp\go-build-ecalc-p2-c2'
```

(Git Bash equivalent: `export GOTMPDIR='C:\tmp\go-build-ecalc-p2-c2'`.) Commit messages end with the trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Write the micro sign (U+00B5), the Greek capital omega (U+03A9), τ, φ, π, √, the degree sign and the minus sign into the YAML as the characters themselves, never as escapes and never as look-alike code points; the files below already contain them.

**Dependencies.** Part A (dimensions `capacitance`, `inductance`, `frequency`, `time`, `angle`, `ratio`, the `units` whitelist) and Part U (the ten schematics files, the `ic` symbol, the field-chip anchoring) must be applied first. GitNexus: this part only adds data files (YAML, JSON vectors, two drawing files) and modifies no existing function, class or method, so no upstream impact analysis applies; before each commit run `node .gitnexus/run.cjs detect-changes --scope all --repo .` from the main checkout and expect only the new files, the regenerated snapshot and the one drawing file of the task.

### Contract deviations

1. **The red step of the TDD order is "the new calculators are not tested yet", not a failure.** `TestCalculatorVectors` walks the calculators of the catalog and reads the vector file of each; a vector file without a calculator is never opened. With the vector files in place and no YAML the new subtests simply do not exist (Step 2 shows that with a `Select-String`). The genuine red runs are the opposite order, YAML without vectors (`TestCalculatorVectors/<id>` fails with `read testdata/vectors/calculators/<id>.json: ... cannot find the file`, seen when the YAML was written first) and the schematics cross-check (Step 5).
2. **Two phase 1 assertions hard-code the basics catalog and fail as soon as any content part is added** (the same as Part C1 reports): `TestPhaseOneCalculators` (`catalog has 25 calculators, want 12` in this worktree) and `TestLocalizedJSONLanguagesAndFallback` (`items 25`). They are Part A's files, so this part does not edit them; the assembler relaxes them once for all content parts (for example: compare only the items of the category `basics`, and `len(en.Items) >= 12`). With both relaxed in a scratch copy the whole package passed; the verification below runs the package with `-skip` for exactly these two tests.
3. **Forward-only calculators: none.** All 13 calculators solve in every direction their rules allow. The three that have a free test input are `rc_lowpass` and `rc_highpass` (the test frequency `f` is an input in every solvable set, dof 3; the gain and phase are derived) and `frequency_period` (dof 2: any two independent values of f, T, D, t_high and t_low, nine sets; f and T alone are not one, because they carry the same information).
4. **`ne555_astable` is a design calculator with dof 3 and 27 solvable input sets.** The variables are R_1, R_2, C, f, t_H, t_L and D (the contract lists f, t_high, t_low and duty as outputs; here they can also be inputs, so that "1 kHz at 60 % with 100 nF" gives both resistors). The constant ln 2 is written `ln(2)` in the rules and the displayed formula; the 0.693 and 1.44 of the datasheet are rounded forms of it and are named in the `doc` (1.44 = 1/ln 2 = 1.4427). The check `D <= 0.5` explains the one input combination a standard 555 cannot realise (R_1 would be zero or negative); the resulting negative R_1 is reported as `range` as well.
5. **`rlc_q_bandwidth` shares one set of rules between the two circuits with the choice constant `s`** (+1 series, −1 parallel): Q = (√(L/C)/R)^s, so the same expression gives √(L/C)/R for the series and R/√(L/C) for the parallel circuit, and BW = f_0/Q holds for both. It solves from 16 of the 20 triples of its six values. Not offered are {L, C, f_0} (f_0 follows from L and C) and {f_0, Q, BW} (BW = f_0/Q), which are dependent for both circuits, and {R, L, BW} and {R, C, BW}: each is dependent for one circuit (series: BW = R/(2π·L); parallel: BW = 1/(2π·R·C)) and independent for the other, and because the rules do not depend on the option they are left out for both. The choice has no `ignore` list (all of R, L, C count in both circuits). One schematic serves both options: the series circuit carries the field chips, the parallel circuit below it is labelled R, L, C (drawings hold no language-dependent words, so there is no "series" or "parallel" caption).
6. **`attenuator_pi` and `attenuator_t` use the voltage ratio K as a derived quantity with four alternatives** (from the attenuation, or from Z_0 with R_p, or from Z_0 with R_s, or from R_s and R_p alone), so all six pairs of Z_0, A, R_s and R_p are solvable. R_s and R_p alone fix both Z_0 and A (R_s/R_p = (K − 1)²/(2K) for both pads). Two checks per pad: A ≤ 0, and the resistor that cannot exist for the pad (pi: R_p ≤ Z_0, T: R_s ≥ Z_0); the resulting values are reported as `range` and `nonfinite` errors as well. The resistors carry `eseries: true` so that the page offers the nearest standard value.
7. **E-series hints on capacitors and inductors.** `eseries: true` is set on the R, C and L variables the user chooses (IEC 60063 defines the preferred values for capacitors and inductors as well as for resistors), not on Z_0, frequencies or times.
8. **Display units.** `units` keeps the dropdowns sensible: the times of the filters and timers offer the automatic prefix only (no min and h), except the pulse width of the monostable, which may be minutes or hours, phase offers ° and rad, amplitude ratios and duty cycles offer % and the plain ratio. The derived labels τ and φ are the characters themselves.
9. **Drawings.** Eleven of the thirteen calculators are circuits and have one (`frequency_period` and `pwm_average` are relations, not circuits). Widths are 24 to 32 grid units (Part U's limit is 33); no symbol was added; the NE555 uses the generic `ic` box with pin labels such as `8 VCC` and `3 OUT` (pin number and the universal pin abbreviation, no translatable words). `twin_t_notch` places the ground symbol sideways of the middle junction so that the two shunt arms meet without a crossing; `sallen_key_lowpass` uses the flipped op-amp (`flip: true`, non-inverting input on top) so that the feedback wire runs below without a crossing. Every drawing was checked by script (every wire end meets a pin, wire or terminal, every pin is connected, every junction of three has a dot, no wire crosses another, no field chip overlaps a drawn path, a part body, a label, a dot or another chip, every chip stays inside the drawing at 20 px per grid unit) and inspected in a headless Chrome render with the chip boxes drawn at their real size.
10. **Source notes** (honest citations: standards and datasheets by number or part, textbooks by book and chapter). Checked by derivation or numerically: every formula (the twin-T zero, the attenuator two-port analysis, the Sallen-Key Q by two algebraic forms). Chapter pointers given from memory and worth a glance by the reviewer: The Art of Electronics, 3rd ed., ch. 1 (RC filters, resonance), ch. 6 (filters, Sallen-Key, twin-T notch), ch. 7 (timers, crystal oscillators); Alexander/Sadiku ch. 14 (frequency response and resonance); the attenuator formulas cite "Reference Data for Engineers, 9th ed. (Newnes), chapter on attenuators" without a chapter number. No application-note number is cited; the NE555 items cite the Texas Instruments NE555/SE555 datasheet by maker and part number only.

```json
    {"inputs": {"rs": 199.36730949974645, "rp": 803.1724877724739}, "expect": {"z0": 600, "att": 6, "k": 1.9952623149688795}, "ref": "hand (independent script): K = 10^(A/20) = 10^(6/20) = 1.99526; R_s = Z_0·(K−1)/(K+1) = 600·0.995262/2.99526 = 199.367 Ω; R_p = 2·Z_0·K/(K²−1) = 2·600·1.99526/2.98107 = 803.172 Ω"},
    {"inputs": {"z0": 50, "att": 0}, "expect": {"k": 1}, "errors": {"rs": "range", "rp": "nonfinite"}, "warnings": [0], "ref": "hand: A = 0 dB gives K = 1; R_s = 50·0/2 = 0 is out of range and R_p = 2·50·1/0 = ∞; the attenuation check fires"},
    {"inputs": {"z0": 50, "rs": 60}, "expect": {"k": -11}, "errors": {"att": "nonfinite", "rp": "range"}, "warnings": [1], "ref": "hand: R_s above Z_0 gives K = (50+60)/(50−60) = −11, a negative ratio; 20·log10(−11) is not a number and R_p = 2·50·(−11)/120 = −9.1667 Ω; the R_s check fires"},
    {"inputs": {"z0": 50}, "expect": {}, "errors": {"att": "undetermined", "rs": "undetermined", "rp": "undetermined"}, "warnings": [], "ref": "one of the two values is missing"}
  ]
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run the vector test and watch it not know the new calculators**
```powershell
go test ./internal/ecalc -count=1 -run TestCalculatorVectors -v | Select-String -Pattern 'PASS: TestCalculatorVectors/(rc_lowpass|rc_highpass|lc_resonance|rlc_q_bandwidth|sallen_key_lowpass|twin_t_notch|attenuator_pi|attenuator_t)'
```

Expected: no output. The test walks the calculators of the catalog, which has none of these yet, so the new vector files are not read (contract deviation 1); the same command in Step 4 prints one `PASS` line per calculator.

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the catalog file**
Create `internal/ecalc/catalog/calculators/filters.yaml` with exactly this content:
```yaml
# Filter calculators. Every name is written in all 16 desktop locales; docs, variable names and warnings in English
# and German (other languages fall back to English). Rules are written out for every direction, in the order the
# solver tries them: the first alternative whose variables are all known wins.

- id: rc_lowpass
  kind: calculator
  category: filters
  name: {cs: "RC dolní propust", da: "RC-lavpasfilter", de: "RC-Tiefpass", el: "Βαθυπερατό φίλτρο RC", en: "RC low-pass filter", es: "Filtro paso bajo RC", fr: "Filtre passe-bas RC", hi: "आरसी निम्न-पास फ़िल्टर", it: "Filtro passa-basso RC", ja: "RCローパスフィルタ", nl: "RC-laagdoorlaatfilter", no: "RC-lavpassfilter", pl: "Filtr dolnoprzepustowy RC", pt: "Filtro passa-baixo RC", sv: "RC-lågpassfilter", zh: "RC低通滤波器"}
  doc:
    en: "A first-order RC low-pass passes low frequencies and attenuates high ones. Cutoff frequency (−3 dB point): f_c = 1 / (2π × R × C). At the test frequency f the amplitude ratio is A_v = 1 / √(1 + (f / f_c)²), the gain is G = 20 × log10(A_v) and the output phase is φ = −arctan(f / f_c) (the output lags). Above f_c the gain falls by 20 dB per decade. Example with the defaults: 10 kΩ and 10 nF give f_c ≈ 1.59 kHz; at 1 kHz the output is 84.7 % of the input (−1.45 dB) and lags by 32.1°. The formulas assume an unloaded output (load resistance much larger than R) and an ideal source."
    de: "Ein RC-Tiefpass erster Ordnung lässt tiefe Frequenzen durch und dämpft hohe. Grenzfrequenz (−3-dB-Punkt): f_c = 1 / (2π · R · C). Bei der Testfrequenz f ist das Amplitudenverhältnis A_v = 1 / √(1 + (f / f_c)²), die Verstärkung G = 20 · log10(A_v) und die Phase φ = −arctan(f / f_c) (der Ausgang eilt nach). Oberhalb von f_c fällt die Verstärkung um 20 dB pro Dekade. Beispiel mit den Standardwerten: 10 kΩ und 10 nF ergeben f_c ≈ 1,59 kHz; bei 1 kHz beträgt die Ausgangsspannung 84,7 % der Eingangsspannung (−1,45 dB) bei 32,1° Nacheilung. Die Formeln gelten für einen unbelasteten Ausgang (Lastwiderstand viel größer als R) und eine ideale Quelle."
  tags: [rc, low-pass, lowpass, filter, cutoff, corner frequency, 3 db, first order, time constant, tiefpass, grenzfrequenz, eckfrequenz, zeitkonstante, filter erster ordnung]
  source: "First-order RC low-pass: f_c = 1/(2πRC), |H| = 1/√(1+(f/f_c)²), φ = −arctan(f/f_c); P. Horowitz, W. Hill: The Art of Electronics, 3rd ed., ch. 1 (RC filters)"
  vars:
    r: {dim: resistance, label: R, name: {en: "Resistor", de: "Widerstand"}, default: "10k", eseries: true}
    c: {dim: capacitance, label: C, name: {en: "Capacitor", de: "Kondensator"}, default: "10n", eseries: true}
    fc: {dim: frequency, label: f_c, name: {en: "Cutoff frequency (−3 dB)", de: "Grenzfrequenz (−3 dB)"}}
    f: {dim: frequency, label: f, name: {en: "Test frequency", de: "Testfrequenz"}, default: "1k"}
  dof: 3
  rules:
    fc: ["1/(2*pi*r*c)"]
    r: ["1/(2*pi*fc*c)"]
    c: ["1/(2*pi*fc*r)"]
  derived:
    tau: {dim: time, label: τ, name: {en: "Time constant R × C", de: "Zeitkonstante R · C"}, expr: "r*c", units: [""]}
    av: {dim: ratio, label: A_v, name: {en: "Amplitude ratio at f", de: "Amplitudenverhältnis bei f"}, expr: "1/sqrt(1+(f/fc)^2)", unit: pct, units: [pct, ""]}
    gain: {dim: gain, label: G, name: {en: "Gain at f", de: "Verstärkung bei f"}, expr: "20*log10(av)"}
    phase: {dim: angle, label: φ, name: {en: "Phase at f", de: "Phase bei f"}, expr: "-atan(f/fc)", unit: deg, units: [deg, ""]}
  formula: ["fc = 1 / (2 * pi * r * c)", "av = 1 / sqrt(1 + (f / fc)^2)", "gain = 20 * log10(av)", "phase = -atan(f / fc)"]
  schematic: rc_lowpass

- id: rc_highpass
  kind: calculator
  category: filters
  name: {cs: "RC horní propust", da: "RC-højpasfilter", de: "RC-Hochpass", el: "Υψιπερατό φίλτρο RC", en: "RC high-pass filter", es: "Filtro paso alto RC", fr: "Filtre passe-haut RC", hi: "आरसी उच्च-पास फ़िल्टर", it: "Filtro passa-alto RC", ja: "RCハイパスフィルタ", nl: "RC-hoogdoorlaatfilter", no: "RC-høypassfilter", pl: "Filtr górnoprzepustowy RC", pt: "Filtro passa-alto RC", sv: "RC-högpassfilter", zh: "RC高通滤波器"}
  doc:
    en: "A first-order RC high-pass blocks low frequencies and passes high ones (a coupling capacitor with the input resistance behind it). Cutoff frequency (−3 dB point): f_c = 1 / (2π × R × C). At the test frequency f the amplitude ratio is A_v = (f / f_c) / √(1 + (f / f_c)²), the gain is G = 20 × log10(A_v) and the output leads the input by φ = arctan(f_c / f). Below f_c the gain falls by 20 dB per decade. Example with the defaults: 10 kΩ and 100 nF give f_c ≈ 159 Hz; at 100 Hz the output is 53.2 % of the input (−5.48 dB) and leads by 57.9°. The formulas assume an ideal source and an unloaded output."
    de: "Ein RC-Hochpass erster Ordnung sperrt tiefe Frequenzen und lässt hohe durch (ein Koppelkondensator mit dem Eingangswiderstand dahinter). Grenzfrequenz (−3-dB-Punkt): f_c = 1 / (2π · R · C). Bei der Testfrequenz f ist das Amplitudenverhältnis A_v = (f / f_c) / √(1 + (f / f_c)²), die Verstärkung G = 20 · log10(A_v) und der Ausgang eilt dem Eingang um φ = arctan(f_c / f) voraus. Unterhalb von f_c fällt die Verstärkung um 20 dB pro Dekade. Beispiel mit den Standardwerten: 10 kΩ und 100 nF ergeben f_c ≈ 159 Hz; bei 100 Hz beträgt die Ausgangsspannung 53,2 % der Eingangsspannung (−5,48 dB) bei 57,9° Voreilung. Die Formeln gelten für eine ideale Quelle und einen unbelasteten Ausgang."
  tags: [rc, high-pass, highpass, filter, cutoff, corner frequency, 3 db, coupling capacitor, first order, hochpass, grenzfrequenz, eckfrequenz, koppelkondensator, filter erster ordnung]
  source: "First-order RC high-pass: f_c = 1/(2πRC), |H| = (f/f_c)/√(1+(f/f_c)²), φ = arctan(f_c/f); P. Horowitz, W. Hill: The Art of Electronics, 3rd ed., ch. 1 (RC filters)"
  vars:
    r: {dim: resistance, label: R, name: {en: "Resistor", de: "Widerstand"}, default: "10k", eseries: true}
    c: {dim: capacitance, label: C, name: {en: "Capacitor", de: "Kondensator"}, default: "100n", eseries: true}
    fc: {dim: frequency, label: f_c, name: {en: "Cutoff frequency (−3 dB)", de: "Grenzfrequenz (−3 dB)"}}
    f: {dim: frequency, label: f, name: {en: "Test frequency", de: "Testfrequenz"}, default: "100"}
  dof: 3
  rules:
    fc: ["1/(2*pi*r*c)"]
    r: ["1/(2*pi*fc*c)"]
    c: ["1/(2*pi*fc*r)"]
  derived:
    tau: {dim: time, label: τ, name: {en: "Time constant R × C", de: "Zeitkonstante R · C"}, expr: "r*c", units: [""]}
    av: {dim: ratio, label: A_v, name: {en: "Amplitude ratio at f", de: "Amplitudenverhältnis bei f"}, expr: "(f/fc)/sqrt(1+(f/fc)^2)", unit: pct, units: [pct, ""]}
    gain: {dim: gain, label: G, name: {en: "Gain at f", de: "Verstärkung bei f"}, expr: "20*log10(av)"}
    phase: {dim: angle, label: φ, name: {en: "Phase at f", de: "Phase bei f"}, expr: "atan(fc/f)", unit: deg, units: [deg, ""]}
  formula: ["fc = 1 / (2 * pi * r * c)", "av = (f / fc) / sqrt(1 + (f / fc)^2)", "gain = 20 * log10(av)", "phase = atan(fc / f)"]
  schematic: rc_highpass

- id: lc_resonance
  kind: calculator
  category: filters
  name: {cs: "Rezonanční obvod LC", da: "LC-svingningskreds", de: "LC-Schwingkreis", el: "Συντονισμός LC", en: "LC resonance", es: "Resonancia LC", fr: "Circuit résonant LC", hi: "एलसी अनुनाद", it: "Risonanza LC", ja: "LC共振回路", nl: "LC-resonantie", no: "LC-resonans", pl: "Rezonans LC", pt: "Ressonância LC", sv: "LC-resonans", zh: "LC谐振"}
  doc:
    en: "An ideal LC circuit resonates at the Thomson frequency f_0 = 1 / (2π × √(L × C)); there the reactances are equal, X_L = X_C = √(L / C) = Z_0, the characteristic impedance. Enter any two of L, C and f_0. Example with the defaults: 100 µH and 1 nF resonate at about 503 kHz (medium-wave band) with Z_0 ≈ 316 Ω. Real coils and capacitors have losses; the RLC calculator gives the quality factor and the bandwidth."
    de: "Ein idealer LC-Kreis schwingt mit der Thomson-Frequenz f_0 = 1 / (2π · √(L · C)); dort sind die Blindwiderstände gleich groß, X_L = X_C = √(L / C) = Z_0, der Kennwiderstand. Zwei der drei Größen L, C und f_0 eingeben. Beispiel mit den Standardwerten: 100 µH und 1 nF schwingen bei etwa 503 kHz (Mittelwellenbereich) mit Z_0 ≈ 316 Ω. Reale Spulen und Kondensatoren haben Verluste; Güte und Bandbreite liefert der RLC-Rechner."
  tags: [lc, resonance, resonant circuit, tank, thomson, oscillator, characteristic impedance, resonanz, schwingkreis, resonanzfrequenz, kennwiderstand, parallelschwingkreis]
  source: "Thomson's resonance formula f_0 = 1/(2π√(LC)) and Z_0 = √(L/C); P. Horowitz, W. Hill: The Art of Electronics, 3rd ed., ch. 1 (resonant circuits); C. K. Alexander, M. N. O. Sadiku: Fundamentals of Electric Circuits, ch. 14 (frequency response, resonance)"
  vars:
    l: {dim: inductance, label: L, name: {en: "Inductor", de: "Spule"}, default: "100µ", eseries: true}
    c: {dim: capacitance, label: C, name: {en: "Capacitor", de: "Kondensator"}, default: "1n", eseries: true}
    f0: {dim: frequency, label: f_0, name: {en: "Resonant frequency", de: "Resonanzfrequenz"}}
  dof: 2
  rules:
    f0: ["1/(2*pi*sqrt(l*c))"]
    l: ["1/((2*pi*f0)^2*c)"]
    c: ["1/((2*pi*f0)^2*l)"]
  derived:
    z0: {dim: resistance, label: Z_0, name: {en: "Characteristic impedance √(L/C)", de: "Kennwiderstand √(L/C)"}, expr: "sqrt(l/c)"}
  formula: ["f0 = 1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(l * c))", "z0 = sqrt(l / c)"]
  schematic: lc_resonance

- id: rlc_q_bandwidth
  kind: calculator
  category: filters
  name: {cs: "Obvod RLC: činitel jakosti a šířka pásma", da: "RLC-kreds: Q-faktor og båndbredde", de: "RLC-Kreis: Güte und Bandbreite", el: "Κύκλωμα RLC: συντελεστής Q και εύρος ζώνης", en: "RLC circuit: Q and bandwidth", es: "Circuito RLC: factor Q y ancho de banda", fr: "Circuit RLC : facteur de qualité et bande passante", hi: "आरएलसी परिपथ: Q गुणांक और बैंडविड्थ", it: "Circuito RLC: fattore Q e larghezza di banda", ja: "RLC回路のQ値と帯域幅", nl: "RLC-kring: Q-factor en bandbreedte", no: "RLC-krets: Q-faktor og båndbredde", pl: "Obwód RLC: dobroć i szerokość pasma", pt: "Circuito RLC: fator Q e largura de banda", sv: "RLC-krets: Q-värde och bandbredd", zh: "RLC电路的Q值与带宽"}
  doc:
    en: "Resonance of a series or a parallel RLC circuit. Both resonate at f_0 = 1 / (2π × √(L × C)). The quality factor is Q = √(L / C) / R for a series circuit (R in series with L and C) and Q = R / √(L / C) for a parallel circuit (R in parallel with L and C, for example a load); the −3 dB bandwidth is BW = f_0 / Q. In the formula the exponent s is +1 for the series and −1 for the parallel circuit. Enter three of the six values; the calculator solves the rest when they determine it (f_0, Q and BW alone do not, because BW = f_0 / Q). Example with the defaults (series circuit): R = 10 Ω, L = 100 µH and C = 1 nF give f_0 ≈ 503 kHz, Q ≈ 31.6 and BW ≈ 15.9 kHz (= R / (2π × L)). For the parallel circuit enter the parallel resistance, for example 10 kΩ, which gives the same Q and BW. A Q below 1 means that the bandwidth is larger than f_0."
    de: "Resonanz eines Reihen- oder Parallel-RLC-Kreises. Beide schwingen bei f_0 = 1 / (2π · √(L · C)). Die Güte ist Q = √(L / C) / R beim Reihenkreis (R in Reihe mit L und C) und Q = R / √(L / C) beim Parallelkreis (R parallel zu L und C, zum Beispiel eine Last); die −3-dB-Bandbreite ist BW = f_0 / Q. In der Formel ist der Exponent s gleich +1 beim Reihen- und −1 beim Parallelkreis. Drei der sechs Werte eingeben; der Rechner bestimmt den Rest, wenn sie ihn festlegen (f_0, Q und BW allein tun das nicht, weil BW = f_0 / Q gilt). Beispiel mit den Standardwerten (Reihenkreis): R = 10 Ω, L = 100 µH und C = 1 nF ergeben f_0 ≈ 503 kHz, Q ≈ 31,6 und BW ≈ 15,9 kHz (= R / (2π · L)). Beim Parallelkreis den Parallelwiderstand eingeben, zum Beispiel 10 kΩ; das ergibt dieselbe Güte und Bandbreite. Ein Q unter 1 bedeutet, dass die Bandbreite größer als f_0 ist."
  tags: [rlc, resonance, quality factor, q factor, q, bandwidth, series resonance, parallel resonance, selectivity, güte, gütefaktor, bandbreite, reihenresonanz, parallelresonanz, schwingkreis, selektivität]
  source: "Series and parallel RLC resonance: f_0 = 1/(2π√(LC)); series Q = √(L/C)/R, parallel Q = R/√(L/C), BW = f_0/Q; C. K. Alexander, M. N. O. Sadiku: Fundamentals of Electric Circuits, ch. 14 (series and parallel resonance); P. Horowitz, W. Hill: The Art of Electronics, 3rd ed., ch. 1"
  vars:
    r: {dim: resistance, label: R, name: {en: "Resistance", de: "Widerstand"}, default: "10", eseries: true}
    l: {dim: inductance, label: L, name: {en: "Inductor", de: "Spule"}, default: "100µ", eseries: true}
    c: {dim: capacitance, label: C, name: {en: "Capacitor", de: "Kondensator"}, default: "1n", eseries: true}
    f0: {dim: frequency, label: f_0, name: {en: "Resonant frequency", de: "Resonanzfrequenz"}}
    q: {dim: number, label: Q, name: {en: "Quality factor", de: "Güte"}}
    bw: {dim: frequency, label: BW, name: {en: "Bandwidth (−3 dB)", de: "Bandbreite (−3 dB)"}}
  choices:
    circuit:
      name: {cs: "Zapojení", da: "Kobling", de: "Schaltung", el: "Συνδεσμολογία", en: "Circuit", es: "Circuito", fr: "Montage", hi: "परिपथ", it: "Circuito", ja: "回路", nl: "Schakeling", no: "Kobling", pl: "Układ", pt: "Circuito", sv: "Koppling", zh: "电路"}
      default: series
      options:
        series:
          name: {cs: "Sériový", da: "Serie", de: "Reihe", el: "Σε σειρά", en: "Series", es: "Serie", fr: "Série", hi: "श्रेणी", it: "Serie", ja: "直列", nl: "Serie", no: "Serie", pl: "Szeregowy", pt: "Série", sv: "Serie", zh: "串联"}
          consts: {s: 1}
        parallel:
          name: {cs: "Paralelní", da: "Parallel", de: "Parallel", el: "Παράλληλο", en: "Parallel", es: "Paralelo", fr: "Parallèle", hi: "समानांतर", it: "Parallelo", ja: "並列", nl: "Parallel", no: "Parallell", pl: "Równoległy", pt: "Paralelo", sv: "Parallell", zh: "并联"}
          consts: {s: -1}
  dof: 3
  rules:
    f0: ["1/(2*pi*sqrt(l*c))", "bw*q"]
    q: ["(sqrt(l/c)/r)^s", "f0/bw"]
    bw: ["f0/q"]
    l: ["1/((2*pi*f0)^2*c)", "c*(r*q^s)^2", "r*q^s/(2*pi*f0)"]
    c: ["1/((2*pi*f0)^2*l)", "l/(r*q^s)^2", "1/(2*pi*f0*r*q^s)"]
    r: ["sqrt(l/c)/q^s"]
  checks:
    - {when: "q < 1", warn: {en: "Q is below 1: the bandwidth is larger than the resonant frequency, the circuit is hardly selective. (For a parallel circuit R is the resistance across the tank.)", de: "Q liegt unter 1: Die Bandbreite ist größer als die Resonanzfrequenz, der Kreis ist kaum selektiv. (Beim Parallelkreis ist R der Widerstand parallel zum Schwingkreis.)"}}
  formula: ["f0 = 1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(l * c))", "q = (sqrt(l / c) / r)^s", "bw = f0 / q"]
  schematic: rlc_q_bandwidth

- id: sallen_key_lowpass
  kind: calculator
  category: filters
  name: {cs: "Sallen-Key dolní propust (zesílení 1)", da: "Sallen-Key-lavpasfilter (forstærkning 1)", de: "Sallen-Key-Tiefpass (Verstärkung 1)", el: "Βαθυπερατό φίλτρο Sallen-Key (κέρδος 1)", en: "Sallen-Key low-pass (unity gain)", es: "Filtro paso bajo Sallen-Key (ganancia 1)", fr: "Filtre passe-bas Sallen-Key (gain unitaire)", hi: "सैलन-की निम्न-पास फ़िल्टर (इकाई लब्धि)", it: "Filtro passa-basso Sallen-Key (guadagno unitario)", ja: "サレンキー・ローパスフィルタ（ゲイン1）", nl: "Sallen-Key-laagdoorlaatfilter (versterking 1)", no: "Sallen-Key-lavpassfilter (forsterkning 1)", pl: "Filtr dolnoprzepustowy Sallen-Key (wzmocnienie 1)", pt: "Filtro passa-baixo Sallen-Key (ganho unitário)", sv: "Sallen-Key-lågpassfilter (förstärkning 1)", zh: "Sallen-Key低通滤波器（单位增益）"}
  doc:
    en: "Second-order active low-pass in the Sallen-Key topology with unity gain (the op-amp is a voltage follower) and two equal resistors R. C_1 is the capacitor from the junction of the two resistors to the output (feedback), C_2 goes from the non-inverting input to ground. f_0 = 1 / (2π × R × √(C_1 × C_2)) and Q = ½ × √(C_1 / C_2). C_1 = 2 × C_2 gives Q = 0.707 (Butterworth, maximally flat); C_1b shows that C_1 for the present C_2. Enter any three independent values. Example with the defaults: R = 10 kΩ, C_1 = 22 nF and C_2 = 10 nF give f_0 ≈ 1.07 kHz and Q ≈ 0.742. The op-amp is assumed ideal; its bandwidth must be much higher than f_0 and the source impedance low."
    de: "Aktiver Tiefpass zweiter Ordnung in der Sallen-Key-Schaltung mit der Verstärkung 1 (der Operationsverstärker ist ein Spannungsfolger) und zwei gleichen Widerständen R. C_1 ist der Kondensator vom Verbindungspunkt der beiden Widerstände zum Ausgang (Rückkopplung), C_2 liegt vom nichtinvertierenden Eingang nach Masse. f_0 = 1 / (2π · R · √(C_1 · C_2)) und Q = ½ · √(C_1 / C_2). C_1 = 2 · C_2 ergibt Q = 0,707 (Butterworth, maximal flach); C_1b zeigt dieses C_1 für das vorhandene C_2. Drei unabhängige Werte eingeben. Beispiel mit den Standardwerten: R = 10 kΩ, C_1 = 22 nF und C_2 = 10 nF ergeben f_0 ≈ 1,07 kHz und Q ≈ 0,742. Der Operationsverstärker gilt als ideal; seine Bandbreite muss deutlich über f_0 liegen und die Quellimpedanz niedrig sein."
  tags: [sallen-key, sallen key, active filter, low-pass, lowpass, second order, butterworth, op-amp, q factor, aktiver filter, tiefpass, filter zweiter ordnung, operationsverstärker, güte]
  source: "Unity-gain Sallen-Key low-pass with equal resistors: f_0 = 1/(2πR√(C_1C_2)), Q = ½√(C_1/C_2), C_1 the feedback capacitor; R. P. Sallen, E. L. Key: A Practical Method of Designing RC Active Filters, IRE Transactions on Circuit Theory, 1955; P. Horowitz, W. Hill: The Art of Electronics, 3rd ed., ch. 6 (filters)"
  vars:
    r: {dim: resistance, label: R, name: {en: "Resistors (both)", de: "Widerstände (beide)"}, default: "10k", eseries: true}
    c1: {dim: capacitance, label: C_1, name: {en: "Feedback capacitor", de: "Rückkopplungskondensator"}, default: "22n", eseries: true}
    c2: {dim: capacitance, label: C_2, name: {en: "Capacitor to ground", de: "Kondensator nach Masse"}, default: "10n", eseries: true}
    f0: {dim: frequency, label: f_0, name: {en: "Natural frequency", de: "Eigenfrequenz"}}
    q: {dim: number, label: Q, name: {en: "Quality factor", de: "Güte"}}
  dof: 3
  rules:
    f0: ["1/(2*pi*r*sqrt(c1*c2))"]
    q: ["0.5*sqrt(c1/c2)"]
    c1: ["4*q^2*c2", "q/(pi*r*f0)"]
    c2: ["c1/(4*q^2)", "1/((2*pi*r*f0)^2*c1)", "1/(4*pi*q*r*f0)"]
    r: ["1/(2*pi*f0*sqrt(c1*c2))"]
  derived:
    c1b: {dim: capacitance, label: C_1b, name: {en: "C_1 for Q = 0.707 (Butterworth)", de: "C_1 für Q = 0,707 (Butterworth)"}, expr: "2*c2"}
  formula: ["f0 = 1 / (2 * pi * r * sqrt(c1 * c2))", "q = 0.5 * sqrt(c1 / c2)", "c1b = 2 * c2"]
  schematic: sallen_key_lowpass

- id: twin_t_notch
  kind: calculator
  category: filters
  name: {cs: "Pásmová zádrž dvojité T", da: "Dobbelt-T-notchfilter", de: "Doppel-T-Sperrfilter", el: "Φίλτρο αποκοπής διπλού Τ", en: "Twin-T notch filter", es: "Filtro de muesca doble T", fr: "Filtre réjecteur double T", hi: "ट्विन-टी नॉच फ़िल्टर", it: "Filtro notch a doppio T", ja: "ツインTノッチフィルタ", nl: "Dubbel-T-notchfilter", no: "Dobbel-T-notchfilter", pl: "Filtr zaporowy podwójne T", pt: "Filtro rejeita-banda duplo T", sv: "Dubbel-T-notchfilter", zh: "双T陷波滤波器"}
  doc:
    en: "Passive twin-T notch (band-stop) filter: two T networks in parallel between input and output, one of two resistors R with a capacitor 2C to ground, the other of two capacitors C with a resistor R/2 to ground. The transfer function has a zero at f_0 = 1 / (2π × R × C), so the output is (ideally) zero there; R/2 and 2C are the shunt parts. Example with the defaults: R = 31.6 kΩ and C = 100 nF give f_0 ≈ 50.4 Hz, a notch for 50 Hz mains hum (shunt parts 15.8 kΩ and 200 nF). The notch is only deep when the parts match closely (use 1 % resistors and matched capacitors). The passive filter has a low Q (a wide notch) and needs a source impedance much lower than R and a load impedance much higher than R."
    de: "Passiver Doppel-T-Sperrfilter (Notch, Bandsperre): zwei T-Glieder parallel zwischen Eingang und Ausgang, das eine aus zwei Widerständen R mit einem Kondensator 2C nach Masse, das andere aus zwei Kondensatoren C mit einem Widerstand R/2 nach Masse. Die Übertragungsfunktion hat eine Nullstelle bei f_0 = 1 / (2π · R · C), dort ist der Ausgang (ideal) null; R/2 und 2C sind die Querglieder. Beispiel mit den Standardwerten: R = 31,6 kΩ und C = 100 nF ergeben f_0 ≈ 50,4 Hz, eine Sperre für 50-Hz-Brummen (Querglieder 15,8 kΩ und 200 nF). Die Sperre ist nur tief, wenn die Bauteile eng zusammenpassen (1-%-Widerstände und gepaarte Kondensatoren verwenden). Das passive Filter hat eine geringe Güte (breite Sperre) und braucht eine Quellimpedanz weit unter R und eine Lastimpedanz weit über R."
  tags: [twin-t, twin t, notch, band-stop, band reject, hum filter, 50 hz, 60 hz, doppel-t, sperrfilter, bandsperre, brummfilter, notch filter]
  source: "Passive twin-T network (arms R-R-2C and C-C-R/2): transmission zero at f_0 = 1/(2πRC), obtained by nodal analysis; filter textbooks, e.g. P. Horowitz, W. Hill: The Art of Electronics, 3rd ed., ch. 6 (filters)"
  vars:
    r: {dim: resistance, label: R, name: {en: "Resistor R", de: "Widerstand R"}, default: "31.6k", eseries: true}
    c: {dim: capacitance, label: C, name: {en: "Capacitor C", de: "Kondensator C"}, default: "100n", eseries: true}
    f0: {dim: frequency, label: f_0, name: {en: "Notch frequency", de: "Sperrfrequenz"}}
  dof: 2
  rules:
    f0: ["1/(2*pi*r*c)"]
    r: ["1/(2*pi*f0*c)"]
    c: ["1/(2*pi*f0*r)"]
  derived:
    rh: {dim: resistance, label: R/2, name: {en: "Shunt resistor R/2", de: "Querwiderstand R/2"}, expr: "r/2"}
    c2x: {dim: capacitance, label: 2C, name: {en: "Shunt capacitor 2C", de: "Querkondensator 2C"}, expr: "2*c"}
  formula: ["f0 = 1 / (2 * pi * r * c)", "rh = r / 2", "c2x = 2 * c"]
  schematic: twin_t_notch

- id: attenuator_pi
  kind: calculator
  category: filters
  name: {cs: "Útlumový článek typu π", da: "π-dæmpeled", de: "Pi-Dämpfungsglied", el: "Εξασθενητής Π", en: "Pi attenuator", es: "Atenuador en pi", fr: "Atténuateur en pi", hi: "पाई एटेन्युएटर", it: "Attenuatore a pi greco", ja: "π型アッテネータ", nl: "Pi-verzwakker", no: "Pi-dempeledd", pl: "Tłumik typu π", pt: "Atenuador em pi", sv: "Pi-dämpsats", zh: "π型衰减器"}
  doc:
    en: "Matched resistive pi attenuator (π pad): one series resistor R_s between two equal shunt resistors R_p. Terminated with Z_0 it presents Z_0 at the other port and attenuates by A dB. With the voltage ratio K = 10^(A / 20): R_p = Z_0 × (K + 1) / (K − 1) and R_s = Z_0 × (K² − 1) / (2K). Enter any two of Z_0, A, R_s and R_p. Example with the defaults: 10 dB in a 50 Ω system need R_s ≈ 71.2 Ω and R_p ≈ 96.2 Ω. The power rating of the resistors must cover the dissipated power; this calculator does not size it."
    de: "Angepasstes Widerstands-Pi-Dämpfungsglied (π-Glied): ein Längswiderstand R_s zwischen zwei gleichen Querwiderständen R_p. Mit Z_0 abgeschlossen zeigt es am anderen Tor Z_0 und dämpft um A dB. Mit dem Spannungsverhältnis K = 10^(A / 20) gilt: R_p = Z_0 · (K + 1) / (K − 1) und R_s = Z_0 · (K² − 1) / (2K). Zwei der Größen Z_0, A, R_s und R_p eingeben. Beispiel mit den Standardwerten: 10 dB in einem 50-Ω-System brauchen R_s ≈ 71,2 Ω und R_p ≈ 96,2 Ω. Die Belastbarkeit der Widerstände muss die umgesetzte Leistung abdecken; der Rechner dimensioniert sie nicht."
  tags: [attenuator, pad, pi attenuator, pi pad, matched, resistive, db, 50 ohm, attenuation, dämpfungsglied, pi-glied, dämpfung, abschwächer, angepasst]
  source: "Matched resistive pi attenuator (image-impedance design): K = 10^(A/20), R_p = Z_0(K+1)/(K−1), R_s = Z_0(K²−1)/(2K); Reference Data for Engineers, 9th ed. (Newnes), chapter on attenuators; formulas checked by two-port analysis"
  vars:
    z0: {dim: resistance, label: Z_0, name: {en: "System impedance", de: "Systemimpedanz"}, default: "50"}
    att: {dim: gain, label: A, name: {en: "Attenuation", de: "Dämpfung"}, default: "10 dB"}
    rs: {dim: resistance, label: R_s, name: {en: "Series resistor", de: "Längswiderstand"}, eseries: true}
    rp: {dim: resistance, label: R_p, name: {en: "Shunt resistors (2×)", de: "Querwiderstände (2×)"}, eseries: true}
  dof: 2
  rules:
    att: ["20*log10(k)"]
    rs: ["z0*(k^2-1)/(2*k)"]
    rp: ["z0*(k+1)/(k-1)"]
    z0: ["rs*2*k/(k^2-1)", "rp*(k-1)/(k+1)"]
  derived:
    k: {dim: number, label: K, name: {en: "Voltage ratio K", de: "Spannungsverhältnis K"}, expr: ["10^(att/20)", "(rp+z0)/(rp-z0)", "rs/z0+sqrt((rs/z0)^2+1)", "(1+rs/rp)+sqrt((1+rs/rp)^2-1)"]}
  checks:
    - {when: "att <= 0", warn: {en: "The attenuation must be greater than 0 dB.", de: "Die Dämpfung muss größer als 0 dB sein."}}
    - {when: "rp <= z0", warn: {en: "R_p must be larger than Z_0 for a pi attenuator; these values do not fit together.", de: "R_p muss bei einem Pi-Glied größer als Z_0 sein; diese Werte passen nicht zusammen."}}
  formula: ["k = 10^(att / 20)", "rp = z0 * (k + 1) / (k - 1)", "rs = z0 * (k^2 - 1) / (2 * k)"]
  schematic: attenuator_pi

- id: attenuator_t
  kind: calculator
  category: filters
  name: {cs: "Útlumový článek typu T", da: "T-dæmpeled", de: "T-Dämpfungsglied", el: "Εξασθενητής Τ", en: "T attenuator", es: "Atenuador en T", fr: "Atténuateur en T", hi: "टी एटेन्युएटर", it: "Attenuatore a T", ja: "T型アッテネータ", nl: "T-verzwakker", no: "T-dempeledd", pl: "Tłumik typu T", pt: "Atenuador em T", sv: "T-dämpsats", zh: "T型衰减器"}
  doc:
    en: "Matched resistive T attenuator (T pad): two equal series resistors R_s with one shunt resistor R_p to ground between them. Terminated with Z_0 it presents Z_0 at the other port and attenuates by A dB. With the voltage ratio K = 10^(A / 20): R_s = Z_0 × (K − 1) / (K + 1) and R_p = 2 × Z_0 × K / (K² − 1). Enter any two of Z_0, A, R_s and R_p. Example with the defaults: 10 dB in a 50 Ω system need R_s ≈ 26.0 Ω and R_p ≈ 35.1 Ω. The power rating of the resistors must cover the dissipated power; this calculator does not size it."
    de: "Angepasstes Widerstands-T-Dämpfungsglied (T-Glied): zwei gleiche Längswiderstände R_s mit einem Querwiderstand R_p nach Masse dazwischen. Mit Z_0 abgeschlossen zeigt es am anderen Tor Z_0 und dämpft um A dB. Mit dem Spannungsverhältnis K = 10^(A / 20) gilt: R_s = Z_0 · (K − 1) / (K + 1) und R_p = 2 · Z_0 · K / (K² − 1). Zwei der Größen Z_0, A, R_s und R_p eingeben. Beispiel mit den Standardwerten: 10 dB in einem 50-Ω-System brauchen R_s ≈ 26,0 Ω und R_p ≈ 35,1 Ω. Die Belastbarkeit der Widerstände muss die umgesetzte Leistung abdecken; der Rechner dimensioniert sie nicht."
  tags: [attenuator, pad, t attenuator, t pad, matched, resistive, db, 50 ohm, attenuation, dämpfungsglied, t-glied, dämpfung, abschwächer, angepasst]
  source: "Matched resistive T attenuator (image-impedance design): K = 10^(A/20), R_s = Z_0(K−1)/(K+1), R_p = 2Z_0K/(K²−1); Reference Data for Engineers, 9th ed. (Newnes), chapter on attenuators; formulas checked by two-port analysis"
  vars:
    z0: {dim: resistance, label: Z_0, name: {en: "System impedance", de: "Systemimpedanz"}, default: "50"}
    att: {dim: gain, label: A, name: {en: "Attenuation", de: "Dämpfung"}, default: "10 dB"}
    rs: {dim: resistance, label: R_s, name: {en: "Series resistors (2×)", de: "Längswiderstände (2×)"}, eseries: true}
    rp: {dim: resistance, label: R_p, name: {en: "Shunt resistor", de: "Querwiderstand"}, eseries: true}
  dof: 2
  rules:
    att: ["20*log10(k)"]
    rs: ["z0*(k-1)/(k+1)"]
    rp: ["2*z0*k/(k^2-1)"]
    z0: ["rs*(k+1)/(k-1)", "rp*(k^2-1)/(2*k)"]
  derived:
    k: {dim: number, label: K, name: {en: "Voltage ratio K", de: "Spannungsverhältnis K"}, expr: ["10^(att/20)", "(z0+rs)/(z0-rs)", "(z0+sqrt(z0^2+rp^2))/rp", "(1+rs/rp)+sqrt((1+rs/rp)^2-1)"]}
  checks:
    - {when: "att <= 0", warn: {en: "The attenuation must be greater than 0 dB.", de: "Die Dämpfung muss größer als 0 dB sein."}}
    - {when: "rs >= z0", warn: {en: "R_s must be smaller than Z_0 for a T attenuator; these values do not fit together.", de: "R_s muss bei einem T-Glied kleiner als Z_0 sein; diese Werte passen nicht zusammen."}}
  formula: ["k = 10^(att / 20)", "rs = z0 * (k - 1) / (k + 1)", "rp = 2 * z0 * k / (k^2 - 1)"]
  schematic: attenuator_t
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the catalog file**
Create `internal/ecalc/catalog/calculators/timers.yaml` with exactly this content:
```yaml
# Timer, oscillator and pulse calculators. Every name is written in all 16 desktop locales; docs, variable names and
# warnings in English and German (other languages fall back to English). Rules are written out for every direction, in
# the order the solver tries them: the first alternative whose variables are all known wins.

- id: ne555_astable
  kind: calculator
  category: timers
  name: {cs: "NE555 astabilní (oscilátor)", da: "NE555 astabil (oscillator)", de: "NE555 astabil (Oszillator)", el: "NE555 ασταθής (ταλαντωτής)", en: "NE555 astable (oscillator)", es: "NE555 astable (oscilador)", fr: "NE555 astable (oscillateur)", hi: "NE555 अस्थायी (ऑसिलेटर)", it: "NE555 astabile (oscillatore)", ja: "NE555 無安定（発振器）", nl: "NE555 astabiel (oscillator)", no: "NE555 astabil (oscillator)", pl: "NE555 astabilny (generator)", pt: "NE555 astável (oscilador)", sv: "NE555 astabil (oscillator)", zh: "NE555 无稳态（振荡器）"}
  doc:
    en: "Astable multivibrator with an NE555 timer: the capacitor charges through R_1 + R_2 up to 2/3 of the supply and discharges through R_2 down to 1/3. The high time is t_H = ln 2 × (R_1 + R_2) × C (ln 2 ≈ 0.693), the low time t_L = ln 2 × R_2 × C, the frequency f = 1 / (t_H + t_L) = 1.44 / ((R_1 + 2 R_2) × C) and the duty cycle D = t_H / (t_H + t_L) = (R_1 + R_2) / (R_1 + 2 R_2), which is always above 50 %. Enter any three independent values (for example f, D and C to design the resistors). Example with the defaults: R_1 = 1 kΩ, R_2 = 68 kΩ and C = 10 nF give about 1.05 kHz at 50.4 % duty cycle (t_H ≈ 478 µs, t_L ≈ 471 µs). With the control pin not driven the result does not depend on the supply voltage; real parts add the tolerances of R and C, leakage and switching delays, so very high frequencies and very small resistors deviate."
    de: "Astabiler Multivibrator mit dem Timer NE555: Der Kondensator lädt sich über R_1 + R_2 bis auf 2/3 der Versorgung auf und entlädt sich über R_2 bis auf 1/3. Die Highzeit ist t_H = ln 2 · (R_1 + R_2) · C (ln 2 ≈ 0,693), die Lowzeit t_L = ln 2 · R_2 · C, die Frequenz f = 1 / (t_H + t_L) = 1,44 / ((R_1 + 2 R_2) · C) und das Tastverhältnis D = t_H / (t_H + t_L) = (R_1 + R_2) / (R_1 + 2 R_2), das stets über 50 % liegt. Drei unabhängige Werte eingeben (zum Beispiel f, D und C, um die Widerstände zu bestimmen). Beispiel mit den Standardwerten: R_1 = 1 kΩ, R_2 = 68 kΩ und C = 10 nF ergeben etwa 1,05 kHz bei 50,4 % Tastverhältnis (t_H ≈ 478 µs, t_L ≈ 471 µs). Bei unbeschaltetem Steuereingang hängt das Ergebnis nicht von der Versorgungsspannung ab; reale Bauteile bringen die Toleranzen von R und C, Leckströme und Schaltverzögerungen mit, sodass sehr hohe Frequenzen und sehr kleine Widerstände abweichen."
  tags: [555, ne555, timer, astable, oscillator, multivibrator, blinker, flasher, frequency, duty cycle, astabil, oszillator, blinkschaltung, rechteckgenerator, tastverhältnis, frequenz]
  source: "NE555 datasheet (Texas Instruments NE555 / SE555 precision timer), astable operation: f = 1.44/((R_A + 2R_B)·C), t_H = ln 2·(R_A + R_B)·C, t_L = ln 2·R_B·C; P. Horowitz, W. Hill: The Art of Electronics, 3rd ed., ch. 7 (timers)"
  vars:
    r1: {dim: resistance, label: R_1, name: {en: "Resistor R_1 (supply to discharge pin)", de: "Widerstand R_1 (Versorgung zu Entladepin)"}, default: "1k", eseries: true}
    r2: {dim: resistance, label: R_2, name: {en: "Resistor R_2 (discharge pin to capacitor)", de: "Widerstand R_2 (Entladepin zu Kondensator)"}, default: "68k", eseries: true}
    c: {dim: capacitance, label: C, name: {en: "Timing capacitor", de: "Zeitkondensator"}, default: "10n", eseries: true}
    f: {dim: frequency, label: f, name: {en: "Frequency", de: "Frequenz"}}
    th: {dim: time, label: t_H, name: {en: "High time", de: "Highzeit"}, units: [""]}
    tl: {dim: time, label: t_L, name: {en: "Low time", de: "Lowzeit"}, units: [""]}
    duty: {dim: ratio, label: D, name: {en: "Duty cycle", de: "Tastverhältnis"}, unit: pct, units: [pct, ""]}
  dof: 3
  rules:
    f: ["1/(th+tl)", "duty/th", "(1-duty)/tl"]
    th: ["ln(2)*(r1+r2)*c", "duty/f", "1/f-tl"]
    tl: ["ln(2)*r2*c", "(1-duty)/f", "1/f-th"]
    duty: ["th/(th+tl)", "th*f"]
    r1: ["th/(ln(2)*c)-r2", "(th-tl)/(ln(2)*c)"]
    r2: ["tl/(ln(2)*c)", "(1/(f*ln(2)*c)-r1)/2"]
    c: ["tl/(ln(2)*r2)", "th/(ln(2)*(r1+r2))", "(th-tl)/(ln(2)*r1)", "1/(f*ln(2)*(r1+2*r2))"]
  derived:
    period: {dim: time, label: T, name: {en: "Period", de: "Periodendauer"}, expr: "1/f", units: [""]}
  checks:
    - {when: "duty <= 0.5", warn: {en: "The duty cycle is not above 50 %: a standard NE555 astable cannot do that (R_1 would be zero or negative). A diode across R_2 allows lower duty cycles.", de: "Das Tastverhältnis liegt nicht über 50 %: Das kann ein normaler NE555-Astabilbetrieb nicht (R_1 wäre null oder negativ). Eine Diode parallel zu R_2 ermöglicht kleinere Tastverhältnisse."}}
  formula: ["th = ln(2) * (r1 + r2) * c", "tl = ln(2) * r2 * c", "f = 1 / (th + tl)", "duty = th / (th + tl)"]
  schematic: ne555_astable

- id: ne555_monostable
  kind: calculator
  category: timers
  name: {cs: "NE555 monostabilní (monostabilní klopný obvod)", da: "NE555 monostabil (monoflop)", de: "NE555 monostabil (Monoflop)", el: "NE555 μονοσταθής (μονοπαλμός)", en: "NE555 monostable (one-shot)", es: "NE555 monoestable", fr: "NE555 monostable", hi: "NE555 मोनोस्टेबल (वन-शॉट)", it: "NE555 monostabile", ja: "NE555 単安定（ワンショット）", nl: "NE555 monostabiel (monoflop)", no: "NE555 monostabil (monoflopp)", pl: "NE555 monostabilny (przerzutnik)", pt: "NE555 monoestável", sv: "NE555 monostabil (monoflop)", zh: "NE555 单稳态（单触发）"}
  doc:
    en: "Monostable (one-shot) with an NE555 timer: a trigger pulse at pin 2 starts the output pulse, during which the capacitor charges through R from 0 up to 2/3 of the supply. The pulse width is t = R × C × ln 3 ≈ 1.0986 × R × C (the datasheet rounds this to 1.1 × R × C). Enter any two of R, C and t. Example with the defaults: 100 kΩ and 10 µF give a pulse of about 1.1 s. The trigger pulse must be shorter than the output pulse; the real width varies with the capacitor tolerance and leakage (use film or low-leakage capacitors for long times)."
    de: "Monostabile Kippstufe (Monoflop) mit dem Timer NE555: Ein Triggerimpuls an Pin 2 startet den Ausgangsimpuls, während dem sich der Kondensator über R von 0 bis auf 2/3 der Versorgung auflädt. Die Impulsbreite ist t = R · C · ln 3 ≈ 1,0986 · R · C (das Datenblatt rundet auf 1,1 · R · C). Zwei der Größen R, C und t eingeben. Beispiel mit den Standardwerten: 100 kΩ und 10 µF ergeben einen Impuls von etwa 1,1 s. Der Triggerimpuls muss kürzer als der Ausgangsimpuls sein; die reale Breite schwankt mit der Kondensatortoleranz und dem Leckstrom (für lange Zeiten Folien- oder verlustarme Kondensatoren verwenden)."
  tags: [555, ne555, timer, monostable, one-shot, one shot, pulse, delay, monoflop, monostabil, impuls, verzögerung, zeitglied, pulsbreite]
  source: "NE555 datasheet (Texas Instruments NE555 / SE555 precision timer), monostable operation: t_w = 1.1·R_A·C, exactly ln 3·R_A·C (charging from 0 to 2/3 V_CC); P. Horowitz, W. Hill: The Art of Electronics, 3rd ed., ch. 7 (timers)"
  vars:
    r: {dim: resistance, label: R, name: {en: "Timing resistor", de: "Zeitwiderstand"}, default: "100k", eseries: true}
    c: {dim: capacitance, label: C, name: {en: "Timing capacitor", de: "Zeitkondensator"}, default: "10µ", eseries: true}
    t: {dim: time, label: t, name: {en: "Pulse width", de: "Impulsbreite"}}
  dof: 2
  rules:
    t: ["ln(3)*r*c"]
    r: ["t/(ln(3)*c)"]
    c: ["t/(ln(3)*r)"]
  formula: ["t = ln(3) * r * c"]
  schematic: ne555_monostable

- id: crystal_load_caps
  kind: calculator
  category: timers
  name: {cs: "Zatěžovací kondenzátory krystalu", da: "Krystallastkondensatorer", de: "Quarz-Lastkondensatoren", el: "Πυκνωτές φορτίου κρυστάλλου", en: "Crystal load capacitors", es: "Condensadores de carga del cristal", fr: "Condensateurs de charge du quartz", hi: "क्रिस्टल लोड संधारित्र", it: "Condensatori di carico del quarzo", ja: "水晶振動子の負荷容量", nl: "Belastingcondensatoren voor kristal", no: "Lastkondensatorer for krystall", pl: "Kondensatory obciążające rezonator kwarcowy", pt: "Condensadores de carga do cristal", sv: "Lastkondensatorer för kristall", zh: "晶振负载电容"}
  doc:
    en: "Load capacitors for a parallel-resonant quartz crystal in a Pierce oscillator: two capacitors C_1 = C_2 from the crystal pins to ground. The crystal sees the load capacitance C_L = C_1 × C_2 / (C_1 + C_2) + C_stray, where C_stray is the pin, trace and board capacitance (a few pF as a rough estimate, 2 to 5 pF). With C_1 = C_2 = C this gives C = 2 × (C_L − C_stray). Take C_L from the crystal datasheet. Example with the defaults: C_L = 18 pF and C_stray = 4 pF give C_1 = C_2 = 28 pF (use the nearest standard value, 27 pF)."
    de: "Lastkondensatoren für einen parallelresonanten Schwingquarz in einer Pierce-Oszillatorschaltung: zwei Kondensatoren C_1 = C_2 von den Quarzanschlüssen nach Masse. Der Quarz sieht die Lastkapazität C_L = C_1 · C_2 / (C_1 + C_2) + C_stray; C_stray ist die Kapazität von Pin, Leiterbahn und Platine (als grobe Schätzung einige pF, 2 bis 5 pF). Mit C_1 = C_2 = C folgt C = 2 · (C_L − C_stray). C_L dem Datenblatt des Quarzes entnehmen. Beispiel mit den Standardwerten: C_L = 18 pF und C_stray = 4 pF ergeben C_1 = C_2 = 28 pF (den nächsten Normwert verwenden, 27 pF)."
  tags: [crystal, quartz, xtal, load capacitance, load capacitor, pierce oscillator, oscillator, microcontroller, quarz, schwingquarz, lastkapazität, lastkondensator, pierce, oszillator, mikrocontroller]
  source: "Load capacitance of a parallel-resonant crystal in a Pierce oscillator: C_L = C_1·C_2/(C_1 + C_2) + C_stray (series connection of the two capacitors plus stray capacitance); the crystal datasheet states C_L; P. Horowitz, W. Hill: The Art of Electronics, 3rd ed., ch. 7 (crystal oscillators)"
  vars:
    cl: {dim: capacitance, label: C_L, name: {en: "Crystal load capacitance (datasheet)", de: "Lastkapazität des Quarzes (Datenblatt)"}, default: "18p"}
    cs: {dim: capacitance, label: C_stray, name: {en: "Stray capacitance (pins, traces)", de: "Streukapazität (Pins, Leiterbahnen)"}, default: "4p"}
    c: {dim: capacitance, label: "C_1,2", name: {en: "Load capacitor C_1 = C_2 (each)", de: "Lastkondensator C_1 = C_2 (je)"}, eseries: true}
  dof: 2
  rules:
    c: ["2*(cl-cs)"]
    cl: ["c/2+cs"]
    cs: ["cl-c/2"]
  derived:
    cser: {dim: capacitance, label: C_ser, name: {en: "Series combination C_1·C_2/(C_1 + C_2)", de: "Reihenschaltung C_1·C_2/(C_1 + C_2)"}, expr: "c/2"}
  checks:
    - {when: "cs >= cl", warn: {en: "C_stray is not below C_L: the board already provides the load capacitance, no load capacitors are needed (or the crystal needs a lower load capacitance).", de: "C_stray liegt nicht unter C_L: Die Platine liefert die Lastkapazität bereits, Lastkondensatoren entfallen (oder der Quarz braucht eine kleinere Lastkapazität)."}}
  formula: ["cl = c / 2 + cs", "c = 2 * (cl - cs)"]
  schematic: crystal_load_caps

- id: frequency_period
  kind: calculator
  category: timers
  name: {cs: "Frekvence, perioda a střída", da: "Frekvens, periode og dutycycle", de: "Frequenz, Periodendauer und Tastverhältnis", el: "Συχνότητα, περίοδος και κύκλος λειτουργίας", en: "Frequency, period and duty cycle", es: "Frecuencia, periodo y ciclo de trabajo", fr: "Fréquence, période et rapport cyclique", hi: "आवृत्ति, आवर्तकाल और ड्यूटी साइकिल", it: "Frequenza, periodo e duty cycle", ja: "周波数・周期・デューティ比", nl: "Frequentie, periode en duty cycle", no: "Frekvens, periode og driftssyklus", pl: "Częstotliwość, okres i wypełnienie", pt: "Frequência, período e ciclo de trabalho", sv: "Frekvens, period och pulskvot", zh: "频率、周期与占空比"}
  doc:
    en: "Converts between the frequency f, the period T = 1 / f and the duty cycle D of a rectangular signal: t_high = D × T and t_low = T − t_high. Enter any two independent values (the frequency and the period alone do not fix the duty cycle). Example with the defaults: 1 kHz at a duty cycle of 30 % is a period of 1 ms with 300 µs high and 700 µs low."
    de: "Rechnet zwischen der Frequenz f, der Periodendauer T = 1 / f und dem Tastverhältnis D eines Rechtecksignals um: t_high = D · T und t_low = T − t_high. Zwei unabhängige Werte eingeben (Frequenz und Periodendauer allein legen das Tastverhältnis nicht fest). Beispiel mit den Standardwerten: 1 kHz bei 30 % Tastverhältnis sind 1 ms Periodendauer mit 300 µs High und 700 µs Low."
  tags: [frequency, period, duty cycle, duty, pulse width, square wave, rectangular, pwm, hertz, frequenz, periodendauer, tastverhältnis, tastgrad, pulsbreite, rechteck]
  source: "Definitions: frequency f = 1/T (hertz = 1/s, SI Brochure, BIPM) and duty cycle D = t_high/T of a periodic rectangular signal"
  vars:
    f: {dim: frequency, label: f, name: {en: "Frequency", de: "Frequenz"}, default: "1k"}
    t: {dim: time, label: T, name: {en: "Period", de: "Periodendauer"}, units: [""]}
    duty: {dim: ratio, label: D, name: {en: "Duty cycle", de: "Tastverhältnis"}, default: 0.3, unit: pct, units: [pct, ""]}
    th: {dim: time, label: t_high, name: {en: "High time", de: "Highzeit"}, units: [""]}
    tl: {dim: time, label: t_low, name: {en: "Low time", de: "Lowzeit"}, units: [""]}
  dof: 2
  rules:
    f: ["1/t", "duty/th", "(1-duty)/tl"]
    t: ["1/f", "th+tl", "th/duty", "tl/(1-duty)"]
    duty: ["th/t", "1-tl/t", "th/(th+tl)"]
    th: ["duty*t", "t-tl", "tl*duty/(1-duty)"]
    tl: ["(1-duty)*t", "t-th", "th*(1-duty)/duty"]
  checks:
    - {when: "if(duty <= 0, 1, duty >= 1)", warn: {en: "The duty cycle must be between 0 % and 100 %.", de: "Das Tastverhältnis muss zwischen 0 % und 100 % liegen."}}
  formula: ["t = 1 / f", "th = duty * t", "tl = t - th"]

- id: pwm_average
  kind: calculator
  category: timers
  name: {cs: "Střední hodnota PWM", da: "PWM-middelspænding", de: "PWM-Mittelwert", el: "Μέση τάση PWM", en: "PWM average voltage", es: "Tensión media de PWM", fr: "Tension moyenne d'un signal PWM", hi: "PWM औसत वोल्टेज", it: "Tensione media PWM", ja: "PWMの平均電圧", nl: "Gemiddelde PWM-spanning", no: "PWM-middelspenning", pl: "Napięcie średnie PWM", pt: "Tensão média PWM", sv: "PWM-medelspänning", zh: "PWM平均电压"}
  doc:
    en: "Average and RMS value of a rectangular PWM signal that switches between V_low and V_high with the duty cycle D: V_avg = V_low + D × (V_high − V_low) (a low-pass filter, or the inertia of a motor, LED or heater, turns the PWM into this DC voltage) and V_rms = √(D × V_high² + (1 − D) × V_low²) (the heating effect in a resistive load). Enter any three of D, V_high, V_low and V_avg. Example with the defaults: 25 % duty cycle between 0 V and 5 V gives V_avg = 1.25 V and V_rms = 2.5 V."
    de: "Mittelwert und Effektivwert eines Rechteck-PWM-Signals, das mit dem Tastverhältnis D zwischen V_low und V_high wechselt: V_avg = V_low + D · (V_high − V_low) (ein Tiefpass oder die Trägheit von Motor, LED oder Heizung macht daraus diese Gleichspannung) und V_rms = √(D · V_high² + (1 − D) · V_low²) (die Heizwirkung an einer ohmschen Last). Drei der Größen D, V_high, V_low und V_avg eingeben. Beispiel mit den Standardwerten: 25 % Tastverhältnis zwischen 0 V und 5 V ergeben V_avg = 1,25 V und V_rms = 2,5 V."
  tags: [pwm, pulse width modulation, average, mean, rms, duty cycle, dimming, motor speed, pulsweitenmodulation, mittelwert, effektivwert, tastverhältnis, dimmen, drehzahl]
  source: "Average and RMS value of a rectangular two-level waveform over one period (integration of the waveform); P. Horowitz, W. Hill: The Art of Electronics, 3rd ed., ch. 1 (signals)"
  vars:
    duty: {dim: ratio, label: D, name: {en: "Duty cycle", de: "Tastverhältnis"}, default: 0.25, unit: pct, units: [pct, ""]}
    vh: {dim: voltage, label: V_high, name: {en: "High level", de: "High-Pegel"}, default: "5 V"}
    vl: {dim: voltage, label: V_low, name: {en: "Low level", de: "Low-Pegel"}, default: 0}
    vavg: {dim: voltage, label: V_avg, name: {en: "Average voltage", de: "Mittelwert"}}
  dof: 3
  rules:
    vavg: ["vl+duty*(vh-vl)"]
    duty: ["(vavg-vl)/(vh-vl)"]
    vh: ["vl+(vavg-vl)/duty"]
    vl: ["(vavg-duty*vh)/(1-duty)"]
  derived:
    vrms: {dim: voltage, label: V_rms, name: {en: "RMS voltage", de: "Effektivwert"}, expr: "sqrt(duty*vh^2+(1-duty)*vl^2)"}
  checks:
    - {when: "if(duty < 0, 1, duty > 1)", warn: {en: "The duty cycle must be between 0 % and 100 %.", de: "Das Tastverhältnis muss zwischen 0 % und 100 % liegen."}}
  formula: ["vavg = vl + duty * (vh - vl)", "vrms = sqrt(duty * vh^2 + (1 - duty) * vl^2)"]
```

Coverage of the vectors. Every set is solved back from every solvable input set of its calculator, so each rule direction is covered by as many sets as the file has: four sets for every calculator except `rlc_q_bandwidth` (three per circuit option), `ne555_astable` (five), and the solve vectors then solve every direction singly: `rc_lowpass` and `rc_highpass` 9 each (the three input sets twice, plus a negative R, a missing frequency and f = 0), `lc_resonance` 8, `rlc_q_bandwidth` 11 (series and parallel, one warning vector for Q below 1), `sallen_key_lowpass` 18 (every one of the 8 solvable sets, most of them twice), `twin_t_notch` 8, `attenuator_pi` and `attenuator_t` 15 each (all six pairs twice, plus A = 0 dB, the impossible resistor and a missing value), `ne555_astable` 15 (design from f, D and C; from f, D and one resistor; from f, C and one resistor; from times; the 40 % duty case with both the check and the range error), `ne555_monostable` 9, `crystal_load_caps` 9 (including C_stray equal to and above C_L), `frequency_period` 21 (all nine pairs twice, plus D = 120 % and D = 100 %), `pwm_average` 11 (all four triples, D above 100 %, V_high = V_low). The numbers come from `c2-tools/vecgen.py` (independent formulas; scratch, not part of the plan).

Honest limits. The browser tests were not run (the coordinator runs them after assembly). The page was not opened with these items; the drawings were checked by script and render only. Chapter pointers of textbook sources are from memory (contract deviation 10).

## Part C3 — Semiconductors and op-amps (tasks C3.1 and C3.2)

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Part C3 of the phase 2 plan** (`CONTRACT.md` section 3): the 13 content items of the categories `semiconductors` (6) and `opamps` (7), each with its hand-checked vector file, plus the two schematics files. Built and verified in the scratch worktree `wc3` on top of Part A (engine) and Part U (UI); all code blocks below are generated from the verified files, nothing is paraphrased.

**Environment:** Windows, set `GOTMPDIR` to a short backslash path first (for example `set GOTMPDIR=C:\tmp\go-build-ecalc-p2-c3`). Do not commit in a scratch worktree that other sessions merge from; commit only on the real execution branch.

### Contract deviations

1. **Red/green of the vector test.** `TestCalculatorVectors` iterates the calculators of the catalog, so vector files without a calculator are never read and the test cannot fail for them. Steps 2 and 4 of each task therefore count the passing subtests of the new calculators (0, then all of them); the UI test `ECalcSchematic` gives a real red before the drawings exist.
2. **Two phase 1 tests pin the number of basics items** and fail as soon as any content part lands: `TestPhaseOneCalculators` (`internal/ecalc/basics_test.go`, `len(cat.Calculators) != len(want)`) and `TestLocalizedJSONLanguagesAndFallback` (`internal/ecalc/localize_test.go`, `len(en.Items) != 12`). They are Part A's files, so this part does not edit them: the runs below use `-skip 'TestPhaseOneCalculators|TestLocalizedJSONLanguagesAndFallback'`. Suggested fix for the assembly: compare only the items with `Category == "basics"` in the first test (basics.yaml sorts first, the order is stable) and drop the item-count pin from the second.
3. **Forward-only calculators:** `bjt_divider_bias` and `mosfet_losses` (every variable is an input, `dof` = 7, one solvable set). All others are solvable in several directions (see the table in each task).
4. **No new engine or UI features are used beyond the contract:** no `choices`, no `finder`, no `chart` (the integrator ramp is linear, a chart would add nothing), no new symbols. Units: `units` whitelists keep dropdowns sensible (`degC`/`degF`/K for temperatures and temperature differences, `°C/W` for thermal resistance, `%` for duty, efficiency and the Schmitt fraction, no `min`/`h` on rise times, no `%` on the signed gain).
5. **Drawings are at most 32 grid units wide** (Part U's measured limit for the default window: at 33 the field chips fall back to a list under the drawing). The output stage of the instrumentation amplifier is drawn as the generic `ic` box "diff. amp ×1" (inputs `+` and `−`, output `out`), because the full four-resistor op-amp stage does not fit next to the field chips within 32 units; the two input op-amps, the three resistors of the input stage and R_G are drawn in full, and the doc text names the three-op-amp topology. Variables that cannot sit on a drawing (`t` of the integrator) are listed below it by the page.
6. **Sources** are named by standard, datasheet or textbook only: Horowitz & Hill, The Art of Electronics, 3rd ed., with a chapter number only where it is certain (ch. 2 Bipolar Transistors for the transistor switch and the BJT bias, ch. 4 Operational Amplifiers for the op-amp stages) and the topic named otherwise (LED/diode circuits, Zener regulators, heat and power design, instrumentation amplifiers); Sedra & Smith, Microelectronic Circuits; Erickson & Maksimović, Fundamentals of Power Electronics; Mohan, Undeland & Robbins, Power Electronics; the gain equations `G = 1 + 50 kΩ / R_G` (INA128, Texas Instruments) and `G = 1 + 49.4 kΩ / R_G` (AD620, Analog Devices). No page, URL, table or application-note number is cited. Rule-of-thumb limits in warnings (0.25 W resistor, 0.5 W Zener, 150 °C junction, saturation below 0.2 V V_CE, 15 V output of an integrator, soft divider when R_TH exceeds a tenth of (β + 1) × R_E) are stated as such in the warning text and are not claimed as standards.
7. **Hand-check method.** Expected values come from exact arithmetic or definitions (decimals and fractions written out in each `ref`); where a logarithm or a long division is needed, the `ref` says "hand (independent script)" and the value was computed with an exact-fraction script that does not read the YAML and never calls the solver. For `bjt_divider_bias` the `ref` shows the rounded intermediate values while the JSON carries the exact numbers.

### Task C3.1: Semiconductors (6 calculators)

**Files:**

No existing function, type or schema is touched (new content files and one wrapper file only), so there is no GitNexus impact analysis to record for this task.

Six semiconductor calculators. `bjt_divider_bias` uses the Thevenin form of the divider with the base current included (`I_B = (V_TH - V_BE) / (R_TH + (β + 1) × R_E)`); `bjt_divider_bias` and `mosfet_losses` are forward-only (every variable is an input, only derived quantities are results, `dof` equals the number of variables and there is exactly one solvable set). The heatsink keeps temperatures as `temperature` (kelvin internally, °C on display, `25 °C` parses) and the stage drops as `tempdiff`.

| id | variables | dof | solvable sets | default example (the default inputs are one of the solvable sets) | vectors (sets / solve) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `led_resistor` | V_S, V_F, n (LEDs per string), m (strings), I_F, R | 5 | 5 | 12 V, 2 V, 3, 2, 20 mA gives R = 300 Ω, I_tot = 40 mA, P_tot = 0.48 W, 50 % of it in the LEDs | 4 / 14 |
| `zener_regulator` | V_in, V_Z, I_L, I_Zmin, R | 4 | 5 | 12 V, 5.1 V, 20 mA, 5 mA gives R = 276 Ω, P_Z = 127.5 mW | 4 / 14 |
| `transistor_switch` | V_in, V_BE, I_C, h_FE, overdrive k, R_B | 5 | 6 | 5 V, 0.7 V, 100 mA, 100, 5 gives R_B = 860 Ω, I_B = 5 mA | 4 / 15 |
| `bjt_divider_bias` | V_CC, R_1, R_2, R_E, R_C, V_BE, β (all inputs, forward-only) | 7 | 1 | 12 V, 47k, 10k, 1k, 4k7, 0.7 V, 100 gives I_C = 1.286 mA, V_CE = 4.655 V | 3 / 5 |
| `mosfet_losses` | I_D, R_DS(on), D, V_DS, t_r, t_f, f_sw (all inputs, forward-only) | 7 | 1 | 10 A, 10 mΩ, 50 %, 12 V, 20 ns, 20 ns, 200 kHz gives 0.5 W + 0.48 W = 0.98 W | 4 / 5 |
| `heatsink` | T_A, P, R_thJC, R_thCS, R_thSA, T_J | 5 | 6 | 25 °C, 10 W, 1.5, 0.5, 3 °C/W gives T_J = 75 °C | 3 / 14 |

- [ ] **Step 2: Run the vector test and watch it fail**

`TestCalculatorVectors` iterates the calculators of the catalog, so before the YAML exists it never reads these vector files. The red signal is therefore the number of passing subtests of the new calculators:

```bash
go test ./internal/ecalc -run 'TestCalculatorVectors/(led_resistor|zener_regulator|transistor_switch|bjt_divider_bias|mosfet_losses|heatsink)$' -count=1 -v 2>&1 | grep -c -- '--- PASS: TestCalculatorVectors/'
```
